issues.author: hammer
issues.body:
🤖 *Drafted with agent assistance on behalf of @hammer.*

## Request

Integrate **[OpenReward](https://openreward.ai)** (the Open Reward Standard / ORS environment ecosystem, ~500 environments from the Papers with Code team) as a first-class environment source in `marin.rl` — by reviving and landing the existing first-pass integration in **#4661**, which has been open since April and predates several relevant refactors.

## Where the codebase is today

The `MarinEnv` adapter layer (`lib/marin/src/marin/rl/environments/`) is now a settled pattern with three vendor/format adapters on main — `prime_intellect_env.py` (Environments Hub via the verifiers protocol), `tinker_environments/`, and the native `math_env.py`/`mock_env.py` — all driving typed `Rollout`/`RolloutGroup` outputs through `inference_ctx` (the token-native data plane from #6186/#6231), configured via `EnvConfig` (which the curriculum system in `marin/rl/curriculum.py` also consumes). Adding a vendor is now approximately one adapter file.

**#4661 already built most of what's needed**: deterministic task-manifest snapshotting (reproducible task sets outside training), typed Qwen/vLLM tool-calling primitives, a single-turn text-only `OpenRewardEnv`, a smoke launcher + docs, and the right credential pattern (`OPENREWARD_API_KEY` resolved from env-var names at runtime, never serialized — `EnvConfig` stores names only). It had 63 focused tests passing at submission. It has drifted for ~3 months and needs a **rebase onto the current `MarinEnv`/`BaseInferenceContext` interface** (with `prime_intellect_env.py` as the reference), not a rewrite.

## Proposed scope

1. **Rebase & land #4661** — single-turn `OpenRewardEnv` + manifest prep + smoke test against the on-cluster vLLM serving path. (Days.)
2. **Multi-turn/tool extension** — most of the ORS catalog (agentic, games, tool-use) is multi-turn; the tool-calling primitives are already in the branch. (~1 week.)
3. **Hosted-vs-local decision** — ORS environments "run anywhere": for RL the env sits inside the rollout loop, so managed hosting means a network round-trip per turn per rollout. Proposal: use the managed platform for browsing/selection, self-host chosen envs alongside the generators for training. Worth a short doc note in the adapter.
4. **Pick 2–3 pilot environments** and wire one into an `EnvConfig` curriculum as the acceptance test.

## Adjacent

- SkyRL upstream is reportedly an early adopter of new RL environment APIs — if that includes ORS, MarinSkyRL would gain a second path cheaply; worth confirming before duplicating effort on the agentic side.
- With verifiers/Prime Intellect, Tinker, Harbor/Daytona, and (pending) OpenReward, we now span four env ecosystems across two RL tracks — at some point a short "which environments for hero post-training" consolidation (in the spirit of #6162 for frameworks) may be warranted; out of scope here.

@taivu1998 — you built #4661; does a rebase seem right to you, or did the design change enough that you'd approach it differently now? Happy to help with the pilot-env selection and smoke testing.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue + confirm scope
- [x] Assess current `MarinEnv`/`inference_ctx` interface vs #4661
- [x] Post Research + proposed approach

This is a multi-week, multi-module feature (revive #4661: ~2,500 LOC across 32 files, 63 tests). Per the agent policy for large work, no PR — analysis below for a human to review before implementation.

# Research

The `MarinEnv` adapter layer has settled since #4661 opened (2026-04-12): each vendor is one adapter file in `rl/environments/` implementing `MarinEnv.sample(inference_ctx, ...) -> (list[RolloutGroup], metrics)`, configured by `EnvConfig(env_class, env_args)`. `prime_intellect_env.py` is the reference. #4661 is textually `MERGEABLE`, but that only means no line conflicts — it was written against the *old* interface and does not match today's contract in three concrete places:

1. **Location.** #4661 lives under `rl/integrations/openreward/` (`env.py` 320L, `manifest.py`, `models.py`, `client.py`, `cli.py`). The settled pattern is an adapter in `rl/environments/`. Its test registers `env_class="marin.rl.integrations.openreward.env.OpenRewardEnv"`, so the path is baked into the config surface.
2. **inference_ctx API drift (main rebase risk).** #4661 imports `ToolSpec` from `inference_ctx` and calls `inference_ctx.assistant_turn_from_choice(...)` — **neither exists** on the current `BaseInferenceContext`. Those are multi-turn/tool primitives #4661 tried to add via its own edits to `inference_ctx/render.py` (+170/−40) and `vllm.py`. Meanwhile the current context *already* provides `batch_completions`, `create_rollout_from_choice`, `response_tokens_from_choice`, `logprobs_from_choice` — so the single-turn path maps cleanly, but the tool path must be reconciled against today's `inference_ctx`, not re-applied wholesale.
3. **Adjacent edits to re-verify** against current signatures: `orchestration.py`, `job_config.py`, `rl_experiment_utils.py`, `run_environment.py`.

The credential pattern (`OPENREWARD_API_KEY` stored as a name in `EnvConfig`, resolved at runtime) is still compatible — keep it.

**Relevant code**
- [`environments/base.py#L15-L47`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/environments/base.py#L15-L47) — current `MarinEnv.sample` contract + `EnvConfig`
- [`environments/prime_intellect_env.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/environments/prime_intellect_env.py) — the reference vendor adapter to mirror
- [`inference_ctx/base.py#L58-L112`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/environments/inference_ctx/base.py#L58-L112) — has `batch_completions`/`create_rollout_from_choice`; **no** `assistant_turn_from_choice`/`ToolSpec`
- [#4661 changed files](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/4661/files) — `openreward/env.py` uses the missing `ToolSpec`/`assistant_turn_from_choice`

# Proposed approach

Split #4661 into two PRs instead of one big rebase, so the low-risk part lands first:

**PR 1 — single-turn `OpenRewardEnv` (the fast win).**
- Move `env.py` → `rl/environments/openreward_env.py`; colocate `manifest.py`/`models.py`/`client.py` as a small `environments/openreward/` submodule. Update `env_class` in configs/tests to the new path.
- Strip the multi-turn/tool code path from `env.py`. Drive generation through the existing `inference_ctx.batch_completions` + `create_rollout_from_choice`, exactly like `prime_intellect_env.py` — this drops the dependency on `ToolSpec`/`assistant_turn_from_choice` and the `render.py`/`vllm.py` edits entirely.
- Keep the manifest snapshotting + `OPENREWARD_API_KEY`-by-name pattern and the `prepare_..._task_manifest.py` script.
- Tests: keep `test_openreward_task_manifest.py` (deterministic, no network) and the single-turn slice of `test_openreward_env.py`; drop the tool-path tests. Re-verify the `orchestration.py`/`job_config.py`/`run_environment.py` edits still apply.
- Acceptance: wire one pilot env into an `EnvConfig` curriculum smoke.

**PR 2 — multi-turn/tool extension.** Design the tool primitives *against today's `inference_ctx`* (does the ORS agentic path need a first-class `ToolSpec` + an `assistant_turn_from_choice`-style helper, or can it compose from existing methods?). This is where #4661's `render.py`/`vllm.py` changes belong, but they need a fresh design review, not a replay.

Open questions for @taivu1998 / RL owners before implementation:
- OK to relocate `integrations/openreward/` → `environments/openreward/` and accept the `env_class` path change?
- For the tool path: extend `BaseInferenceContext` with tool primitives, or keep tools inside the adapter?
- Which 2–3 pilot ORS envs are the acceptance target, and should the pilot be single-turn (unblocks PR 1) or agentic (needs PR 2)?

<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This issue scales the best one-phase OLMix KL settings found in the 3e18 sweep. The sweep showed that the original scaled `KL=0.05` anchor was not best for either target: `KL=0.1` gave the best uncheatable BPB, while `KL=0.005` gave the best OLMoBaseEval Table-9 macro BPB. The follow-up ladder launches those two target-specific winners at `2e19`, `3e20`, and `1e21` with native Table-9 eval enabled. The current conclusion is still pending scaling results; the only settled decision is to scale the two KL winners rather than rerun the full grid or relaunch completed 3e18 points.

### Helpful links
- Completed sweep parent: `/calvinxu/iris-run-launch_delphi_uncheatable_optimized_mixtures-20260706-001339`.
- Scaling parent: `/calvinxu/iris-run-launch_delphi_uncheatable_optimized_mixtures-20260706-052124`.
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

This tracks a follow-up to the one-phase OLMix baseline. We originally scaled the paper-style one-phase OLMix settings with `delta=0.01`, `KL=0.05`, and cap 4. A direct 3e18 KL sweep showed that the best OLMix KL depends on the target:

* Uncheatable target: best observed `eval/uncheatable_eval/bpb` was `KL=0.1` at `1.002202`, improving over the scaled `KL=0.05` anchor at `1.003851`.
* Table-9 target: best observed Table-9 macro BPB was `KL=0.005` at `1.076865`, improving over the scaled `KL=0.05` anchor at `1.081359`.

The Table-9-tuned OLMix point improves OLMix but still does not beat the current one-phase DSP Table-9 point at 3e18 (`1.070728`). The scaling ladder is still useful to establish whether the better OLMix KL setting transfers across scale.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Determine whether tuning the OLMix KL regularization at 3e18 improves the one-phase OLMix scaling curves for uncheatable BPB and Table-9 macro BPB relative to the already scaled `KL=0.05` baselines.

## Status

* 3e18 KL sweep completed for both targets.
* Selected winners: uncheatable `KL=0.1`; Table-9 `KL=0.005`.
* Scaling parent submitted for `2e19`, `3e20`, and `1e21` for both selected mixtures.
* Native OLMoBaseEval Table-9 eval is enabled for the scaling jobs.
* Initial launch health: parent running, six child training jobs created, pending on east5 TPU scheduling/coscheduling capacity with no code failures observed.

## Links

* Logbook: Fieldbook `exp_01kwtbdknwahvedc24g2trhht4`
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:
  * Scaling parent: `/calvinxu/iris-run-launch_delphi_uncheatable_optimized_mixtures-20260706-052124`
  * Completed sweep parent: `/calvinxu/iris-run-launch_delphi_uncheatable_optimized_mixtures-20260706-001339`

## Decision Log

* Do not relaunch the 3e18 points; they already completed in the sweep.
* Scale only the target-specific OLMix winners, not the full KL grid.
* Keep native Table-9 eval enabled on all launched scaling checkpoints.

## Conclusion

Pending scaling results.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment investigated a Blackwell MoE source-push path for the target shape `T/rank=65536`, `D=3072`, `I=3072`, total experts `256`, topk `4`. The intended true fused Warpgroup peer-reference design was ruled out because the tested JAX/Mosaic stack cannot lower peer-id GMEM refs, so the practical path became staged source-push transport plus local Blackwell compute. Transport tuning reached `1596.34` useful W13-equivalent TFLOP/s/rank on B300 with zero drops, clearing the corrected topk-expanded 60% gates. The public `moe_mlp` path now has a reusable preplanned boundary that cuts target forward steady-state from about `39.965 s` direct to `0.093318 s`, while package-private prepared runs remain faster. Backward initially OOMed at target D/I due to per-route row materialization, but regrouping by destination-local expert with a 512-row tile unblocked the full target fwd+bwd run at `1.90717 s` steady-state with zero dropped routes. The remaining recommendation is to treat staged Blackwell as the viable path and reserve further work for production API boundary decisions and a tuned Pallas backward.

### Helpful links
- Peer-ref lowering gate: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6933#issuecomment-4881270376
- Public preplanned target timing: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6933#issuecomment-4883691661
- Full target fwd+bwd unblocked: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6933#issuecomment-4884581545
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Investigate a Blackwell implementation of the source-push fused all2all(lhs) + W13/GMM path for MoE. The first decision point was whether remote peer GMEM references can be used under Pallas GPU Warpgroup lowering on Blackwell. That path is unsupported on the tested JAX stack, so the active implementation direction is staged: source-push copy/pack followed by local Blackwell ragged/GMM W13 or materialized W13/SwiGLU.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Reach at least 60% of the best measured local Blackwell W13/SwiGLU throughput for the inbox-send source-push path on the target MoE shape: roughly 65K tokens, hidden_dim=3072, intermediate_dim=3072, total experts=256, topk=4. Because topk=4 expands W13 work, the apples-to-apples local compute baseline uses `M=262144` useful W13 rows per rank.

## TL;DR

The practical Blackwell path is staged, not true fused Warpgroup peer-ref. The peer-ref probe failed with `GMEM refs with peer ids are not supported in warpgroup lowering`. Corrected topk-expanded B300 local baselines are `1824.22` useful TFLOP/s/rank for W13-only and `1534.20` useful W13 TFLOP/s/rank for materialized W13/SwiGLU at `M=262144`. After copy tuning, B300 EP=8 staged transport repeat medians reached `1596.34` useful W13-equivalent TFLOP/s/rank and `267.73 GB/s/rank` with zero drops. That clears 60% of both corrected baselines: W13-only target `1094.53`, materialized W13/SwiGLU target `920.52`. A direct hand-adapted fused W13/SwiGLU epilogue remains blocked by a Mosaic `copy_gmem_to_smem` swizzle assertion even on tiny non-collective smokes.

## Results

- Peer-ref Warpgroup probe: failed at the intended decision gate with peer-id GMEM refs unsupported in Warpgroup lowering.
- Local Blackwell W13/GMM at `M=65536`: best `1.565 ms`, `1580.53` useful TFLOP/s/rank.
- Local materialized W13/SwiGLU at `M=65536`: best `1.746 ms`, `1416.95` useful W13 TFLOP/s/rank.
- Corrected topk-expanded local W13/GMM at `M=262144`: `5.425 ms`, `1824.22` useful TFLOP/s/rank.
- Corrected topk-expanded local materialized W13/SwiGLU at `M=262144`: `6.450 ms`, `1534.20` useful W13 TFLOP/s/rank.
- Initial B300 EP=8 target source-push transport repeat medians: `copy_release_only` median `10.284 ms`, `161.39 GB/s/rank`, `962.26` useful W13-equivalent TFLOP/s/rank, zero route/row/entry drops.
- Tuned B300 EP=8 target source-push transport repeat medians with `inbox_slots=24`, `send_worker_programs_per_peer=4`: `6.199 ms`, `267.73 GB/s/rank`, `1596.34` useful W13-equivalent TFLOP/s/rank, zero route/row/entry drops.
- Fused W13/SwiGLU prototype: not lowering. Reducing pipeline depth avoids one shared-memory limit, but the prototype still hits `assert copy_params.get("swizzle") is None` in Mosaic copy lowering.

## Scope

- Add a Blackwell-only implementation path without rewriting the existing Hopper source-push kernel.
- Keep Hopper and Blackwell benchmark rows separate in JSONL artifacts.
- Compare local Blackwell GMM/W13, W13/SwiGLU, copy-only, and inbox-send staged/fused variants.
- Prefer the staged Blackwell path until Warpgroup peer refs or the fused epilogue lowering issue changes upstream.

## Decision log

- 2026-07-04: Start with peer-ref capability probe before tuning fused source-push W13.
- 2026-07-04: Peer-id GMEM refs are unsupported in Warpgroup lowering on the tested stack; switch to staged copy/pack plus local Blackwell compute.
- 2026-07-04: Use tuned local W13 config `128x128x64`, `max_concurrent_steps=6`, `collective=True`, `grid_minor_dim=M`, `epilogue_tile_n=64`.
- 2026-07-04: Corrected B300 topk-expanded local baselines use `M=262144`.
- 2026-07-04: B300 staged transport with `inbox_slots=24`, `send_worker_programs_per_peer=4` clears 60% of both corrected W13-only and materialized W13/SwiGLU baselines.
- 2026-07-04: Direct hand-adapted fused W13/SwiGLU remains a lowering follow-up, not the current practical path.

## Negative results index

- Warpgroup peer-id GMEM refs: unsupported in lowering on the tested stack.
- Upstream local W13 sweep: most `collective=False` rows failed from an unbound cluster-axis path; larger memory/layout configs failed from shared-memory or layout constraints.
- Direct fused W13/SwiGLU epilogue: still blocked by Mosaic copy lowering assertion after small-shape, non-collective, lower-pipeline-depth, and single-contiguous-W13-SMEM isolation attempts.
- Earlier `M=65536` local baseline comparison was not apples-to-apples with the EP=8 `topk=4` source-push transport row; corrected local compute baselines use `M=262144`.

## Current baseline

- Existing Hopper source-plan W13 context from `.agents/logbooks/6597-moe-mgpu-forward.md`: `8.441 ms`, `215.94` rounded TFLOP/s/rank, `203.54` useful TFLOP/s/rank on that Hopper target shape.
- Blackwell local W13 baseline at `M=262144`: `1824.22` useful TFLOP/s/rank.
- Blackwell materialized W13/SwiGLU baseline at `M=262144`: `1534.20` useful W13 TFLOP/s/rank.
- 60% targets: `1094.53` useful TFLOP/s/rank against W13-only; `920.52` against materialized W13/SwiGLU.
- Tuned B300 staged transport repeat median: `1596.34` useful W13-equivalent TFLOP/s/rank.

## Links

- Research logbook: `.agents/logbooks/blackwell-source-push-inbox.md`
- Related Hopper/source-push context: `.agents/logbooks/6597-moe-mgpu-forward.md`
- JAX reference kernel: https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/blob/main/jax/experimental/pallas/ops/gpu/blackwell_ragged_dot_mgpu.py

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Assessment: research/experiment kickoff — no PR.**

This is a Blackwell port of the Hopper source-push inbox MGPU MoE `permute_up`/W13 path, gated on a Pallas Warpgroup peer-GMEM-ref capability probe. It requires Blackwell GPU hardware, a lowering probe, and kernel benchmarking — design + experiment work, not a self-contained bug fix. Per the fix-issue workflow I'm posting analysis for a human rather than opening a PR.

# Research

Neither the Hopper source-push kernel (`source_push_inbox`) nor the referenced logbooks are in `main` yet. The proven Hopper prototype lives only in open PRs #6840 / #6841, and the logbooks (`.agents/logbooks/6597-*`, `blackwell-source-push-inbox.md`) are on research branches. So the Blackwell work has **no in-tree base to build on** until that lands. The nearest in-tree EP dispatch code is the ragged-all2all path.

**Relevant code / links**
- #6597 — Hopper parent (fused dispatch + W13/SiLU)
- #6848 — source-push inbox research tracker; stable Hopper baseline `8.353ms`, `218.19 TFLOP/s/rank`, decomposition `send_only=5.593ms / store_zero=5.650ms / full_wgmma=8.313ms`
- #6840 / #6841 — package-private `source_push_inbox.py` prototype (open, **not merged**)
- [`ep_ragged_all_to_all.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py) — nearest in-tree EP all2all dispatch
- [JAX `blackwell_ragged_dot_mgpu.py`](https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/blob/main/jax/experimental/pallas/ops/gpu/blackwell_ragged_dot_mgpu.py) — reference local Blackwell GMM

# Proposed approach

Target shape: ~65K tokens, hidden=3072, intermediate=3072, EP=256, topk=4. Goal: ≥60% of best local Blackwell GMM/W13 throughput for the inbox-send source-push path.

1. **Gate first — peer-ref probe.** Minimal Pallas GPU Warpgroup kernel that reads/writes a *remote* peer GMEM ref under Blackwell lowering. This is a compile/lowering capability check, not a perf run — it determines the whole design and should be its own tiny artifact. Record pass/fail + the lowering error verbatim in the logbook before any tuning.
2. **Branch on the gate:**
   - **Probe passes** → fused single-kernel source-push: peer-GMEM inbox send overlapped with local Blackwell ragged/GMM W13 (mirror the Hopper inbox layout from #6840).
   - **Probe fails** → staged fallback: source-push copy/pack into a local inbox, then a separate local Blackwell ragged/GMM kernel (JAX reference above as the GMM baseline).
3. **Baselines to measure separately, Blackwell rows kept apart from Hopper in the JSONL:** local Blackwell GMM/W13, W13+SwiGLU, copy-only, and inbox-send fused vs staged. Use the Hopper decomposition style (`send_only` / `store_zero` / `full_wgmma`) so the send/slot floor vs WGMMA-scheduling tax is attributable.

**Dependency / sequencing:** land or branch off #6840/#6841 first so the Blackwell path can reuse `PushInboxConfig` / inbox layout instead of forking from `scripts/bench`. Add the Blackwell path as a separate module (Warpgroup lowering differs enough that a shared kernel factory would be premature).

**Blocking questions for a human before implementation:**
- Which Blackwell target + Iris cluster/reservation should the probe and benchmarks run on?
- Should this build directly on the #6840/#6841 branches, or wait for merge to `main`?
- Is there a known-good JAX/Mosaic version pin where Warpgroup peer-GMEM refs are expected to lower on Blackwell, or is that itself the open question?

I can scaffold the probe kernel + logbook once the base branch and target hardware are confirmed.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
## Description

Track the work to make the issue #6044 d=2560 May Recipe Grug MoE shape fast on CoreWeave H100s. The target is a repeatable profile-bearing short run at >=20% training MFU, followed by profile-evidence optimization of MoE, attention, FSDP/sharding, cross entropy, data/host overhead, and optimizer/update overhead.

## Hypothesis or Goal

The current Grug MoE path can reach >=20% MFU for the d=2560, 26-layer, 256-expert, top-k 4 shape if the H100 topology is kept to a viable expert-parallel layout and the remaining hot paths are optimized from measured profiles rather than guessed.

### Links

* Source recipe: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6044#issuecomment-4607416665
* Research logbook: `.agents/logbooks/grug-moe-d2560-mfu.md`
* Branch logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/codex/research-grug-moe-d2560-mfu/.agents/logbooks/grug-moe-d2560-mfu.md
* Latest checkpoint: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/55847db99
* Latest run: `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260615-065544` (`GM2560-MAY-036B64-N8-FASTPROFILE-cw-20260615-0655`)
* Latest W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/GM2560-MAY-036B64-N8-FASTPROFILE-cw-20260615-0655

<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## TL;DR

No >=20 MFU claim yet. The current live run is `GM2560-MAY-036B64-N8-FASTPROFILE-cw-20260615-0655`, parent `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260615-065544`, on `cw-us-east-02a`. It follows the updated direction to reduce batch size rather than add train-time microbatching: full d2560/L26, seq_len 4096, batch 64, N8/EP8/model1, ring MoE, FA4/CuTe attention, XLA CE, replicated embeddings, `compute_with_master`, `save_moe`, W&B tracker, and the earliest callback-eligible profiler window (`profiler_start=3`, `profiler_steps=1`, HLO proto enabled). MAY-034 hit a pre-step 128-device clique stall; MAY-035 B128/N8 stayed pre-first-step without metrics in a short window, so MAY-036 reduces global batch to 64 while keeping the 64-GPU launch size.

The memory evidence localizes the original B256 blocker to full-depth, sequence/batch-scaled activation or workspace pressure. Full-depth B256 failed before the first step across fp32 live params, bf16 live params with fp32 master, Pallas CE, and `recompute_all`; full-depth B128 succeeded; one-layer B256 succeeded; full-depth B256 at seq2048 succeeded. MAY-032 at seq3072 was killed before first-step evidence, so it is not evidence for or against that memory bracket.
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Scope

Baseline shape from #6044: d=2560, 26 layers, 20 Q heads, 5 KV heads, head_dim 128, 256 experts, top-k 4, seq_len 4096, half-RoPE, PKO on every 4th plus last layer, routing renorm sum 2.5, router z-loss 0, ring MoE, MuonH, mixed precision `params=float32,compute=bfloat16,output=bfloat16`.

## Current Baseline

Current executable profile target: 8 H100 nodes, `MAY_EXPERT_AXIS=8`, `MAY_MODEL_AXIS=1`, `MAY_REPLICA_AXIS=1`, `MAY_BATCH=64`, `MAY_SEQ_LEN=4096`, `MAY_STEPS=4`, `MAY_DATA=synthetic`, `MAY_TRACKER=wandb`, `MAY_CHECKPOINTS=none`, `MAY_PROFILER_START=3`, `MAY_PROFILER_STEPS=1`, `MAY_PROFILER_ENABLE_HLO_PROTO=true`, `MAY_WATCH_INTERVAL=0`, `MAY_ATTENTION_IMPLEMENTATION=gpu_fa4_cute`, `MAY_CE_IMPLEMENTATION=xla`, `MAY_LIVE_PARAM_MODE=compute_with_master`, `MAY_INPUT_EMBED_SHARDING=replicated`, `MAY_OUTPUT_PROJ_SHARDING=replicated`, and `MAY_REMAT=save_moe`.

Original full-B256 target gate remains memory-negative at seq4096. Latest successful B256 diagnostic: same as the target gate except `MAY_SEQ_LEN=2048` in `GM2560-MAY-031S2048-B256-N16-cw-20260615-0520`.

## Results

No >=20 MFU claim yet. Search space reduced so far:

* Replicating input/output embeddings removed the old `%fake_parameter.2 = bf16[1,4096,2560]` full-rematerialization warning on the one-layer layout probe.
* FA4/CuTe backward now compiles with the CUTLASS atomic wrapper.
* Full-depth B256 on N16/EP8/model1 still OOMed before the first step at ~74 GiB under three one-axis variants: fp32 live params, bf16 live params with fp32 master, and Pallas CE.
* Full-depth B128 fits, and one-layer B256 fits. This localizes the current B256 blocker to full-depth activation/remat liveness rather than static optimizer/parameter storage or the loss/output local-token workspace alone.
* Full-depth B256 with `recompute_all` still OOMs before the first step, but the request drops to 72.03 GiB. That makes sequence/token scaling the next diagnostic axis rather than another param/optimizer-state probe.
* Full-depth B256 with `seq_len=2048` and `recompute_all` succeeds on N16/EP8/model1. The run produced no usable MFU row, but it proves the remaining memory blocker is sequence/token-scaled.
* MAY-032 (`seq_len=3072`, B256) was killed before a first-step metric or allocator result, so it is not memory evidence.
* MAY-033 was healthy but intentionally stopped before first metrics/profile because `profiler_start=6` would delay evidence on the slow B128 path.
* MAY-034 hit a pre-step `Initialize clique: devices=128` rendezvous stall with zero W&B history/profile and was intentionally stopped.
* MAY-035 B128/N8 was intentionally stopped pre-first-step after a short no-progress window with zero W&B scalar history.
* MAY-036 is live as the reduced-batch B64 N8 fast-profile/MFU run, with W&B and the earliest callback-eligible profiler window enabled.

## Decision Log

* 2026-06-13: Use fp32 sharded params plus bf16 compute for the baseline. `params=bfloat16` remains a diagnostic knob, not the requested fp32-master mode.
* 2026-06-14: Force XLA cross entropy after Pallas CE caused autotune noise and a full-logits-shaped startup allocation.
* 2026-06-14: Treat mixed default ring EP plus `model_axis>1` as invalid for now after repeated local `kCollectivePermute`/rendezvous failures.
* 2026-06-14: Keep production MoE topology at `expert_axis=8`, `model_axis=1`, `moe_implementation=ring` until a non-ring backend proves otherwise.
* 2026-06-14: Disable checkpoints, profiler, watch stats, and W&B for executable-gate runs; only relaunch with profiler once the shape can step.
* 2026-06-15: Use replicated input/output embeddings for the full May gates because the one-layer layout probe removed the old SPMD full-remat warning.
* 2026-06-15: Treat full-depth B256 memory as activation/remat-liveness dominated after B128 full-depth and one-layer B256 both fit.
* 2026-06-15: Use sequence length as the next one-axis diagnostic after `recompute_all` only reduced the B256 full-depth request to 72.03 GiB.
* 2026-06-15: Since full-depth B256 `seq_len=2048` fits, recover full sequence length by attacking token/activation pressure before launching the profile-bearing full-shape run.
* 2026-06-15: Per updated direction, reduce global batch to B128 instead of adding train-time microbatch accumulation, and use the fitting full-sequence shape for the first profile-bearing MFU run.
* 2026-06-15: Replace MAY-033 with MAY-034 using `profiler_start=3`, `profiler_steps=1`, and HLO proto enabled so the first profile artifact arrives as soon as callback gating permits.
* 2026-06-15: Stop MAY-034 after persistent pre-step 128-device clique rendezvous warnings; relaunch as MAY-035 on 8 nodes / 64 H100s to get profile evidence while isolating N16 launch stability.
* 2026-06-15: Stop MAY-035 after it stayed pre-first-step with no W&B rows in a short evidence window; relaunch as MAY-036 with global batch 64 rather than adding microbatching.

## Negative Results Index

* GM2560-MFU-004/005: failed before step 0 with allocator requests around 60 GiB; no W&B history or profile artifact.
* GM2560-MFU-006: moved past the old allocator signal with 0.95 XLA memory fraction, then wedged pre-metrics in XLA collective/clique startup; no W&B scalar history or profile artifact.
* GM2560-MFU-007 and GM2560-MAY-020: reproduced the 256-device clique/JAX coordination fatal path around the old `%fake_parameter.2` activation-layout warning.
* GM2560-MIN-009/011/012: mixed ring EP plus model-axis sharding failed before metrics with collective/rendezvous symptoms. This is a topology/backend negative result, not evidence against EP8/model1.
* GM2560-MAY-025: full-depth B256 with fp32 live params failed before step 0 with `74.75GiB` allocation request.
* GM2560-MAY-026: same shape with bf16 live params plus fp32 master failed before step 0 with `74.42GiB` allocation request.
* GM2560-MAY-027: same shape with Pallas CE failed before step 0 with `74.41GiB` allocation request.
* GM2560-MAY-030: same full-depth B256 shape with `recompute_all` failed before step 0 with `72.03GiB` allocation request.

## Conclusion

Open. The original full d2560 B256 shape remains memory-negative at seq4096; the current path is to finish the profile-bearing B64 full-sequence run, then use the profile to decide whether attention, MoE EP communication, FSDP/update, or optimizer work is the next bottleneck.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Grug MoE d2560 MFU status update as of 2026-06-15

Pushed branch: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/codex/research-grug-moe-d2560-mfu
Latest commit: `c8ae03af2` (`[grug] Avoid AdamH hyperball materialization`)

Current headline: attention/MoE throughput work has a viable baseline, but the immediate blocker is still a first-step memory allocation around the loss/output/vocab or SPMD liveness path. The optimizer-hyperball materialization hypothesis is now weak after MAY-059 reproduced the same allocation with patched AdamH.

Status by area:

- Attention: FA4/CuTe is the real path. The usable MAY-042 profile shows attention backward as the top compute op, so attention still matters for throughput. It is not currently the strongest explanation for the short-seq first-step OOM.
- MoE: EP8 ring/ragged all-to-all gave the best usable profile path so far. Other MoE routes remain more fragile or memory-sensitive. DeepEP only has a small smoke result, not enough to make it the d2560 default.
- Optimizer/sharding: opt-state sharding and `compute_with_master` are in place. `expert_3d_optimizer=adamh` routes the routed expert 3D weights away from MuonH. MuonH and AdamH hyperball updates now both have algebraic, norm-preserving helpers that avoid building the intermediate `new_p` tensor.
- Parameters: the short-seq diagnostic confirms `parameter_count=67078882816` and mesh `{'replica_dcn': 1, 'data': 16, 'expert': 1, 'model': 4}; batch_shards=16` on H100 80GB.

Run chronology:

- MAY-042: B128/seq4096 EP8 ring profile completed enough to inspect. Profile artifact: `marin-community/marin_moe/jax-profile-step-3-4:v0`. Profile read was roughly 65.65% compute, 33.68% comm, 0.68% stall; top op was FA4/CuTe segmented attention backward, with NCCL all-gather prominent.
- MAY-055: B8/N4 M4/E1 full seq4096, algebraic MuonH, true global batch reduction. OOMed on first loss materialization with `132.44GiB`, showing that reducing true batch from B16 to B8 did not remove the large allocation at full sequence length.
- MAY-056/MAY-057: B16/N8 M4/E1 full seq4096 with `expert_3d_optimizer=adamh`. MAY-056 failed in FA4/CuTe Cutlass compile before giving an optimizer-memory signal. MAY-057 sat for hours after mesh/train-loop setup with no scalar rows, so it was stopped.
- MAY-058: B16/N8 M4/E1, `seq_len=1024`, synthetic, XLA CE, `output_proj_sharding=lm_head`, `live_param_mode=compute_with_master`, `remat=recompute_all`, `expert_3d_optimizer=adamh`. It OOMed at `jax.block_until_ready(metrics["train/loss"])` with `63.80GiB` (`68504603904` bytes). This ruled out routed-expert MuonH as the sole cause, but later inspection found AdamH still had its own materialized hyperball path.
- MAY-059: same short-seq shape after patching AdamH hyperball algebraically. It again reached the train loop but produced no scalar rows or profile artifact, then OOMed at first-step loss materialization with `63.69GiB` (`68388945152` rounded bytes). Parent `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260615-165139`; child `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260615-165139/grug-train-GM2560-MAY-059S1024-B16-N8-M4E1-ADAMH-HYPALG-cw-20260615-0930`. Iris retried once (`failure_count=1`, `preemption_count=0`), then we stopped the parent and child intentionally to avoid a deterministic retry loop.

Loss/vocab investigation:

Rawls traced the training loss path to `compute_params.next_token_loss` inside `jax.value_and_grad`, then to `fused_linear_softmax_cross_entropy_loss`; the train path does not call `Transformer.logits`. For MAY-058/MAY-059, the intended XLA CE local shape should be roughly `x=(1024, 2560)` and `w=(2560, 32064)`, with streaming vocab tiles on the order of tens of MiB. A plain local logits tensor is only about 0.122 GiB fp32, not 63 GiB.

The suspicious scale is instead global-ish: `B16 * S1024 * V128256 * fp32` is 7.83 GiB, and 8x that is 62.6 GiB, close to the observed 63.7-63.8 GiB. That points toward a global logits-like/loss-output buffer being replicated or kept live through SPMD/lowering, or a layout/gradient round trip around output projection and fused CE.

What the new branch changes:

- Adds an algebraic AdamH hyperball helper in `experiments/grug/moe/adamh.py` to avoid materializing `new_p`.
- Adds parity tests in `experiments/grug/moe/test_optimizer.py` for vector, matrix, and stacked cases.
- Records MAY-058 and MAY-059 in `.agents/logbooks/grug-moe-d2560-mfu.md`, including commands, job ids, final state, and interpretation.

Validation on the branch:

- `./infra/pre-commit.py --changed-files --fix` passed.
- `python -m py_compile experiments/grug/moe/adamh.py experiments/grug/moe/optimizer.py experiments/grug/moe/test_optimizer.py` passed before the final vector test addition; pytest also exercises import/compile after that edit.
- `uv run pytest experiments/grug/moe/test_optimizer.py -q` passed (`5 passed`).

Recommended next step:

Run the same short-seq diagnostic with `--output-proj-sharding replicated`. This removes the `lm_head -> CE-local -> lm_head` layout/gradient round trip. If the `63GiB` allocation changes or disappears, focus on output-projection/loss gradient sharding. If it does not, capture XLA buffer assignment for the MAY-058/MAY-059 shape and identify the exact owner of the giant buffer before further tuning.

comments.body:
🤖 FA4/CuTe Hopper attention update

Pushed research branch: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/codex/add-hopper-cutlass-path
Checkpoint commit: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/63232bbba890991e949278f554ffac1485fac4de
Logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/add-hopper-cutlass-path/.agents/logbooks/grug-fa4-cute-hopper.md

Summary:

- The original May208 profile was not just a naming/dispatch artifact. The old correct compatibility path was slow for the May208 per-device FA4 shape: about `1.10 ms` backward, `14.8% SoL`.
- A native SM90 backward route is now correct for the relevant D128 GQA case. It uses upstream SM90 backward mainloop, arch-90 postprocess with gmem-backed accumulators, and Grug lower-bound/full-block sparse metadata.
- Production routing is intentionally narrow: H100/SM90 native path only for GQA with `head_dim=128`; MHA and other head dims stay on the compatibility fallback.
- Correctness against the available upstream-local FA4/CuTe path is within `0.01` max abs. May208 D128 direct Grug-mask vs built-in-local native backward had max abs `dq=0.000488`, `dk=0.000061`, `dv=0.000977`.
- Strict max-abs `0.01` against materialized JAX float32 is not met for standard-normal BF16 inputs, but the miss is shared with upstream FA4 numerics rather than introduced by the Grug wrapper. Relative norms were about `0.3-0.5%`.
- Performance now tracks the upstream-local SM90 path closely:
  - B=1 May208 shard: production backward `0.5229 ms`, `31.15% SoL`; built-in-local direct backward `0.5040 ms`, `32.31% SoL`; production is `96.4%` of upstream-local.
  - B=8 probe: production backward `3.142 ms`, `41.47% SoL`; built-in-local direct backward `3.015 ms`, `43.22% SoL`; production is `95.95%` of upstream-local.
- The remaining gap to published FA3/FA4 headline utilization is not obviously a Grug mask/wrapper bug. It looks like shape/integration limits: GQA ratio 4, local window/block sparse scheduling, split preprocess/main/postprocess, and JAX/CuTe call boundaries. We should not try to out-schedule FA4 at the WGMMA/TMA level without a more specific structural advantage.

Next action: extract a smaller production PR from this research branch with only the routed SM90 D128 GQA path and CPU-safe tests, excluding the logbook and benchmark-only harness changes.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Full thread summary for the Grug d2560 May H100 profiling/recovery push.

## TL;DR

The only 8-node no-TP shape that got clean training steps in this thread was E8M1/B128 with `recompute_all` and `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_enable_nccl_comm_splitting=false`; the 5-step smoke finished at about 67.4k tokens/s and 7.78s/step, with loss around 11.419 and internal analytic MFU around 1.82. That is functionally useful but far too slow. Attempts to recover the larger profiled May shapes with `save_moe` repeatedly ran into first-step memory pressure. The strongest infrastructure finding is that XLA NCCL communicator splitting causes the ring path to fail with `ncclCommSplit`/peer-disconnect behavior on the 8-node run, and disabling it fixes the smoke. The strongest model/profile finding is that the remaining bottlenecks are not just CE or FA4; remat boundaries, routed MoE transpose/collective behavior, and non-expert parameter/optimizer sharding dominate the next debugging steps.

## Scope

This thread started from marin-community/marin#6395, merged in `main`, switched optimizer focus from MuonH to AdamH, and targeted 8-node CoreWeave H100 Grug d2560 runs. It explicitly tracked the CE-path question in #6695 and the FA4/SM90 question in #6696. Tokenization was allowed to fall back to synthetic data if it blocked progress; it did, so most useful results below are synthetic.

## What changed while debugging

* Adopted the one-task-per-GPU/NVSHMEM bootstrap model from marin-community/marin#6776: fork one child process per GPU before JAX starts and set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICE` per child.
* Added/fixed launch wrapper plumbing for `--processes-per-task 8`, `XLA_FLAGS`, `--optimizer sgd` / `MAY_OPTIMIZER=sgd`, compile diagnostics, profiler stop barrier timeout, and profiler mirroring to `<ctx.output_path>/profiler`.
* Added/corrected Grug MoE trainer validation mesh behavior so batch validation excludes tensor-parallel `model` and, for expert-hidden/non-expert expert sharding, uses data batch axes instead of treating `expert` as a data-loader batch axis.
* Added a d2560 remat control path and switched the profile default from `save_moe` to `recompute_all` while isolating memory pressure.
* Patched AdamH/master-param update sharding experiments so gradients are matched to master-param sharding before moment updates; local eval-shape checks showed live attention projection params replicated while master params and AdamH moments could remain batch-sharded.
* Patched FA4 CuTe metadata handling so `lower_bounds`/`valid` are explicitly resharded before `shard_map`; this became PR #6910. The 2-node B16 compile validated that the earlier FA4 metadata local/global shape mismatch was gone.
* Patched routed-token unflattening for expert-hidden modes so flat routed outputs are resharded before reshaping back to activation layout.
* Explored ring-combine variants to remove rematerialized all-gathers: saving gather payloads, `psum + slice`, and `ppermute` combine. Local JAXPRs showed `psum_scatter` transpose was responsible for a remaining remat all-gather, but remote variants either OOMed or still needed profile validation.

## Run chronology and results

* Slimg Pajama/tokenizer run `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260701-182817` stalled at tokenization: 8/48 complete, 40 in-flight, 0.0/s. It was stopped and the work moved to synthetic data.
* First synthetic submissions exposed integration bugs before training: missing FA4 frontend `valid` argument, then CUTLASS forward expecting 5 specs but seeing 4 tensors. Fixes were committed through `1862761f7`.
* 8-node synthetic E8M1/B64-ish early runs with `save_moe` failed before step 1 with NCCL `ncclCommSplit` plus CUDA OOM symptoms. Switching d2560 to `recompute_all` in `e9433bc85` did not clear the first-step OOM at that shape.
* Lower-batch/model-axis diagnostics used `--expert-axis 4 --model-axis 2 --batch 32`. They found trainer validation bugs: first Levanter treated all 64 devices as batch-parallel and hit `ZeroDivisionError`; then `replica_dcn=1` was invalid on CoreWeave because `num_slices=8`. Fixes in `bb1c9ced7` and `2c1bf452f` corrected validation, but this path was stopped because tensor parallelism was explicitly not desired.
* No-TP May-shape recovery used E8M1 with B512/B8 per GPU. With `save_moe`, `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260701-225808` failed before step 1 allocating 181.32GiB in `jit_train_step`. With `recompute_all`, `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260701-231442` still failed before step 1 allocating 171.89GiB. This pointed to large routed MoE forward state, especially `grug_moe_expert_hidden`, not just optimizer state.
* B256/B4 per GPU was attempted next. One run died due coscheduled sibling rescheduling fallout; a resubmit reached CE selection but failed before a step with rank exits/GRPC disconnect and no clear allocator traceback in available logs.
* B128/B2 per GPU with ring reached child GPU startup and selected `batched_xla` CE, then failed before step 1 with NCCL `ncclCommSplit` peer-disconnect/SIGABRT.
* B128/B2 per GPU with `ragged_all_to_all` avoided the immediate ring split failure but was compile-pathological: it stayed in host/XLA compile work for more than an hour with no first step, so it was stopped as a diagnostic dead end. Another ragged attempt was lost to coscheduled sibling bounce.
* B128/B2 per GPU with ring and `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_enable_nccl_comm_splitting=false` succeeded 5/5 on `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260702-032031`: about 67.4k tokens/s, 7.78s/step, loss 11.419, internal analytic MFU about 1.82. This was the first clean 8-node no-TP training result.
* The first profiled B128 run with the same XLA flag reached step 20 but failed during profiler teardown: `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` at `levanter_barrier_sync_2`, with 31/64 tasks reaching the barrier under the default 200s timeout. The branch then added `MAY_PROFILER_STOP_BARRIER_TIMEOUT=1800` and wrapper plumbing.
* A follow-up profiled B128 run was stopped after appearing quiet pre-step with GPUs allocated but idle. The lesson from the user was that this compile can be very slow; future babysitting should not stop a run solely because pre-step compile is quiet, high-memory, or low-GPU-utilization.
* The B64 `save_moe` profile run from `codex/grug-profile-output-path`, `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260702-194512`, was meant to verify the new `<ctx.output_path>/profiler` mirror. It ultimately failed and produced no profile.
* SGD/optimizer-state diagnostics were dispatched to test whether dropping AdamH moments buys batch size for `save_moe`. The intended sequence was B256 first, then B512 if B256 stepped, with `--optimizer sgd`, `--non-expert-param-sharding batch`, and compile diagnostics. No final positive SGD result was captured in this parent thread summary.
* 2-node B16 `compute_with_master` / AdamH-sharding validation first failed during `jit_train_step` compile allocating 26.74GiB. After AdamH update-sharding fixes, local eval-shape evidence showed live Q projection replicated and master/mu/nu sharded as intended, but remote validation remained memory-sensitive.
* 2-node B16 profile runs then focused on FA4 metadata and QKV/non-expert sharding. The main-style FA4 shard map initially failed because `lower_bounds` was global while local Q was sharded; PR #6910 fixed that by resharding metadata. The corrected B16 run compiled, proving that fix, then OOMed on first train step allocating 39.94GiB.
* B8 expert-hidden/QKV runs from `/Users/dlwh/.codex/worktrees/grug-6377-qkv-profile` found and fixed more shape/layout bugs: launcher validation included `expert` in batch shards, train/eval loaders treated `expert` as a data batch axis, and `routed_flat` reshape failed because `bfloat16[32768@(replica_dcn,data,expert),2560]` could not reshape to `(8,4096,2560)` without explicit output sharding.
* After those fixes, `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260703-164824` lowered and compiled successfully but failed first train step with NCCL `ncclAlltoAll` reporting CUDA OOM. This was treated as OOM, not communicator-splitting evidence, so no 1-process-per-node fallback was launched from that result.
* `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260703-170751` succeeded with replicated QKV params and produced a usable profile. It removed the exact `qkv_projection` 49ms all-gather but left an attention-adjacent all-gather around 66ms under `CausalSelfAttention/bsd,dn->bsn`, pointing at output projection or broader non-expert sharding rather than QKV alone.
* `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260703-172851` then tested non-expert hidden-over-expert sharding with `--non-expert-param-sharding expert --attention-qkv-sharding hidden_model --moe-expert-param-sharding data_model` at the same 2-node B16 save_moe/O1 profile shape. It lowered and compiled successfully, then failed first train step with deterministic BFC allocator OOM trying to allocate about 39.95GiB in `jit_train_step`. W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/cw-may-d2560-profile-nonexpert-expert-6377-N2-b16-p8-o1-20260703-172848. No profile or throughput came out of this run.

## Current evidence for #6695 and #6696

For #6695, the runs repeatedly selected `batched_xla` CE, and CE was not the first-order blocker for the 8-node recovery. A clean readable profile is still needed to quantify CE share, but the dominant failures in this thread were memory/collective/remat/sharding issues before CE became the main optimization lever.

For #6696, FA4 was active enough to expose real FA4/CuTe frontend and metadata-sharding issues. The `valid` argument and metadata local/global mismatch were fixed, and PR #6910 specifically guards the metadata sharding failure. FA4 is not currently the only suspected throughput limiter; attention-adjacent all-gathers remained even after replicated QKV removed the original qkv projection gather.

## Current conclusions

* Keep no tensor parallelism for this line of investigation unless there is a new explicit reason to reintroduce it. The model-axis diagnostic was useful for validation bugs but not the desired long-term shape.
* Keep `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_enable_nccl_comm_splitting=false` for the ring path on multi-node H100 until there is a better XLA/NCCL fix. It converted the B128 no-TP ring run from `ncclCommSplit` failure to a successful smoke.
* `save_moe` at May-like batch sizes is still memory-prohibitive. Even B16 on 2 nodes hit about 39.95GiB first-step allocations for some sharding variants, and B512/B8 per GPU hit 181GiB-class allocations.
* `recompute_all` buys enough memory for B128/B2 per GPU on 8 nodes but the observed throughput is poor. It is a viability baseline, not a satisfying profile shape.
* `ragged_all_to_all` was not a practical immediate fallback at the full shape because compile behavior was pathological.
* Non-expert param/optimizer state sharding matters. AdamH moments and master params need to stay aggressively sharded, but sharding live params can reintroduce attention all-gathers. `compute_with_master` remains promising but memory-sensitive.
* The remaining profile bottleneck after replicated QKV appears attention-output/non-expert related, not the original qkv projection gather.
* Profiler durability should now be treated as `<ctx.output_path>/profiler`, with W&B `jax_profile` as helpful but not the only source. The B64 run intended to validate this failed before producing a profile.

## Open next steps

* Get one stable, readable profile for a shape that actually steps, likely starting from the successful 2-node replicated-QKV profile and the 8-node B128 recompute_all smoke shape.
* Attribute the remaining `CausalSelfAttention/bsd,dn->bsn` all-gather to output projection versus broader non-expert sharding with HLO/profile evidence.
* Continue `compute_with_master` or equivalent live/master sharding work so live compute avoids all-gathers while master params and AdamH opt state stay aggressively sharded.
* Re-test `save_moe` only after memory reductions are concrete; otherwise it keeps failing before useful profile data.
* Keep PR #6910 moving; it fixes a real FA4 metadata sharding bug and had green CI plus no blocking review feedback at last check.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This open experiment/design issue is part of the perplexity-gap surrogate work and asks for factuality and abstention validation slices that avoid benchmark contamination. The proposed direction is to build known-answer and known-unknown target-likelihood probes from held-out Wikipedia/Wikidata-style sources, label them explicitly as surface/likelihood probes rather than calibrated hallucination evals, and wire them into the existing perplexity-gap bundle registry. A design comment mapped the request onto existing Marin PPL infrastructure and left implementation waiting on human decisions about source snapshots, abstention phrases, multilingual scope, and contamination corpus access.

### Helpful links
- Parent issue: #5819
- Design comment: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5826#issuecomment-4482323566
- Registry hook discussed in design: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/perplexity_gap_registry.py#L72-L110
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Part of #5819. Add factuality and abstention-surface validation coverage without using AA-Omniscience questions or near-duplicates.

PPL is an indirect proxy for factuality and weak for abstention, but known-answer and known-unknown target likelihood can still catch broad data/knowledge regressions during training.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Build non-benchmark validation slices from held-out Wikipedia/Wikidata snapshots, public knowledge bases, and generated entity-attribute cloze/QA. Include separate known-answer targets and unknown/insufficient-information targets, clearly labeled as surface/likelihood probes rather than calibrated hallucination evals.

If raw PPL is too weak, use supervised target-only scoring over answer strings or abstention phrases. The metric should be smooth enough to show movement before e19/e20 flops and should not become a hidden benchmark test set.

### Links

* Parent: #5819

## Results

Open. Define allowed sources, entity/attribute sampling, known vs unknown construction, and contamination checks.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue + parent #5819
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no overlapping PR/issue found beyond parent)
- [x] Map issue requirements onto existing PPL registry infrastructure
- [x] Post research + proposed design (this comment — analysis only, no PR)
- [ ] Awaiting human direction before any implementation (research scope, >100 lines)

# Research

The request is to extend the perplexity-gap surrogate suite (#5819 / #5005) with non-benchmark factuality and abstention slices: known-answer entity/attribute cloze plus known-unknown / insufficient-information probes, scored by raw PPL or target-only likelihood, contamination-clean against AA-Omniscience, GPQA, HLE, AIME, MATH, MMLU-Pro, IFBench, LiveCodeBench, SciCode. Existing infra already supports both raw-text and target-only scoring and a pluggable bundle registry, so this is a content/methodology design problem, not a framework gap. Treating the surface explicitly as a "surface/likelihood probe" (per issue) means a `factuality_abstention` bundle parallel to `bio_chem` and `runnable_long_tail`, not a new code path.

**Relevant code**
- [`perplexity_gap_registry.py#L72-L110`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/perplexity_gap_registry.py#L72-L110) — bundle registry; `factuality_abstention_bundle()` slots in here
- [`long_tail_ppl.py#L29-L65`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/long_tail_ppl.py#L29-L65) — metadata-first slice pattern to copy (`StrEnum` family + `*PplSlice` dataclass)
- [`long_tail_ppl_runnable.py#L45-L98`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/long_tail_ppl_runnable.py#L45-L98) — HF-backed runnable bundle template
- [`perplexity_gap.py#L93-L138`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/perplexity_gap.py#L93-L138) — `raw_text_dataset` vs `supervised_text_dataset` (target-only loss already supported via `input_key`/`target_key`)
- [`paloma.py#L26-L43`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/paloma.py#L26-L43) — versioned HF snapshot pattern for held-out Wikipedia surfaces

# Proposed Design

Scope this issue as a design + small scaffolding ticket. Implementation should be split into child issues once the design is approved.

Allowed sources (held-out, public, dated snapshots only):
- Wikipedia: HF `wikimedia/wikipedia` pinned to a snapshot strictly newer than what training mixes already saw; per-article hash exclusion against Paloma `wikitext_103` and Uncheatable `wikipedia_english` to avoid double-counting tracking signal.
- Wikidata: HF `wikimedia/wikidata` snapshot or `Wikidata5M` for entity-attribute templates; tuples filtered to attribute predicates with high coverage (`P19 birthplace`, `P569 birthdate`, `P50 author`, `P361 part-of`, `P36 capital`, etc.).
- Public knowledge bases for cross-source corroboration: DBpedia abstracts, OpenAlex (paper→authors/venue), MusicBrainz (artist→releases) — each used only to confirm a Wikidata triple, not as a primary surface.

Construction (two slice families, both surface probes, both clearly tagged):
- `factuality_known_cloze`: take Wikidata triples `(subject, predicate, object)` whose object is corroborated in ≥2 sources and whose subject's English Wikipedia article exists in the held-out snapshot. Template into natural-language cloze of the form `"<context sentence about subject>. The <attribute> of <subject> is ____"`, with the gold object as `target`. Score with target-only loss via `supervised_text_dataset`. Stratify by predicate and by subject-popularity bucket (Wikidata sitelink count quartile).
- `factuality_unknown_target`: same template but with `target` set to a canonical insufficient-information phrase set (`"unknown"`, `"insufficient information"`, `"not specified"`, `"the article does not say"`). Negative items drawn two ways: (a) attributes the article demonstrably lacks (`P*` missing from the Wikidata entity and absent from the Wikipedia article body via string match), (b) plausible-but-false subjects fabricated by predicate-swapping. Score target-only likelihood of the abstention phrases. Track separately as `unknown_abstention_*` — explicitly a surface/likelihood probe, not a calibrated hallucination metric.

Contamination filter (mandatory before mirroring anything):
1. Normalize (lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace) and SHA-256 each candidate (`prompt + " " + target`).
2. Build hash sets and 5-gram MinHash signatures for AA-Omniscience public sample, GPQA, HLE, AIME 2024–2025, MATH test, MMLU/MMLU-Pro, IFBench, LiveCodeBench, SciCode, and Marin's `lm_eval_bridge` task list. Drop any candidate with an exact match or MinHash Jaccard ≥0.7 against any benchmark item.
3. Drop subjects whose Wikipedia article body appears verbatim in any Paloma slice (string hash) or Uncheatable mirror — these would re-leak training data into the probe.
4. Cap to ~2k items per slice and pin them as versioned outputs; the cap keeps eval cost low and discourages this becoming a hidden benchmark.

Sampling controls: stratify by predicate, popularity quartile, and language (English-only first pass); cap items per (predicate, quartile) bucket so a few high-coverage predicates don't dominate. Persist the exact `(subject_qid, predicate)` tuples used so the slice is reproducible from the pinned snapshot.

Scoring: use `supervised_text_dataset(target_key="target")` — target-only loss is already in `perplexity_gap.py` and is smoother than raw PPL on cloze tails. Raw PPL on the templated string can be exposed as a secondary metric for the known-answer slice only; do not expose raw PPL for the unknown slice (the loss is on a fixed phrase set and dominated by phrase prior).

Registry wiring: add `factuality_abstention_bundle()` to `perplexity_gap_registry.py`, register two slices (known, unknown), and add the bundle to `registered_perplexity_gap_bundles()`. Reuse `PerplexityGapBundle` exactly — no new abstraction. Tag every score with `surface_probe=factuality_abstention` so dashboards can keep it visually separate from calibrated evals.

Definition of done (proposed, for human confirmation):
1. Sources, predicates, popularity strata, abstention phrase set, contamination thresholds, and per-bucket cap chosen and recorded in a short doc under `docs/design/`.
2. `experiments/evals/factuality_abstention_ppl.py` mirrors the `long_tail_ppl_runnable.py` shape: dataclass + `StrEnum` family + slice list + `factuality_abstention_raw_validation_sets()` factory.
3. `perplexity_gap_registry.py` exposes `factuality_abstention_bundle()` and includes it in `registered_perplexity_gap_bundles()`.
4. A unit test under `tests/evals/` asserts the bundle materializes and that contamination-filter output sizes are non-zero and stable across re-runs of a fixed seed.
5. Dataset generation job is reproducible from pinned `wikimedia/wikipedia` + Wikidata snapshot revisions (versioned in the `ExecutorStep`).

Open questions for the issue owner before implementation begins:
- Which exact Wikipedia/Wikidata snapshot revisions should be pinned, and is there an existing held-out snapshot we already trust as out-of-training?
- Is the abstention phrase set fixed by team convention elsewhere in Marin (RL/SFT eval rubrics), or do we choose it here?
- Should multilingual variants ship in the first pass or be deferred to a follow-up issue per language?
- Is the AA-Omniscience contamination corpus available internally for hashing, or do we need to constrain to public benchmarks only?

This is design work + >100 LOC implementation across multiple files plus a new dataset generation pipeline, so per agent instructions I am not opening a PR. Awaiting human review of the design before scaffolding.

Config: d2048 / L24 / 64 experts top-4 (4:1 GQA) / shared expert = hidden_dim / sliding window 2048 (short layers) / MuonH heuristic LR / datakit mixture with **simulated epoching off** / seq 4096 / b512 / 500B tokens. Permanent checkpoint every 5k steps + 20-min rolling temp.

Caveat: the MFU number counts attention as full-quadratic over seq_len (the FLOP counter doesn't model the 2048 sliding window), so it's slightly optimistic on the attention term.

issues.body:
# Description 

This issue tracks tracks the initial exploration at integrating a vision encoder and projection with the Delphi language only base model that Marin has already trained with the goal of extending this to omnimodal capability.
We leverage the prior work done on baseline VLM training with Qwen3 1.7B and 4B language model backbones. 

# Results

# References

-  #2383
- [Qwen 3.8 Omni](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.25611)
- [SmolVLA](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.01844)

comments.author: bkolligs
comments.body:
# Evaluation strategy
The first thing to establish are some useful evals to measure the performance of the Marin based VLM. Previously in #2383 the following benchmarks were used and scores achieved. 


Benchmark | Score
-- | --
MMMU | 46.7
ChartQA | 75.6
MMStar | 58.1
OCRBench | 68.8
RealWorldQA | 70.6
SeedBench | 76.2
ScienceQA | 89.6


This result was obtained using a [three stage training approach](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2383#issuecomment-4130294651): 

| Stage | Goal | Data | What's Trained |
|-------|------|------|----------------|
| **Stage 1 — Language-Image Alignment** | Align vision encoder feature space with LLM embedding space | LLaVA-558K image-caption pairs | MLP projector only (vision encoder & LLM frozen) |
| **Stage 1.5 — High-Quality Knowledge Learning** | Inject broad visual knowledge before instruction tuning | LLaVA-OneVision-1.5-Mid-Training-85M (concept-balanced image-caption pairs from COYO-700M, Obelics, DataComp1B, LAION, ImageNet-21K, SAM-1B, etc.) | Full parameter training |
| **Stage 2 — Visual Instruction Tuning** | Teach the model to follow complex visual instructions across diverse multimodal tasks | LLaVA-OneVision-1.5-Instruct (~22M samples, 124 task types) + FineVision | Full parameter training |

comments.author: bkolligs
comments.body:
Our first experiments will test the architecture we plan to merge in the PR, which will aim to quantify some of the basic behavior/tensor flow before we move to the next step of type of scaling behavior in typical Marin fashion. 

There are some design questions we can investigate to deepen understanding: 

1. What's the best size of the projector? 
2. How to weight the tokens between language and visual? 
3. Delphi uses the Qwen tokenizer, do we need to adapt a new one to incorporate images? 
4. How does loss correlate to benchmark performance?

issues.author: ClassicLarry
issues.body:
This issue tracks iterative improvements to the Marin pretraining scaling ladder (`experiments/grug/fast_track`) using the **Marin Belay** process. It is a twist on autoresearch: an agent runs experiments in batches, and anyone can steer it with research directions. > **To suggest a research direction, comment on [Marin Belay Intake (#9514)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9514).** Suggestions a maintainer approves (👍 from a `marin-devs` member) are copied into this thread automatically, and the agent acts only on this thread. This thread holds the agent's batch reports and maintainer steering. ![fast_track MoE ladder: Marin 535B baseline, clean KMA and candidate 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/9697c11ef215ec0f9d536a1bceb0876f768fcf26/v1/ladder_scaling.png) The Marin 535B compute-optimal baseline follows `L(C) = 1.2 + 59.0·C^(−0.0843)` over four data-matched rungs. Clean KMA, the current baseline (★), is 0.022 lower at d512, 0.049 lower at d768, 0.040 lower at d1024 and 0.033 lower at d1280, which is about 1.14×, 1.43×, 1.40× and 1.35× the baseline's compute efficiency. Its dashed curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 64.8·C^(−0.0870)`. The **?** marks the open question this issue is chasing: how much further down each point can go. The red diamonds are the current best recipe, candidate 9 (Status below): **2.977 / 2.725 / 2.515 / 2.397** at d512 / d768 / d1024 / d1280. d512 and d768 are seed means, and the bigram table follows rule A. d768–d1280 are data-matched; d512 sits at its fixed-time step count (2817 vs 2383 steps), so it's plotted slightly to the right. That is 0.157 / 0.098 / 0.078 / 0.074 below clean KMA. Its dash-dot curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 55.0·C^(−0.0847)`. Its slope is a little shallower than clean KMA's, so the gap narrows with compute: projected to **1e24 FLOPs, 1.710 vs clean KMA's 1.727, about 1.48× clean KMA's compute efficiency and 2.95× the 535B baseline's**. Because the fixed-time d512 point flattens the fitted slope, that projection is probably conservative. The right panel is clean KMA's training MFU at each rung on one 8×H100 node: 9.5% at d512 and d768, 12.2% at d1024, and 13.0% at d1280. FLOPs are counted from KMA's own layers (KDA, MLA + Inkling, AttnRes), as 3× forward with no recompute. The trainer's logged `throughput/mfu` uses the baseline architecture's FLOP formula, so it is slightly off for KMA. ## Objective **Minimize Paloma macro loss (`eval/paloma/macro_loss`, final step) at the d512 rung after a fixed 8 minutes of 8×H100 train-step time.** - **Fixed time, not fixed tokens.** Faster code trains on more tokens within the 8 minutes, so a pure speedup counts as a win. - The LR schedule depends on the step count, so fix steps before each run: `num_steps = round(480 s × ex/s ÷ batch)`. - Measure ex/s with a short `--no-eval` probe (~30 steps) on the same cluster, and use the steady-state throughput. - Compile, evals and startup are excluded from the 8 minutes. - **Numerics changes are allowed** (e.g. FP8, precision changes, approximate kernels). They count as ordinary wins; no parity check needed. - **Noise.** Differences under ~0.005 are noise. A win must beat the current best by more than 0.005. ### Gates (both relative to the current baseline, same fixed-time rule at each rung) - **Gate 1:** beat the baseline at d512 and d768. - **Gate 2:** also beat it at d1024 and d1280, **and** project to lower Paloma macro loss at 1e24 FLOPs. Fit a power law of final loss against training FLOPs across the four rungs, for both the baseline and the variant, fixing the asymptote to 1.2. ### Fixed - Training data, the 16k BPE tokenizer, and the eval sets. - Sequence length 4096. - One 8×H100 node per rung. - The FLOP accounting used for the gate-2 projection. ### Judgment calls - **Hero-scale speed is out of scope for v1, so use discretion.** - Robust target criteria would also check training speed and inference speed at hero scale. Marin Belay v1 skips those checks. - Judge whether a change's d512 gain would carry over to hero scale, and avoid changes whose gain comes from d512-only effects. Two examples: - Dropping MoE for dense would be a clear win at d512 because dense gets ~5× higher MFU there, but that MFU gain would not carry over at hero scale. - A much larger KV cache would also be a clear win at d512, but it would hurt long-context inference speed. - **Avoid magic numbers.** - Prefer changes with few new tuned constants. A tuned constant is justified when its gain is above the noise threshold and holds as a pattern across scales. For example, a 2× LR on one parameter group qualifies if it clears the noise threshold and the gain shows up consistently at larger rungs. - The higher a change's risk of curve fitting, the more scales it must be validated at before it counts as a win. - **Spend effort in proportion to an idea's likelihood of improvement.** - Promising ideas deserve several attempts. Long shots can be tried once and dropped. - A first run is not a verdict for a large change. If you try a new architecture or component, tune its optimizer assignment, LR, init and other key hyperparameters before concluding it doesn't work. The baseline's settings were tuned for the baseline, not for the new idea. ## Architecture (current best, d512) The diagrams below show **clean KMA**. The current best recipe adds the components listed under **Status → Current best recipe**: MLA key norm and key offset, a gated bigram-memory AttnRes source, ReLU² experts, and optimizer, schedule and logit changes. The diagrams show d512; the other rungs differ in the Shape table only. **1. Layer stack and Block Attention Residuals.** Every sublayer reads its input through its own AttnRes gate, a per-token softmax over the residual history. At d512 each layer closes an AttnRes block, so the history at layer *i* is the embedding plus one sum per earlier layer. [¹](#arch-note) ```mermaid flowchart TB tok["token ids
B × 4096, packed documents"] --> emb["token embedding
16384 × 512"] emb --> en["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] en --> S0(["source 0
embedding"]) S0 --> L0 subgraph STACK["6 layers: local KDA ×4, global MLA ×2 (every 4th + last)"] direction TB L0["layer 0 · KDA + MoE"] --> L1["layer 1 · KDA + MoE"] --> L2["layer 2 · KDA + MoE"] L2 --> L3["layer 3 · MLA + Inkling + MoE"] --> L4["layer 4 · KDA + MoE"] --> L5["layer 5 · MLA + Inkling + MoE"] end L0 -. "block sum b0" .-> H L1 -. "b1" .-> H L2 -. "b2" .-> H L3 -. "b3" .-> H L4 -. "b4" .-> H S0 -.-> H H[("AttnRes history, read by every gate

+ running partial")] L5 --> FG["final AttnRes gate
softmax over embedding, b0…b4, partial"] FG --> fn["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] fn --> head["lm_head (untied) 512 × 16384
fused CE, vocab tile 8192, z-loss 1e-4"] head --> loss(["next-token loss"]) ``` **2. One layer.** The two sublayers each have an AttnRes gate. The MoE gate also sees the attention output written just before it, as the running partial. ```mermaid flowchart TB Hin[("history
embedding + b0…b(i−1)")] --> GA subgraph GATE["AttnRes gate (one per sublayer, 13 at d512)"] direction TB GA["logit_n = q · rms_norm(source_n)
