KDA (local) or MLA + Inkling (global)"}} MIX --> SCA["ShortConv (MLA layers only)"] --> PA(["partial = attn out"]) PA --> GM["AttnRes gate
history + partial"] Hin --> GM GM --> M1["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] --> MOE{{"LatentMoE + 2 shared experts"}} MOE --> SCM["ShortConv"] --> PB(["block b_i = attn out + MoE out"]) PB --> Hout[("appended to history")] ``` **3a. Kimi Delta Attention, the local mixer (layers 0, 1, 2, 4 at d512; D = 512, 4 heads × 128).** ```mermaid flowchart TB kx["x"] --> kq["q = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_q))"] & kk["k = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_k))"] & kv["v = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_v))"] kx --> kg["decay g = −5 · σ(exp(A_log) · (x W_a↓ W_a↑ + dt_bias))
rank-128 gate, per channel; A_log per head"] kx --> kb["write strength β = σ(x W_β), per head"] kq & kk --> kn["L2-norm q, k; q × 1/√128"] kn & kv & kg & kb --> rec["delta rule, chunked Pallas kernels (chunk 16)
S_t = (I − β k kᵀ) Diag(e^g) S_{t−1} + β k vᵀ
o_t = S_tᵀ q_t · state resets at document starts"] rec --> kon["per-head RMSNorm (shared 128-wide scale)"] --> kog["× σ(x W_g), per channel"] --> ko["W_o → sublayer out
no RoPE, no window, no output ShortConv"] ``` **3b. MLA + Inkling, the global mixer (layers 3 and 5 at d512).** ```mermaid flowchart TB mx["x"] --> mq["q = x W_q (full rank, 4 × 128)"] mx --> ml["KV latent = RMSNorm(x W_dkv), 512 wide, learnable gain"] --> mk["k = latent W_uk"] & mv["v = latent W_uv"] mx --> rel["Inkling bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]
R = x W_r (16 per head) · P 16 × 1024, shared across heads"] mq & mk & mv & rel --> fa["FA4 causal attention (fwd + SM90 bwd)
logits × 1/√128 (qk_mult 1) · no RoPE · no QK-norm
Inkling bias added before softmax"] fa --> xsa["XSA: subtract each head's component along its own v"] --> mg["× 2σ(x W_gate), per head, zero-init"] --> mo["W_o → ShortConv → sublayer out"] ``` **3c. LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing (every layer).** ```mermaid flowchart TB ex["x (512)"] --> fused["one fused GEMM:
router · W_latent↓ · shared-expert gate/up"] fused --> rt["router logits (fp32)
top-(8+1) on logit − β_QB; 9th = threshold α"] rt --> qb["QB: β_e = global (1 − 8/384) quantile of logit − α
10k-bin histogram each step; router bias = −β, not trained"] rt --> cw["combine weights = σ(unbiased logits) of the top 8,
renormalized to sum to 2.5"] fused --> lat["latent = RMSNorm(x W_latent↓), 256 wide"] lat & cw --> ep["384 SwiGLU experts, hidden 256
pooled-wave EP all-to-all over 8 GPUs, capacity 1.15"] ep --> up["W_latent↑ 256 → 512"] fused --> sh["2 shared SwiGLU experts, 512 → 256 → 512
down projections fused into one GEMM"] up & sh --> sum["routed + shared → ShortConv → sublayer out"] ``` ¹ AttnRes rolls a new block at layer *i* while `i % max(1, L // 8) == 0` and fewer than 8 blocks exist. At d512 and d768 every layer closes a block. At d1024 (12 layers) and d1280 (14 layers) only layers 0–7 do, so layers 8 and up all accumulate into one running partial instead of their own blocks. **Optimizer routing:** - **MuonH:** every attention and MoE matrix, and every GatedNorm (KDA `W_β` at 2× the MuonH LR). - **AdamH:** lm_head. - **Adam:** embedding, router, attention output gate, norm gains, ShortConv kernels, KDA decay parameters, Inkling weights. - **Adam at 0.1× the Adam LR:** the AttnRes queries. ## Baseline: clean KMA Branch [`fasttrack-moe-kma`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/fasttrack-moe-kma) @ `4eba59cafa`. Build from this branch. The recipe below covers every model and optimizer component. Values are for d512 unless noted; the code is `experiments/grug/fast_track/{model,optimizer,heuristic,launch}.py`. **Shape** | Rung | Width D | Layers | Local (KDA) / global (MLA) layers | Heads × head dim | Batch | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | d512 | 512 | 6 | 4 / 2 | 4 × 128 | 128 | | d768 | 768 | 8 | 6 / 2 | 6 × 128 | 128 | | d1024 | 1024 | 12 | 9 / 3 | 8 × 128 | 256 | | d1280 | 1280 | 14 | 10 / 4 | 10 × 128 | 256 | - Every 4th layer and the last layer are global; all other layers are local. - The run uses a 16k vocab and sequence length 4096 with packed documents. Every ShortConv and the KDA state respect document boundaries (the KDA state resets at each document start). - Weights are initialized with std 0.5/√D. Compute is bf16. **Embedding and output** - Token embedding → RMSNorm → GatedNorm. The result is AttnRes source 0. - Output path: final AttnRes gate → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → untied lm_head (`output_proj`). - The fused lm_head + cross-entropy loop uses a vocab tile of 8192. - GatedNorm (every GatedNorm in the model) is `x · sigmoid(W_up · SiLU(W_down · x))`, with a rank-128 bottleneck. **Block (every layer)** - **Attention sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → mixer (KDA or MLA). - **MoE sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → MoE → ShortConv on the MoE output. - Each ShortConv is a 4-tap causal depthwise conv. **Local layers: Kimi Delta Attention** (Kimi K3's layer) - **Projections:** q/k/v are D → N·128 with full heads (no GQA). Each goes through a ShortConv followed by SiLU. q and k are L2-normalized, and q is scaled by 1/√128. - **Decay:** per-channel log-decay `g = −5·sigmoid(exp(A_log)·(x·W_a_down·W_a_up + dt_bias))`. - The gate projection has rank 128. - `A_log` is one value per head, initialized to 0. - `dt_bias` is one value per channel, initialized so the decay rate spans 0.02–0.5. - **Write strength:** `β = sigmoid(x·W_β)`, one value per head. - **Recurrence:** `S_t = (I − β·k·kᵀ)·Diag(exp(g))·S_{t−1} + β·k·vᵀ`, read out as `o_t = S_tᵀ·q_t`. - It runs as chunked Pallas kernels, with a stable block-doubling inverse inside each chunk. - **Output:** per-head RMSNorm with a learnable 128-wide scale shared across heads → full-rank per-channel gate `sigmoid(x·W_g)` → `W_o`. - No positional encoding, no window, no XSA, and no ShortConv on the branch output. **Global layers: MLA + Inkling relative position** - **q:** full-rank, D → N·128 (no Q latent). - **k and v:** k = `W_uk · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)` and v = `W_uv · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)`. - They share one 512-wide KV latent, with a learnable RMSNorm on the latent. - Heads are 128 wide with no RoPE part. - There's no ShortConv on K, so the up-projections can be absorbed at inference. - **Scaling:** no QK-norm; `qk_mult` = 1, i.e. standard 1/√128 logit scaling. - **Position — Inkling relative-position bias**, added to the pre-softmax logits in place of RoPE: - `bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]`, where `R = x·W_r` is 16 values per head. - `P` is a bank of shape [16 × 1024] shared across heads. The relative extent is 1024. - It runs inside the FA4 attention kernel (forward, backward, and the SM90 backward pass). - **XSA** (exclusive self-attention): subtract the component of each head's output that is parallel to its own value vector. - **Output gate:** per head, `2·sigmoid(x·W_gate)`. `W_gate` is zero-initialized, so the gate is 1 at init. - The branch output also gets a ShortConv. **MoE sublayer (LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing)** - **Experts:** 384 routed experts, top-8. Each is a SwiGLU with hidden size D/2. - **Latent space:** experts operate in a D/2-wide latent. The input goes through `W_latent_down` → RMSNorm, and the combined expert output goes back up through `W_latent_up`. - **Router:** reads the full-width token and computes logits in fp32. - Experts are selected by top-(8+1) on bias-adjusted logits, where the 9th logit is the threshold α. - Combine weights are the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, renormalized to sum to 2.5. - **Quantile balancing:** each step, each expert's threshold β is the global (1 − K/E) quantile of the logit margins (logit − α), read from a 10k-bin histogram. The router bias is set to −β. - The router bias is not trained by gradient. - **Capacity:** capacity factor 1.15, with pooled-wave expert-parallel dispatch. Receiver ranks are sort-based and the expand backward is gather-based. - **Shared experts:** 2 shared SwiGLU experts that bypass the latent: D → D/2 hidden → D. - **Fused projections:** - The router, latent-down, and both shared experts' gate/up projections run as one GEMM. - The shared experts' down-projections run as one GEMM. **Residual stream: Block Attention Residuals** - **Sources:** the embedding source, one running sum per completed block of sublayer outputs, and the running partial sum of the current block. - The model has 8 blocks. Block sums use the raw sublayer outputs. - **Gates:** every sublayer (attention and MoE) has its own gate, and there is one final gate before the output norm. Each gate has one learned pseudo-query `q ∈ ℝᴰ`, zero-initialized so every gate starts as a uniform average. - **Mixing:** per token, `logitᵢ = q · rms_norm(sourceᵢ)`, using a parameter-free (frozen) RMS key norm, then `softmax` over sources and a weighted sum of the raw sources. - **Implementation:** - Each completed block is scored once against every gate that reads it. - Backward: at d512 the layer's forward intermediates are saved. At d768–d1280 each layer is recomputed. At d1280 the attention branch is also rematerialized. - The model keeps one layer stack per mixer kind. **Optimizer** | Group | Update rule | LR | Parameters | |---|---|---|---| | `muonh` | MuonH | MuonH LR | all attention and MoE matrices: MLA `W_q`/`W_dkv`/`W_uk`/`W_uv`/`W_o`; KDA `W_q`/`W_k`/`W_v`/`W_o`/`W_g`; experts; shared experts; latent down/up. Also every GatedNorm `W_down`/`W_up`. | | `kda_beta` | MuonH | 2 × MuonH LR | KDA `W_β` | | `adamh` | AdamH | MuonH LR | lm_head (`output_proj`) | | `adam` | Adam | Adam LR | token embedding; router; attention output gate; router bias slot (overwritten by QB); all 1-D norm gains; ShortConv kernels; KDA `W_a_down`/`W_a_up`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`; Inkling `W_r` and `P` | | `attn_res_query` | Adam | 0.1 × Adam LR | the AttnRes pseudo-queries | - **MuonH:** Nesterov momentum 0.95 → Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (5 quintic steps, bucketed across same-shape matrices) → a step along that direction, then projection back onto the matrix's Frobenius sphere. Each matrix's norm stays fixed at its init value. - **AdamH:** the Adam direction with the same Frobenius-sphere (hyperball) projection. - **Adam:** β1 0.9. This means that if you tweak one knob and the loss goes off the rails, the experiment can still be considered a success! We better understand the system sensitivity! comments.body:
Some ideas to get started. Treat this as a general pool of ideas, that indicates the spirit of what can be tried.
1. https://blog.tilderesearch.com/blog/online-kl-shampoo. Consider interactions with hyperball and selectively replace matrices.
2. Add a second embedding table with its own random init. Attn residuals queries both embedding tables, treating them as unique inputs.
3. Lets add value embeddings. That is, a second embedding table that gets added to V on the MLA layers. So take KV latent-> project to num_heads of size 128. Then do values = lambda1*values + lambda2*value_embeds[layer_i]. lambda 1 init to 1, lambda2 init to 0. value_embeds has [vocab_size, num_heads*head_dim, num_mla_layers] dimension. Can also try gated value embeds, where instead of lambda2, its conditional on residual stream via sigmoid(linear(x)).
4. Add learnable scalars to each submodule output, that feeds into attention residuals. May be worth tracking and plotting these in wandb, to see if indicates any architecture changes will help.
5. Try different variations of linear attention to replace KDA.
6. It has been shown in many places that the final couple layers of attention dont prefer to attend to outputs from the final MLPs. See if there is any change to attention residuals to help make this more natural.
7. Adding an lm_head auxillary loss to the output of layer 1 for the first X (say 500) steps can help give the routed experts a cleaner role early. Unclear how this interacts with attention residuals.
8. Hash routing on first layer.
9. Instead of Adam/AdamH on embed and lm_head, look into other optimizers here that have shown promise in literature.
10. Do any weights benefit from extremely different beta1/beta2/momentum terms, or swapping their optimizer group.
11. Update the router behavior (sigmoid vs softmax), normalizing over picked experts vs not, sampling over experts instead of top k).
12. Null routing (enable tokens to select null experts which skips their computation, dynamic compute per token).
13. Multi-token-prediction.
14. Sparse attention.

If users give comments with singular specific ideas, give it priority over this laundry list.

🤖 **Batch 1: cheap architecture adds from the idea list, an LR check, and a noise and profile baseline** (d512, 2475 steps) — **done**

**Goal.** Test the lowest-cost ideas from @ClassicLarry's list: `#2` (second embedding table), `#3` (value embeddings, both forms), and `#4` (learnable sublayer output scalars, logged to W&B). Also check whether the `MoeHeuristic` LR, which was fit on the old baseline architecture, is still right for KMA (×1.5 and ×0.67 on both LRs). Add a seed-1 baseline to calibrate noise, and a 60-step profile to find speed levers. Speed counts as a win under the fixed-time objective.

**Assumption (I'll correct it next batch if it's wrong).** None of these changes adds meaningful compute, so all runs use the baseline's 2475 steps instead of a separate probe. After each run I check its steady-state ex/s. If it is more than about 1% below 660, I rerun at `round(480 × ex/s / 128)` steps. Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch01`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/eb26f3cbc9) @ `eb26f3cbc9`: every change is gated by a `--model-set` / `--opt-set` flag and defaults to off.

**Implementation details**
- **ve:** each MLA layer gets a [16384 × N·128] table, and `v = λ1·v + λ2·VE[token]` (λ1 = 1, λ2 = 0 at init). The tables, λ and the gate go to Adam at the Adam LR, like `token_embed`.
- **veg:** `v = λ1·v + sigmoid(x·W)·VE[token]`, with one gate per head. `W` is zero-initialized, so the gate starts at 0.5.
- **osc:** a scalar initialized to 1 on each attention and MoE sublayer output before it enters the AttnRes history (Adam). Logged as `train/attn_res/scale_{attn,mlp}_L*`.
- **emb2:** a second randomly initialized table → learnable RMSNorm, prepended as an extra AttnRes block that every gate can read.

**Takeaway.**
- **Noise is the story.** The identical-code seed-1 baseline landed at 3.1195, 0.0056 below seed 0. Against the two-seed baseline mean of 3.1223, none of the architecture changes clears noise: emb2 −0.005, veg −0.004, osc −0.002, ve −0.002. ve, veg and emb2 also ran 7–13% slower, so at a fair 8-minute step count they would lose part of that.
- **The LR heuristic holds for KMA.** Both ×1.5 and ×0.67 are clearly worse.
- **The learned scalars in osc point at the MoE output.** Its final values: MoE outputs grow to 1.2 / 1.4 / 1.5 / 2.1 / 1.7 / 1.9× by layer, the early KDA outputs shrink to 0.48×, and the MLA outputs stay near 1.0. The routed-expert output magnitude is capped by MuonH's sphere and the 2.5 combine renorm, and it wants to grow.
- **Profile (8×H100, d512, ~187 ms/step).** Compute is ~155 ms: elementwise fusions ~61, GEMMs ~43, sort/scatter/gather ~23, KDA ~14, FA4 ~7. Exposed EP all-to-all is ~18 ms, and the host gap between steps is ~6 ms.
  - **One kernel is a bug:** the token-embedding gradient takes **~11 ms/step**. Under the bf16 compute policy, the gather's transpose scatter-adds every token's cotangent directly into a **bf16** table. That means contended bf16 atomics, with frequent tokens' gradients rounded at every add. A single-GPU microbenchmark puts the fp32 scatter at 0.2 ms. The same scatter is why ve, veg and emb2 were slow: each extra table adds one.

- Probe throughput with the fix, then rerun ve, veg and emb2 on it at fair step counts, with replicate seeds.
- Test MoE output-magnitude variants: combine renorm sum 2.5 → 4, sigmoid without renorm, softmax combine, and K3's normalized LatentMoE.
- In response to the literature-scan comment: a background scan turned up these candidates for later batches: K3 normalized LatentMoE, per-head Muon, NorMuon-style row normalization, Engram n-gram memory, null experts, and FP8 lm_head.
**Next batch (tentative):** act on the profile. Validate any win above 0.005 at d768. Try combinations of the winners, MTP, and router variants (`#11`).

Gate 2 (d1024/d1280) will run once on the bundled winners, to save slots.

  - The early aux lm_head loss (`#7`): **+0.016**. A lighter retry is queued: weight 0.3 over 200 steps.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 5: @ClassicLarry's three requests: z-loss weight, projection biases, and freezing QB at 50%** (d512, 2817 steps; reference = batch-3 base mean **3.0990**)

**Addresses** the comment asking to vary the logit z-loss, add biases to some weight matrices, and freeze QB updates halfway through training. All runs build on the fp32-embedding base, branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch05`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02).
- **z-loss:** the current weight is 1e-4 (`--z-loss-weight`). One run turns it off, one raises it 10×.
- **Biases:** zero-initialized and trained with Adam, at three sites:
  - Qwen-style q/k/v: KDA q/k/v before their ShortConvs, and MLA q plus the KV latent before its RMSNorm.
  - The attention sublayer output.
  - The MoE sublayer output.

  If the combined run moves, I'll split the sites next batch.
- **QB freeze:** from step 1408 on, the router bias keeps its last quantile-balanced value (`qb_freeze_step`). Routing can then drift, and load balance is no longer enforced.

| change | branch@commit | W&B | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ vs 3.0990 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| z-loss weight 0 (vs 1e-4) | [`ea0592bd02`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02) | [lc1-b05-z0](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-z0) | 2817 | 751 | 3.3902 | 3.0966 | −0.0024 |
| z-loss weight 1e-3 | [`ea0592bd02`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02) | [lc1-b05-z1e3](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-z1e3) | 2817 | 749 | 3.4029 | 3.1046 | +0.0056 |
| biases: q/k/v + attention out + MoE out | [`ea0592bd02`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02) | [lc1-b05-bias](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-bias) | 2817 | 742 (−1%) | 3.3913 | 3.0993 | +0.0003 |
| freeze QB router biases at step 1408 (50%) | [`ea0592bd02`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02) | [lc1-b05-qbfrz](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-qbfrz) | 2817 | 751 | 3.3924 | 3.1059 | +0.0069 |
| **AttnRes logit bias** per (gate, source), zero-init, Adam at 0.1× (human, 2nd comment) | [`f1734ddcdf`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/f1734ddcdf) | [lc1-b05-arb](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-arb) | 2817 | 751 | 3.3954 | 3.1001 | +0.0011 |
| AttnRes logit bias + AttnRes z-loss 1e-3 | [`f1734ddcdf`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/f1734ddcdf) | [lc1-b05-arbz3](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-arbz3) | 2817 | 748 | 3.3996 | 3.1045 | +0.0055 |
| AttnRes logit bias + AttnRes z-loss 1e-1 | [`f1734ddcdf`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/f1734ddcdf) | [lc1-b05-arbz1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-arbz1) | 2817 | 746 | 3.4570 | 3.1475 | +0.0485 |

**AttnRes logit bias and z-loss** (added for the follow-up comment). Each of the 13 gates gets a zero-init bias per source it reads: one per completed block, plus one for the running partial. It is added to the logit before the softmax and trained with Adam at 0.1× the Adam LR, the same as the queries. The z-loss is the mean over tokens of logsumexp(gate logits)², averaged over gates, and added to the loss. Every run now logs the pseudo-query norms: `train/attn_res/query_norm_{mean,max,gNN}` plus the unweighted `train/attn_res/z`. One caveat: a z-loss can be satisfied by shifting a gate's biases down together, which leaves the mix unchanged. I'll compare the q norms across the three runs.

**Correction:** the AttnRes z-loss runs' eval losses also included the z-loss term (the same bug, found in batch 18). That inflated them by weight × z: about +0.0012 for 1e-3 and +0.001 for 1e-1. Their deltas are about +0.004 and +0.047 instead of +0.0055 and +0.0485, so both are still worse.

**Takeaway (all done).**
- **AttnRes logit bias is neutral (+0.0011).**
- **The AttnRes z-loss hurts:** +0.0055 at 1e-3 and +0.049 at 1e-1.
- **It raises the pseudo-query norms rather than lowering them.** Final values:

  | run | AttnRes z (unweighted) | query norm mean | query norm max |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | bias only | 6.31 | 0.227 | 0.377 |
  | bias + z 1e-3 | 1.23 | 0.286 | 0.583 |
  | bias + z 1e-1 | 0.01 | 0.332 | 0.565 |

  The z-loss is minimized by pushing every logit down. With keys that are RMS-normalized but not mean-centred, the query does this by growing along the direction opposite the common component of the sources, instead of shifting all biases together. That distorts the mix.
- The other results from this batch:
  - Freezing QB at 50%: +0.007.
  - lm_head z-loss 1e-3: +0.006.
  - lm_head z-loss 0: −0.002.
  - Projection biases: neutral.

comments.author: neel04
comments.body: Try a simple version of looped models (w/ and wo/ growing, a la https://github.com/qlabs-eng/slowrun/pull/92 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19107) with untying and see if that improves performance. Make sure to include the input injection as well!

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 9: looped models (@neel04's request): tied looping, with and without growth, with input injection** (d512, paired seed 0 vs qk_mult-2.5 base **3.0858**)

**Addresses** @neel04's comment. It follows [slowrun#92](https://github.com/qlabs-eng/slowrun/pull/92) (1× for 70% of training, then 2×) and [arXiv 2609.19107](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19107) (boundary operator `Norm(h) + α·e`, growth partway through training, backprop through all passes, and FLOPs of every pass counted). Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch09`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0).

**How it maps onto KMA** (`loop_passes`, `loop_grow_step`):
- **The looped core is the whole 6-layer stack**, weights tied. Each pass extends the Block AttnRes history. Pass 2's gates read the embedding, every pass-1 block, and the pass-2 blocks so far. Pass 2 has its own zero-initialized AttnRes pseudo-queries, so its gates start as uniform averages over that longer history.
- **Input injection.** At the start of each extra pass, the running partial is initialized to `α·e`, where e is the normalized embedding source and α is learned (init 1, Adam), and the pass's layers write onto it. The AttnRes gates already see e as source 0. This is the explicit re-injection from both references. The AttnRes softmax already normalizes what each sublayer reads, which plays the part of `Norm(h)`.
- **Growth** uses a step-gated `lax.cond`. Before the growth step only pass 1 executes, at full base speed. After it both passes run, with gradients through both. The router biases are shared per physical layer; their QB statistics are averaged over the passes.
- **Fixed-time steps.** Two passes run at 0.506× the base throughput (80-step probe: 381.8 vs 754.1 ex/s), so every run is given 8 minutes of train-step time:
  - loop2 throughout: 1426 steps.
  - Grow at 70%: N solves `0.7N/751 + 0.3N/380 = 480/128`, so N = 2179 and growth is at step 1525.
  - Grow at 50%: N = 1892, growth at step 946.
- **Not in this batch: untied growth**, where the core is copied at the growth step and the copies train separately. It changes the parameter tree and optimizer state mid-run, so it needs trainer work. It's next if tied growth looks promising.

| change | branch@commit | W&B | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ (paired) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| loop ×2 throughout (tied, injection) | [`c2803601b0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0) | [lc1-b09-loop2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-loop2) | 1426 | 381 | 3.5052 | 3.1766 | **+0.0908** |
| grow 1→2 passes at 70% of steps (step 1525) | [`c2803601b0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0) | [lc1-b09-grow70](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-grow70) | 2179 | | | OOM: 79.8 GiB (lax.cond kept both branches' buffers); fixed, rerun below | |
| grow 1→2 passes at 50% (step 946) | [`c2803601b0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0) | [lc1-b09-grow50](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-grow50) | 1892 | | | OOM: 79.8 GiB (lax.cond kept both branches' buffers); fixed, rerun below | |
| grow 1→2 at 70% (step 1525), static per-phase programs | [`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9) | [lc1-b09-grow70b](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-grow70b) | 2179 | 747 → 380 | 3.5435* | 3.1065 | +0.0207 |
| grow 1→2 at 50% (step 946), static per-phase programs | [`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9) | [lc1-b09-grow50b](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-grow50b) | 1892 | 747 → 380 | 3.5647* | 3.1195 | +0.0337 |

The mid-run eval always runs every pass, so for the growth runs the mid loss evaluates a model that has not trained its second pass yet. Only the final loss is comparable.

**Takeaway.**
- **Looping loses at d512 fixed time**, in every variant:

  | variant | Δ |
  |---|---|
  | 2× throughout | +0.091 |
  | grow 1→2 at 50% | +0.034 |
  | grow 1→2 at 70% | +0.021 |

  The less time spent in the 2× slower phase, the smaller the loss. The measured phase throughputs, 747 then 380 ex/s, match the budget, so all three got 8 minutes. \* marks mid losses from evals that ran both passes before the second pass had trained.
- **Why it loses.** The paper's gains are compute multipliers at ≥1e20 FLOPs with 7–8 tokens per parameter for its growth variants. Here the whole run is about 1e17 FLOPs and data-limited: in 8 minutes the model sees only about 1.1B tokens. An extra pass costs tokens, which are the scarce resource at this rung. Untied growth has the same FLOP cost after growth, so I'm not building it for d512. It is a better fit for a hero-scale study.

**Earlier notes.**
- **Fixed 2× looping throughout is much worse at fixed time: +0.091.** It gets only 1426 steps. At d512, one pass of the 6-layer stack is not the bottleneck; tokens seen are.
- **The growth runs first OOMed.** The step-gated `lax.cond` allocated 79.8 GiB, because XLA holds buffers for both branches. I replaced it with two statically compiled train steps, a one-pass program before the growth step and a two-pass one after, chosen per step in Python ([`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9)). Its CPU check matches the plain model exactly.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 10: slimming ablations (@ClassicLarry's request)** (d512, 2817 steps, paired seed 0 vs the qk_mult-2.5 base **3.0858**)

**Addresses** the comment asking to drop the GatedNorm on the embedding, drop the GatedNorm on the lm_head input, and make the KDA output gate per head instead of per channel. Each runs independently on top of qk_mult 2.5. All three remove compute, so running them at the base's 2817 steps slightly under-credits them, which is the conservative direction.
- `embed_gated_norm=false`: embedding → RMSNorm only.
- `final_gated_norm=false`: final AttnRes gate → RMSNorm → lm_head.
- `kda_gate_per_head=true`: `W_g` becomes [D, N] instead of [D, N·128], and `σ(x W_g)` is broadcast over each head's 128 channels. It stays on MuonH, like `W_β`.

| change | branch@commit | W&B | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ (paired) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no GatedNorm on the embedding | [`afa837be5f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/afa837be5f) | [lc1-b10-noembgn](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b10-noembgn) | 2817 | 748 | 3.3773 | 3.0863 | +0.0005 |
| no GatedNorm before the lm_head | [`afa837be5f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/afa837be5f) | [lc1-b10-nofingn](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b10-nofingn) | 2817 | 749 | 3.3822 | 3.0864 | +0.0006 |
| KDA output gate per head (not per channel) | [`afa837be5f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/afa837be5f) | [lc1-b10-kdagh](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b10-kdagh) | 2817 | 705 (−6%, see below) | 3.3877 | 3.0912 | **+0.0054** |
| both GatedNorms removed (embedding + lm_head input) | [`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9) | [lc1-b10-nogn2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b10-nogn2) | 2817 | 752 | 3.3803 | **3.0821** | **−0.0037** |

**Takeaway.**
- **Both GatedNorm removals are neutral** (+0.0005 embedding, +0.0006 lm_head input), so they are free simplifications. **Removing both gives 3.0821 (−0.0037)**, so they stack. The model is simpler and, if anything, better. The batch-12 bundle drops both.
- **The per-head KDA output gate is worse: +0.0054 at the same 2817 steps.** The per-channel gate carries information. It also ran 6% slower, because my `jnp.repeat` broadcast of the gate didn't fuse; a reshape to `[B, S, N, 128]` would avoid that. The step count was the same as the base, so the loss comparison is fair either way. Not pursuing it.

comments.author: AMX07
comments.body:
try NoPE on the MLA layers (drop Inkling), following Kimi K3 [https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K3/blob/main/k3_tech_report.pdf](url)

K3 and Kimi Linear both pair KDA with NoPE MLA, relying on KDA's recurrent decay for position. KMA already has the same pieces (KDA before every MLA layer, q/k/v ShortConvs), so Inkling may be redundant here.

From Opus 5.5:

**Implementation (small):**

- `GrugModelConfig.__post_init__`: remove the `mla requires inkling_relpos` check. MLA layers are all global, so `disable_rope=True` there, and removing `rel_pos` gives pure NoPE (no RoPE, no bias).
- `CausalSelfAttention.init`, MLA branch: `rel_pos=InklingRelPos.init(...) if cfg.inkling_relpos else None`.
- Check that the optimizer group routing Inkling `W_r`/`P` to Adam doesn't break when they're absent.

**Runs (d512, paired seed 0 vs the qk_mult-2.5 base, 3.0858):**
1. NoPE, qk_mult 2.5, steps from its own ex/s probe.
2. NoPE, qk_mult 2.0 and 3.5 (the current optimum was tuned with Inkling present).
3. Diagnostic: NoPE token-matched at 2817 steps, to separate "learns as well" from "trains faster."
4. If it loses slightly, try NoPE + ShortConv on MLA q only (keeps W_uk absorbable).

Replicate on seeds 1–2 if it clears 0.005 paired.

**For gate 2:** `attn_res_remat_attention` is forced on at d1280 partly because of the `[B, H, S, W]` Inkling bias. NoPE might let that remat be dropped at larger rungs, which is an extra speed gain there.

**Addresses** @AMX07's comment. Kimi K3 and Kimi Linear pair KDA with NoPE MLA and rely on KDA's decay for position; KMA already has KDA before every MLA layer. With `inkling_relpos=false`, the MLA layers are pure NoPE: they are all global, where RoPE is already off. The optimizer routing is unaffected, and the KDA tests and CPU smoke tests pass. **Takeaway.**

Removing both GatedNorms, which was −0.0037 on the qk-2.5 base, costs about +0.004 once the lm_head z-loss is off. Plausibly both were controlling the scale of the lm_head input.

It is a tuned constant, so it needs to hold across scales. It may be that the right multiplier depends on depth or width, or that d768 needs its own value; a learnable scalar at init 2.5 would adapt per rung. I'll decide once the two other d768 runs (bundle, and qk + β1 0.8 + z-loss 0) finish.

1. **AttnRes weight logging.** Every gate now logs its token-mean softmax weight per source, as `train/attn_res/w_gNN_bMM` (source = block MM) and `w_gNN_p` (the running partial). At d512, block 00 is the embedding and block k is layer k−1's output. Gates are numbered attn₀, MoE₀, …, attn₅, MoE₅, final. `lc1-b14-ref` reruns the current best config with this logging. I'll post a gates × sources heatmap at a few training steps once it finishes.
2. **KDA β MLP:** `β = σ(SiLU(x W_β↓) W_β↑)`, rank 16 (`kda_beta_rank`). Variants:
   - MuonH at 2× (the current `W_β` group) with random init.
   - Adam with random init.
   - Adam with `W_β↑` zero-initialized, so β = 0.5 at start like LoRA. Zero init can't use MuonH, which keeps each matrix at its initial norm.
   - An LR check if one wins.
3. **Smaller KV.** The MLA KV latent is the only KV cache that grows with context; KDA's state is fixed-size. I'm trying latent 256 and 128 (currently 512). Cross-layer latent reuse, with layer 5 reading layer 3's latent, comes next if the smaller latents hold up.

The launcher bundles the working tree. Three runs were submitted a moment before the commit landed, and ran with the same code as `eb17304a56` (the only difference is a docstring). The submit script now refuses a dirty tree.

**AttnRes source weights** ([lc1-b14-ref](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b14-ref), current best config; token-mean softmax weight per gate × source at steps 100, 1408 and 2816; gray = source not visible to that gate):

![AttnRes source weights](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/75caa89903ede30815f61c23ef54ca935ec43141/v1/attnres_weights_lc1-b14-ref.png)

What the average distribution shows (final step):
- **Attention gates mostly read the immediately preceding layer's output**, a learned residual stream. The weight on it decays with depth: L1 0.73, L2 0.66, L3 0.48, L4 0.43.
- **The last MLA layer (L5) is the exception.** It puts 0.32 on L2's output, more than on L3 (0.17) or L4 (0.15), so it skips back over the two most recent layers. That fits idea `#6` (late attention layers don't want the latest sublayer outputs).
- **MoE gates mostly read their own layer's attention output (the partial):** 0.85 at L0, down to 0.40 at L4. L5's MoE instead splits across L3 out (0.18), L4 out (0.31) and the partial (0.31).
- **The final gate feeding the lm_head uses almost only the last three layers:** L3 0.16, L4 0.33, L5 0.41. The embedding and L0–L2 get ≤ 0.05 there, although every attention gate keeps 0.13–0.27 on the embedding.
- **The pattern forms early.** By step 1408 it is nearly final, and at step 100 the gates are still close to uniform.

Also: the rerun of the current best config landed at 3.0788 vs 3.0805 before, on the same seed. **Same-seed reruns differ by about 0.002** from GPU nondeterminism, so paired Δ below about 0.003 is noise.

**Takeaway.**
- **KDA β as a rank-16 MLP is neutral in every variant:** −0.0004 (MuonH 2×, random init), +0.0006 (Adam), +0.0012 (Adam with W_β↑ zero-init). The linear β already seems to capture what the gate needs at this scale. Two more tunings follow in batch 15: rank 64 and a higher Adam LR.
- **A smaller MLA KV latent clearly hurts:** 512 → 256 gives +0.016 and → 128 gives +0.019, with no measurable speedup at d512. Attention there is a small share of step time. Batch 15 tests cross-layer reuse instead: the last MLA layer reads the first MLA layer's KV latent, which halves the MLA cache.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 15: full AttnRes, per-layer gradient norms, per-expert hyperball (@ClassicLarry), plus KV reuse and β-MLP tuning** (d512, 2817 steps, paired seed 0 vs the current best config, qk 2.5 + β1 0.8 + z-loss 0: **3.0797**, the mean of two same-seed runs)

**Addresses** the comment asking for full AttnRes to see MLP-vs-attention source trends, per-layer gradient norms for routed experts, shared experts and attention (are layer-0 routed experts dying?), and a hyperball per expert. Also continues batch 14's KV-reuse and β-MLP requests. Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch14` @ `7112828d18`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/7112828d18).

**Per-layer gradient norms** ([lc1-b14-ref](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b14-ref), current best config; W&B already logs these per layer; 25-point rolling median, log scale):

![per-layer gradient norms](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/55097ad3a9b3d66a0edffc0d066535971cc669d3/v1/gradnorm_lc1-b14-ref.png)

- **Layer-0 routed experts are not dying.** Their gradient norm *rises* over training, from 0.015 early to 0.019 at the end. That is on par with L1 (0.018) and above L2 (0.016). Every layer's routed-expert gradient norm grows across training, the global layers L3–L5 most (0.024–0.027).
- **The shared experts do the opposite.** Their gradient norms fall after about step 1300 in every layer; L0 drops from 0.021 to 0.011. The shared path does its learning early, and the routed experts carry the later learning.
- **Attention gradients decay steadily** from their early peak, fastest in L0. The exception is L5 (last MLA): it dips early and then climbs back to the second-largest norm.
- A layer-mean norm can hide individual dead experts. The per-expert routing counts are computed but not logged. If you want per-expert detail, I'll add a per-expert load / grad-norm histogram next.

**Runs**
- **Full AttnRes** (`attn_res_full`): every attention and every MoE output is its own source, so the final gate reads 13 sources instead of 7, and the weight logging now separates attention sources from MoE sources. A heatmap follows when it lands. It costs slightly more than block mode; I'll check its ex/s and rerun at a fair step count if it's more than 1% slower.
- **Per-expert hyperball** (`hyperball_per_expert`): the MuonH projection normalizes each routed expert's matrix to its own Frobenius norm. Before, one sphere covered each layer's whole `[E, in, out]` stack, which let norm shift between experts (±3% per step in a toy check). That is one possible route for experts to shrink.
- **MLA KV-latent reuse** (`mla_share_kv_latent`): layer 5 reuses layer 3's normed 512-wide latent, with its own W_uk / W_uv so absorption still works. This halves the MLA KV cache. Shrinking the latent to 256 cost +0.016, so this tests reuse instead.
- **β MLP tuning:** rank 64, and rank 16 on MuonH at 4× (vs 2×).
- **MLA placement** (@ClassicLarry's follow-up): MLA moves to layers 3 and 6, i.e. KDA, KDA, MLA, KDA, KDA, MLA, via a new `global_layers` override. It runs on 2 seeds.
- **Full AttnRes also tests @ClassicLarry's hypothesis** that L5's MLA wants the L3 and L4 attention outputs but not their MoE outputs. The full-mode heatmap gives attention and MoE sources separate columns.
- **d768, learnable qk_mult initialized at 2.5.** Fixed 2.5 gave only −0.0014 at d768 vs −0.009 at d512. This shows where the scalar wants to go at d768.

**Full AttnRes source weights** ([lc1-b15-arfull](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b15-arfull); every attention and MoE output is its own column):

![full AttnRes source weights](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/023feb0dd73ce75e202b69cf32b11513bb4855bc/v1/attnres_full_lc1-b15-arfull.png)

Final-step readout:
- **L5's MLA gate (the hypothesis):** L3 MoE 0.21, L2 attn 0.17, L1 MoE 0.11. It avoids L4 MoE (0.03), L3 attn (0.03) and L4 attn (0.08). It does skip back over the most recent sublayers, but not by preferring attention outputs over MoE outputs; its top source is an MoE output (L3's).
- **The general pattern alternates by sublayer type.** Attention gates read the *previous MoE output*: L1 attn → L0 MoE 0.78, L2 attn → L1 MoE 0.57, L4 attn → L3 MoE 0.41. They nearly ignore the previous *attention* output (0.02–0.13). MoE gates read their own layer's attention output (L1 0.49, L4 0.20) plus the previous MoE output.
- **The final gate spreads over the last few sublayers:** L5 MoE 0.26, L4 MoE 0.20, L5 attn 0.14, L4 attn 0.13.

**Takeaway.**
- **Full AttnRes is neutral on loss (−0.0013) and 3% slower** (724 vs about 745 ex/s). At a fair ~2714 steps it would be slightly negative, so block AttnRes stays. The source-type pattern above is the useful output of this run.
- **MLA at layers 3 & 6 is neutral** (+0.0005 / +0.0006 on seeds 0 and 1), so the current placement at 4 & 6 stays.
- **Per-expert hyperball: neutral (+0.0017),** and about 1% slower.
- **KDA β MLP: all 5 variants neutral** (−0.0004 to +0.0023): rank 16 and 64, MuonH 2× and 4×, Adam with random or zero init. The linear β stays.
- **MLA KV-latent reuse costs +0.0056.** L5 reads L3's latent, which halves the MLA KV cache. Halving the latent instead (512 → 256) cost +0.016, so reuse is the cheaper way to shrink the cache if long-context inference memory matters at hero scale. It is not a loss win, so it stays out of the recipe. The **d768 learnable-qk** run is still going.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
L4 KDA pays almost zero attention to all prior attention layers. That is suspicious. Perhaps the state tracking nature of KDA gets overwhelmed with too much cross token smearing. Block attention residuals doesn't let KDA layers pick out just the prior MLPs.

Lets try full attention residuals, but block L4 KDA from attending to any prior attention layer outputs. If that improves over the full attention residuals baseline, it indicates an opportunity. We should also assess the impact of dropping sconv from the attention outputs and mlp outputs.

Standard attention residuals follows a 'push' methodology. Each layer output gets to decide what future layers it gets propogated to, since the queries are static per layer. Alternatively, one could use a 'pull' methodology. Every output submodule has a static key, and the query is defined by the current residual stream activation. Lets try that approach, zeroing the keys at init. Also try a hybrid, where we follow standard attn residuals, but just vary the embed. It seems odd that the embed should pre-decide how much it appears in each subsequent layer. To get the embed logit, run a linear projection over the current residual stream. (So we can think of that as the query is the residual stream, and the key is a learned weight).

comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 18: AttnRes routing structure (@ClassicLarry's latest comment), ShortConv ablations, and a linear-attention variant** (d512, 2817 steps, paired seed 0 on the current bundle with z-loss kept: qk 2.5 + β1 0.8 + no GatedNorms = **3.0854**)

**Addresses** the comment about L4 KDA ignoring earlier attention outputs, the ShortConv ablations, and "pull" vs "push" AttnRes. Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch14` @ `5eb01900ba`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/5eb01900ba).

1. **Full AttnRes with L4's KDA attention gate blocked from every earlier attention output** (`attn_res_mask_attn_for=4`). That gate reads only the embedding and the MoE outputs; the masked sources get a −1e9 logit. It is compared against full AttnRes on the same base (`lc1-b18-full`). The batch-15 full run used z-loss 0, so it's rerun here. If the masked version wins, it points to KDA wanting to pick out MoE outputs, which Block AttnRes can't do.
2. **ShortConv ablations:** drop the conv on the attention sublayer output (`sconv_sites=mlp`; only the MLA layers had one, since KDA's output never did), on the MoE output (`sconv_sites=attn`), and both (`sconv_sites=`). KDA's own q/k/v convs stay.
3. **Pull AttnRes** (`attn_res_pull`). Each source has a static learned key k_n, zero-initialized (the running partial has its own). A gate's query is its **current residual stream**: the RMS-normed plain sum of the sources it can see. So logit_n = rms_norm(Σ sources) · k_n. Keys train with Adam at 0.1×, like the push queries. At init it's identical to push (uniform mix).
4. **Hybrid:** push AttnRes, except the **embedding's logit is pulled**: a learned zero-initialized vector per gate, dotted with the gate's RMS-normed current stream (`attn_res_pull_embed`). The embedding no longer pre-decides its weight in each layer.
5. **Gated-DeltaNet-style per-head decay in KDA** (`kda_decay_per_head`): one log-decay per head instead of per channel. This is idea `#5`, a different linear attention.

A depth-1 **MTP** head (idea `#13`: predict t+2 from h_t + W·norm(embed(t+1)) through the shared lm_head, weight 0.3) is implemented at [`06bbf60466`](/06bbf60466). It adds a second lm_head pass, which is expensive at d512, The probe measured 689.6 vs 754.1 ex/s (−8.6%), so it runs at 2576 fixed-time steps.

- **Blocking L4's KDA attention gate from earlier attention outputs hurts: +0.0138 vs full AttnRes.** So KDA does want the earlier attention outputs, even though, in full AttnRes, L4's gate ends up weighting mostly the most recent MoE output.
- **Pull AttnRes (+0.0093) and the pulled embedding logit (+0.0071) are both worse**, and both are about 4% slower: each gate has to sum its visible sources for the query. Push AttnRes stays.
- **The ShortConv on attention outputs is removable** (+0.0005, neutral; only the MLA layers had it). Removing the MoE-output ShortConv is slightly worse (+0.0030) despite 1% more speed. Removing both gives +0.0026, which matches the MoE-conv cost. The MoE-output ShortConv earns its keep; the attention-output one does not.
- **GDN-style per-head decay is clearly worse: +0.0129.** KDA's per-channel forget gate matters at no extra speed cost.
- **The first MTP run's eval is invalid.** My MTP term was added inside `next_token_loss`, which the Paloma eval also calls, so the reported eval loss (4.69) included it. Fixed at [`2f06885909`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/2f06885909): training-only terms (MTP, AttnRes z-loss) are now added only in the training step. **The rerun is clearly worse: 3.2272 (+0.14)**, and its mid-run eval is already far behind (3.487 vs ~3.37). With only a linear MTP head and no block of its own, the final hidden state has to serve both t+1 and t+2 through the shared lm_head. DeepSeek's MTP has a full transformer block in that path, which would cost even more at d512. It is also 8.6% slower. MTP was a long shot, tried once and dropped at this rung.

comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 19: a real go at Online KL-Shampoo, applied selectively (@ClassicLarry), and the ShortConv comparison at d768**

**Addresses** the comment asking to give [Online KL-Shampoo](https://blog.tilderesearch.com/blog/online-kl-shampoo) a real go, applied selectively so we can see its direction per matrix family, and to compare dropping all branch-output ShortConvs at d768.

**What the earlier attempt found** (branch `okls-optimizer`, on the pre-KMA baseline). It replaced MuonH on *every* matrix with OKLS's own muP-scaled, AdamC-decayed update. It never beat MuonH (+0.005 to +0.027 over an LR sweep, 16% slower), and its one hyperball variant crashed before step 25. The crash matches the broken-scipy job environment seen elsewhere, so it was never actually tested.

**This version** ([`7d5f5dd116`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/7d5f5dd116)):
- `okls_targets` picks matrix families; everything else stays on MuonH. The families are:
  - **attn**: MLA `w_q/w_o/w_dkv/w_uk/w_uv` and KDA `w_q/w_k/w_v/w_o/w_g`
  - **routed**: the expert gate/up/down stacks
  - **shared**: the shared experts
  - **latent**: the LatentMoE down/up projections
  - **gated_norm**: the GatedNorms
- For the selected matrices, the **direction** is the OKLS whitening `U = S_a^{-1/2} · N · S_b^{-1/2}`. Here N is Nesterov momentum, S_a/S_b are the Kronecker-factor EMAs with the blog's β1 0.9684 / β2 0.9482, and the roots come from 10-step Scaled-CANS coupled Newton-Schulz. **That direction then takes MuonH's hyperball step at the MuonH LR.** Only the direction changes, so there's no new LR scale to tune, and the matrices stay on their Frobenius spheres like the rest of the model.
- CPU checks: the 6 ported OKLS math tests pass (CANS inverse-sqrt accuracy, warm start, whitening conditioning, norm-preserving hyperball step). Routing is verified per family.
- 80-step throughput probes are running for 4 selections. OKLS roots cost O(d³) per matrix, so each gets its own fixed-time step count. Then the full runs go, paired against the current bundle's seed 0 (3.0854):
  - attention only (fp32 CANS)
  - routed experts only (fp16 CANS, since there are 384 small matrices per layer)
  - shared + latent (fp32)
  - all families (fp16)
  - Promising families get LR and β2 variations after that.

**d768 without branch-output ShortConvs** ([lc1-b19-d768-nosc](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b19-d768-nosc), `sconv_sites=`, 7325 steps) vs the z-loss-kept bundle at d768 (2.8046). At d512 it was +0.0026, and dropping only the attention-output conv was neutral.

| OKLS attn, roots refreshed every 10 steps (fp32), probe | [`7bcae1918a`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/7bcae1918a) | [lc1-b19p-oklsattn-k10](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b19p-oklsattn-k10) | 80 | 713.3 (−5.4%) | — | — | — |

| **OKLS attn, roots every 10 steps, fp16 CANS: fixed-time** | [`7bcae1918a`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/7bcae1918a) | [lc1-b19-oklsattn-ft](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b19-oklsattn-ft) | 2693 | 714 | 3.3786 | 3.0879 | +0.0025 |
| same, seed 1 | [`7bcae1918a`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/7bcae1918a) | [lc1-b19-oklsattn-ft-s1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b19-oklsattn-ft-s1) | 2693 | 712 | 3.3849 | 3.0908 | +0.0006 vs 3.0902 |

**OKLS cost.** The probes put OKLS at 19–21% slower for a single family and 31% slower for all families, because of the per-step O(d³) CANS roots. Following @ClassicLarry's follow-up, the full runs are **token-matched (2817 steps)** to first check for a loss win; fixed-time accounting comes after, if one shows up.

**On KDA at layer 0 and a decay that "looks at the state first".** The observation is right, and it holds for every KDA layer, not just layer 0. KDA's forget gate (like GDN's and Mamba's) is **input-dependent but not state-dependent**: g_t = f(x_t), where at layer 0 x_t is just the normed embedding.
- **Why it's built that way:** the chunked algorithm needs every position's gates *before* running the recurrence, which is what makes it parallel. A decay that reads S_{t−1} makes the layer a nonlinear RNN (LSTM/sLSTM-style), which can only run step by step. That's the trade Kimi, GDN and Mamba all make.
- **What already reads the state:** the delta rule itself. S_t = (I − β kkᵀ) Diag(e^g) S_{t−1} + β k vᵀ first erases whatever S currently stores along key k (β k (kᵀS)), and only then writes v. So "how much to overwrite" is content-addressed against the state; the per-channel decay is only the context-free background forgetting.
- **Two cheap probes of the intuition that stay parallel:**
  1. `kda_decay_conv`: a 4-tap causal ShortConv over the rank-128 decay input, so g_t sees the last few tokens instead of just its own (the q/k/v paths already have such convs). It applies to all KDA layers.
  2. Layer 0 as MLA instead of KDA. If KDA-at-layer-0 is the weak spot, a softmax layer there should show it. It is slower, so the token-matched run is only a first look.

**Interim.**
- **Layer 0 as MLA is neutral (−0.0006)**, and at d512 it runs at the same speed as KDA there (757 ex/s). So KDA at layer 0 isn't a weak spot: a softmax layer does no better.
- **ShortConv on the KDA decay input: −0.0043**, 1.6% slower. **The seed-1 replicate gives +0.0005, so the paired mean is −0.002: within noise**, and it's 1.6% slower. Local context for the decay doesn't measurably help at d512.

**OKLS, token-matched (directional check):**
- **Attention matrices: −0.0055 (seed 0) and −0.0058 (seed 1).** The OKLS direction consistently helps per step on the MLA and KDA projections.
- **Routed experts +0.0033, shared + latent +0.0042:** worse than Newton-Schulz on the MoE matrices.
- **All families together: +0.0001.** The attention gain is cancelled by the MoE losses, at 33% lower throughput.

So OKLS has a real per-step benefit, and it is specific to the attention projections. At fixed time, the attention-only variant is 18% slower in the full run (614 vs ~750 ex/s) because the O(d³) Scaled-CANS roots were computed four times per step. Next, cutting the cost with standard Shampoo practice ([`7bcae1918a`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/7bcae1918a)):
1. The inverse roots are **stored** in optimizer state rather than recomputed for the EMA.
2. They are **refreshed only every k steps** (`okls_root_every`), via one step-level `lax.cond` so non-refresh steps skip CANS entirely.
3. Optionally, **fp16 CANS**.

A CPU check over 12 steps shows k=10 stays within 3% of refreshing every step. Throughput probes for attention-only at k=10 (fp32 and fp16) are running. A seed-1 token-matched replicate of OKLS-attention is also running. The probes put OKLS-attention at −5.4% (fp32) and **−4.4% (fp16 CANS)** with roots refreshed every 10 steps, down from −18%. The fp16 variant now runs **at fixed time (2693 steps)** on 2 seeds.

**Note:** the OKLS runs in this batch use a *hybrid*: OKLS's whitened direction with MuonH's norm-preserving hyperball step and LR. They are not the paper's full update; see the correction in batch 21.

**Takeaway (OKLS).**
- **OKLS gives a consistent per-step gain on the attention projections:** −0.0055 / −0.0058 token-matched on 2 seeds. On the MoE matrices it loses: routed +0.0033, shared + latent +0.0042. Applied everywhere, the effects cancel (+0.0001).
- **At d512 fixed time the gain doesn't survive:** +0.0025 / +0.0006 (mean +0.0016). That's with roots stored and refreshed every 10 steps, and fp16 CANS. The overhead fell from −18% to about −5% throughput, and the 10-step refresh may give back part of the per-step gain.
- **For hero scale,** this is one of the few changes whose d512 penalty is mostly overhead. Optimizer cost is a much smaller share of step time at large width and batch, so OKLS on attention projections is worth revisiting in a larger-rung, fixed-time test. I'm not adding it to the gate-2 recipe.
- **KDA-decay ShortConv:** −0.0043 / +0.0005, mean −0.002, so within noise. **Layer 0 as MLA:** neutral. Neither helps at d512.
- **Dropping all branch-output ShortConvs at d768: +0.0049** (2.8095 vs 2.8046), with 1.3% more throughput, worth about 0.001 back at a fair step count. **The output ShortConvs still pay for themselves at d768, even with KDA,** so they stay. At d512, only the attention-output conv (MLA layers) was removable, and it's worth too little to change the recipe.

comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 21: what drives AttnRes, and which attention projections OKLS helps (@ClassicLarry)** (d512)

**Addresses** the comment asking to dissect full AttnRes and to narrow OKLS down to specific attention projections with their best LR, plus the article's LR schedule. Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch14` @ `ab77de298e`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ab77de298e).

**1. AttnRes dissection.** The baseline is full AttnRes on the same recipe at fair fixed-time steps (`lc1-b18-full-fair`, 3.0774 at 2712 steps, seed 0); every run is paired against it. New knobs:
- `attn_res_final_mode=uniform`: the final query is fixed at 0, so the lm_head input is a plain average of all streams.
- `attn_res_final_mode=sum`: the lm_head input is a straight sum of all streams, like a standard residual.
- `attn_res_sum_inputs=q` / `k` / `v` / `mlp`: one component at a time reads the **straight sum** of its visible streams, through the same RMSNorm → GatedNorm, instead of its AttnRes mix. For MLA, k and v share a latent, so a K-only or V-only override computes a second latent from the sum stream with the same W_dkv and latent norm.
- At init the sum and mix inputs are identical: the zero-initialized queries give a uniform average, and RMSNorm removes the scale. Any difference is learned.

**2. OKLS on individual attention projections.** Token-matched at 2817 steps, per your earlier note, paired against the bundle's seed 0 (3.0854); OKLS on all attention was −0.0057 over 2 seeds.
- Projection families, KDA and MLA together: q (`w_q`), k (KDA `w_k`, MLA `w_uk`), v (KDA `w_v`, MLA `w_uv`), o (`w_o`), and other (MLA `w_dkv`, KDA gate `w_g`).
- LR on all attention at ×0.67 and ×1.5 of the MuonH LR (`okls_lr_mult`).
- **From the article:** linear decay after warmup (1B tokens), β1 0.9684 / β2 0.9482 (it stresses β1² ≈ β2), OKLS on hidden matrices only. Most relevant here: "**even a single-step delay in updating the preconditioner severely destabilizes training.**" That likely explains why my every-10-steps root refresh lost the gain at fixed time. These runs use **fresh roots every step**: stored roots feed the EMA, and fresh roots do the whitening, so 2 CANS roots per step instead of 4. They also use fp16 CANS to keep the cost down. The article also finds its largest gains on the value projections and MLP matrices.

**Correction: what "OKLS" has meant in batches 19–21 so far** (@ClassicLarry asked whether we apply the paper's full OKLS; we don't). The runs so far use a **hybrid**. OKLS's momentum, preconditioner EMAs and whitened direction `U = S_a^-1/2 · N · S_b^-1/2` are as in the paper. The **step** is MuonH's, though: `U` is rescaled to the weight's norm × the MuonH LR and projected back onto the weight's fixed Frobenius sphere, with no weight decay. There is no Newton-Schulz in that path, but the step rule and the fixed weight norms are MuonH's. The paper instead applies `lr · c · s_shape · U`: peak LR 0.09434, a per-matrix muP shape scale, Nesterov variance correction, AdamC decoupled weight decay 0.0303, and weight norms free to change.

The paper's update is now selectable as `okls_hyperball=false` ([`e15a46b973`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/e15a46b973)), with fresh roots every step and fp16 CANS. Four **paper-mode runs** are queued first, token-matched: attention only, all hidden matrices (as in the paper), and attention at peak LR ×0.5 and ×2. The previous session's paper-mode test replaced MuonH on every matrix of the pre-KMA baseline and lost by +0.005 to +0.027. It had never been run on this model or selectively.

| component that reads the straight residual sum instead of its AttnRes mix | Δ |
|---|---|
| **MoE input** | **+0.0275** |

comments.body:
On KDA, lets try dropping alpha entirely, 1 layer at a time. To see which layers need the decay.
Do the same with beta.

The push mechanism on attn residuals is interesting. I wonder if KDA could benefit from a push mechanism-when a key and value get written to S, normally future tokens have to decide whether or not to decay the state. but alternately, a token could choose its own half-life when it gets written to S. Think through how we'd set up this math, then try some options. Likely we need to manage a second S that decays each step, and subtracts itself from the main S on each position. The initial hypers will likely be off, so get it a few chances.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 22: which KDA layers need decay and write strength, and "push" decay (@ClassicLarry)** (d512, token-matched at 2817 steps, paired seed 0 vs the gate-2 recipe `lc1-b17-bzl` = **3.0834**)

**Addresses** the comment asking to drop KDA's decay (α) and β one layer at a time, and to set up a "push" decay where each written token chooses its own half-life.

**1. Per-layer ablations** ([`d80ac50049`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/d80ac50049)). `kda_no_decay_layers=L` sets g = 0 in layer L, so that state never forgets. `kda_no_beta_layers=L` sets β = 1, a full-strength delta-rule write. The KDA layers are 0, 1, 2 and 4 (3 and 5 are MLA). A CPU check confirms only the targeted layer's parameters stop receiving gradient.

**2. Push decay: the math** ([`d80ac50049`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/d80ac50049)).
- **Pull (current KDA):** `S_t = (I − β_t k_t k_tᵀ) Diag(e^{g_t}) S_{t−1} + β_t k_t v_tᵀ`. The **reader** t sets one decay applied to everything already stored.
- **Push (ideal):** write i sets its own rate λ_i, and its contribution at time t is `e^{−λ_i (t−i)} · β_i k_i v_iᵀ`. Arbitrary per-write rates don't compose into one running state.
- **Push with buckets:** keep M delta-rule states, each decaying at its own **static, learned, per-channel** rate λ_m that no token controls. The writer splits its write with weights π_{t,m}:
  `S⁽ᵐ⁾_t = (I − β_t π_{t,m} k kᵀ) Diag(e^{−λ_m}) S⁽ᵐ⁾_{t−1} + β_t π_{t,m} k_t v_tᵀ`, and the read is `o_t = Σ_m S⁽ᵐ⁾_tᵀ q_t`.
  - With M = 2 this is your "second S": a slow state and a fast one, where each token decides what fraction of itself is temporary. The "subtract the decayed copy from the main S" form is the same thing written differently: S_perm + S_temp.
  - Each bucket is an ordinary KDA recurrence with a constant g and a scaled β, so the existing chunked kernel runs it unchanged. The cost is one extra kernel pass per bucket, about 8% step time per bucket at d512. These runs are token-matched, to check for a loss effect first.
  - **Parameters:** `push_decay` [M, heads, 128] holds the bucket decay logits, initialized log-spaced over a |g| range. `W_push` [D, heads·M] is zero-initialized, so the split starts uniform. Both train with Adam like the other KDA decay parameters.
- **Hybrid:** each bucket decays at the reader's g plus its own static rate, clamped to KDA's −5 per-token floor. Both writer and reader get a say.

| push, 2 buckets, wider init (\|g\| 0.005 / 1.0) | [`608c000007`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/608c000007) | [lc1-b22-push2-wide](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b22-push2-wide) | 2817 | 600 | 3.3925 | 3.1065 | +0.0231 vs 3.0834 |

These submit as run slots free, after batch 21's OKLS runs.

**Takeaway:** pending.

**Readout.**
- **Decay:** every KDA layer needs its decay. Removing it costs +0.019 (layer 0), +0.005 (layer 1), +0.012 (layer 2) and +0.008 (layer 4).
- **β:** removing it from any single layer is within noise (+0.0001 to +0.0032). Removing it from several layers at once is consistently a little worse, though: +0.0076 for layers 0, 1, 4 and +0.0042 for all four layers. It also gains no throughput (777–784 vs 786 ex/s), so **β stays**.
- **Push decay (the writer picks its own half-life) is a negative result.** Every variant lost by +0.012 to +0.023, and the second state costs 19–38% of throughput (600 and 459 ex/s vs 740). The best was the hybrid that keeps the reader's decay (+0.0124). No more push variants unless there's a new angle.

comments.body:
🤖 **Batches 23–24: the MoE-input split, router variants, RMT-inspired AttnRes, and the MFU plan (@ClassicLarry)** (d512)

**Addresses** four comments: AttnRes on the shared vs routed experts; low-rank router variants; combining [Residual Matrix Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.22696) with AttnRes; and a shift toward MFU gains if these don't pan out.

**1. Which part of the MoE input needs AttnRes** ([`c786c05f69`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c786c05f69)). Batch 21 found that the MoE input reading the straight sum costs +0.028. This splits it: the shared experts only, the routed path only (router + latent-down), and the router alone. The router run separates the routing decision from the expert input. The runs are full AttnRes at 2712 steps, paired against 3.0774.

**2. Low-rank router** ([`c786c05f69`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c786c05f69)): `logits = f(x W_r↓) W_r↑` at rank 32 or 128, where f is identity, a learnable RMSNorm, or SiLU. W_r↓ replaces the router column block in the fused MoE-input GEMM. The logits are computed in fp32 as before, both matrices train with Adam and the router weight decay, and QB balancing is unchanged. Token-matched, paired against the gate-2 recipe (3.0834).

**3. RMT × AttnRes** ([`82abc339ac`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/82abc339ac)). RMT stores sublayer outputs in an outer-product matrix and reads it with **R per-head read keys**. AttnRes is already a residual *memory* with one slot per source, read by a softmax over pseudo-query scores; the dissection found that different readers (V and MoE vs Q/K) want different mixes. Two variants borrow RMT's per-head, per-reader retrieval:
- **Multi-head AttnRes** (`attn_res_heads=H`): each gate's pseudo-query is split into H chunks of D/H. Chunk h scores the sources on its own channel slice, with the same parameter-free RMS key norm, and mixes that slice with its own softmax. It's H retrieval heads over the same memory, adds no parameters, and reduces exactly to today's AttnRes at H = 1. H = 4 and 8.
- **A separate V-input gate** (`attn_res_v_gate`): each layer gets a second zero-init pseudo-query for its value projections, so V reads its own mix while Q/K keep the attention gate's.
- Heavier RMT pieces (a matrix residual with outer-product writes) would replace AttnRes rather than combine with it. I'm holding those unless these show signal.

**4. MFU.** A fresh 60-step profile of the gate-2 recipe is first in the queue, to pick the low-hanging items. One suspect is already visible: the per-step logging I added (about 70 AttnRes weight, query-norm and qk_mult scalars every step) goes through the blocking host loop. Recent runs sit at ~740 ex/s vs ~751 before it. Making the logging sparse is the first cheap item, and the profile will rank the rest.

One more silly idea: instead of a fixed query in attn residuals per layer, lets try 2 queries per layer. Then the residual stream goes through a linear -> sigmoid to weight the two queries. each query pulls a weighted sample of the earlier outputs. then we merge the weighted samples according to the weights on the queries. To keep the queries different, give them slightly different init. (but we still want init to be very close to even over all outputs). 

Another variation is to have attention residuals only learn the delta vs equal share. So layer input = lambda1*attn_res_input + lambda2*standard_input. lambda1 and lambda 2 are learned scalars per layer. Or those scalars can be made dynamic.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 25: two-query AttnRes, blended AttnRes, and spreading the MoE input** (branch `ladderclimb_v1_batch14`, d512, paired against the current best, 3.0834)

These follow up [the two-query / λ-blend comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5844691943) and [the MLP input-spread comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5844712356). Every flag defaults off. The changes apply to every AttnRes gate, including the final one.

**Two queries per gate (`attn_res_dual_query`).** Each gate keeps its zero-init query `q_a` and adds a second query `q_b ~ N(0, σ)`, so both start close to an even mix over the sources.
- Each query takes its own softmax-weighted sample of the sources, giving `mix_a` and `mix_b`.
- Merge per token: `s = σ(rms_norm(stream) · w + b)`, input = `s · mix_a + (1 − s) · mix_b`. Here `stream` is the plain sum of the gate's sources.
- `w` and `b` are zero-init, so `s = ½` at init.
- σ is tried at 0.005 and 0.02. The initial logit spread is about σ·√D, i.e. 0.11 and 0.45.

**Blend with the standard residual (`attn_res_blend`).** Input = `λ₁ · attnres_mix + λ₂ · mean(sources)`, with learned scalars per gate, both init 1.
- I used the mean rather than the sum. The RMSNorm that follows makes the two equivalent, apart from how λ₂ is parameterized.
- **static:** λ are plain scalars.
- **dynamic:** λₖ also gets `+ rms_norm(stream) · wₖ`, a zero-init per-token term.
- Caveat: at init the AttnRes mix *is* the uniform mean, and the following RMSNorm cancels scale. So the λ gradient is about 0 until the gate moves off uniform. The params are on Adam, which rescales small gradients, so they will still move.

**MLP input spread.** Here is how I read the idea. How well a neuron can choose which fraction of tokens it fires on depends on the spread of `w·x`. If `x` sits on a small, anisotropic manifold (a large shared mean direction and a few dominant directions), most `w` see little variance, and the high-variance directions dominate learning.
- **Whitening** the input (`x → C^{-1/2}(x − μ)`) makes every direction carry unit variance, so any `w` sees the same spread.
- For a linear layer that follows, whitening is a reparameterization of `W`, so it adds no expressivity. It changes what Adam and Muon do: it is K-FAC's / Shampoo's input-side factor applied to the activations. Muon orthogonalizes the update but ignores the input covariance, so that factor is what our optimizer is missing.
- It also changes the router, since QB reads the whitened input.
- The matching knobs:
  - **center:** subtract the batch mean (over all tokens, stop-gradient) from every MoE input.
  - **whiten, p:** `x → (x − μ) · C^{−p/2}`, with `C` the batch covariance. Its eigenvalues are trace-normalized, then shrunk by `+1e-3`, via `eigh` on a 512×512 matrix. Stop-gradient, so there is no backward through `eigh`. p = 0.5 is half-whitening (Shampoo's exponent); p = 1 is full ZCA whitening.
- Caveats:
  - Batch statistics leak about 1/N of each token into all others (N ≈ 130k tokens), and eval uses the eval batch's own statistics. If whitening wins, I'll switch to EMA statistics from previous steps, which are strictly causal.
  - These runs are **data-matched** (2817 steps). If one wins, I'll check its throughput and fixed-time step count.

Other ideas for the spread question (not yet run): a spread penalty on the MoE input's covariance (for example log-det or effective rank), an EMA-whitened version as above, or whitening only the expert down path while leaving the router alone.

comments.body: On lc1-b17-d768-bzl, we scaled the number of steps, so its not clear how much the ML changes happened. If we just consider the compute and the scaling law, what is the speedup of the ML changes. assume equal tps.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 Re: [the question on `lc1-b17-d768-bzl`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5848255022). **The ML changes alone are worth about 1.10× compute at d768** (range 1.10–1.11×). At d512 they're worth about 1.11× (range 1.10–1.12×). This counts only the model/optimizer changes and gives no credit for throughput.

**Method.** I fit the clean-KMA ladder (d512 through d1280, each at its reference budget) to `L(C) = 1.2 + A·C^(−α)`, with L∞ = 1.2 as in the objective. The fit gives α = 0.0865, with residuals within ±0.009. For a candidate run, the effective compute multiplier over the baseline *at the same rung* is `((L_base − 1.2) / (L_run − 1.2))^(1/α)`. I anchor on the actual baseline run at that rung rather than the fitted curve, because the d768 baseline sits 0.009 below the fit. Dividing that multiplier by the compute the run actually used removes the extra steps. What remains is the ML-only speedup at equal tokens per second.

| rung | baseline loss | bzl loss | bzl compute / baseline | total effective multiplier | **ML-only (equal tps)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| d768 | 2.8234 (2 runs) | 2.8016 | 1.057× (7324 vs 6928 steps) | 1.17× (1.16–1.18) | **1.10× (1.10–1.11)** |
| d512 | 3.1223 (2 seeds) | 3.0834 | 1.138× (2817 vs 2475 steps) | 1.27× (1.25–1.28) | **1.11× (1.10–1.12)** |

The ranges come from α: the local d512→d768 slope is 0.0913, the global fit 0.0865, and the local d768→d1024 slope 0.0840.

**Caveats**
- **Noise:** the noise level (about 0.005 of loss) corresponds to about ±3.5% compute at d768. The d768 figure rests on one bzl run.
- **Extra steps:** crediting them through the across-rung law assumes the rungs are near compute-optimal. There, a small extra amount of data alone buys about the same as extra compute along the frontier.
- **Throughput:** the extra steps come from throughput work: the fp32 embedding-gather backward (+12% ex/s) and, going forward, the MFU fixes (+5.5%). That is where the rest of the total 1.17–1.27× comes from.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 28: q/k sharpness, V-gate heatmaps, Delta AttnRes, multi-head AttnRes at d768** (branch `ladderclimb_v1_batch14`)

This batch follows up [the qk_mult comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5848415944) and [the multi-head / Delta AttnRes comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5849538511).

**Step-count rule, adopted.** ML changes validated at d768–d1280 now use the baseline's step counts (d768 6928, d1024 9268, d1280 16667). I restarted gate 2 on that basis as `lc1-g2-d1024-bs` (9268 steps) and `lc1-g2-d1280-bs` (16667 steps), with checkpointing. The earlier attempts used throughput-scaled counts. MFU changes are measured separately in ex/s.

**Why qk_mult grows.** MuonH's hyperball step keeps each matrix at its initial Frobenius norm for the whole run. |W_q| and |W_uk| (|W_k| on KDA) never change, so the only way the model can sharpen q·k is the free scalar. The new `muon_free` group keeps MuonH's step size, `−lr·|W₀|·d/|d|` (`d` = the Newton–Schulz direction), but drops the re-projection and adds decoupled weight decay `−lr·wd·W`. With roughly orthogonal steps, the norm settles near `|W|²/|W₀|² ≈ lr/(2·wd)`. At d512 (lr 0.0214) the sweep `wd ∈ {0, 0.001, 0.003, 0.01}` spans an unbounded norm, about 3.3×, about 1.9× and about 1× the initial norm. It applies to `attn_q` and `attn_k` on both KDA and MLA. Learnable qk_mult stays on, so we can watch whether it stops growing. The best WD from d512 then goes to d768.

**Can the learnable KV-latent RMSNorm cover this?** Not cleanly, and your guess is right. On the MLA layers, K and V both come from `kv_latent_norm(x·W_dkv)`, so raising its gain scales K and V together. Sharper logits would therefore also scale the attention output relative to the other AttnRes sources, and that output gets no RMSNorm before the AttnRes mix. The gain is also elementwise and on Adam, so it could learn it in principle, but it has to trade logit sharpness against V magnitude. Q is full-rank and not normalized, and it is also held fixed by the hyperball. The KDA layers L2-normalize q and k, so there the scale is fixed by construction (× 1/√128).

**Delta Attention Residuals (arXiv 2605.18855).** Their sources are the per-sublayer outputs `v_i = h_{i+1} − h_i`. Those are exactly the sources our full AttnRes already uses (embedding + each attention and MoE output). Their "AttnRes" baseline attends over *cumulative* states, which is where I think the misunderstanding you mentioned comes in. The real change is **additive routing**: `input = h̄ + Σ softmax(w·RMSNorm(v_i))·v_i`, where `h̄` is the plain residual stream, with no final gate. I implemented it as `attn_res_additive` (plus `attn_res_final_mode=sum`):
- **Delta AttnRes:** full AttnRes + additive.
- **Delta Block:** our block AttnRes + additive. At d512 every layer is a block.

**V-gate heatmaps.** `attn_res_v_gate` under full AttnRes now applies to the **KDA layers only**, and the V gates' source weights are logged (`train/attn_res/w_g{2L+i}_*`). That lets me plot what V attends to next to what the Q/K gate reads.

**Multi-head AttnRes at d768** (6928 steps, paired against a d768 recipe baseline at the same steps):
- 4 heads
- 4 heads with the query LR at ×3 and ×1/3 (`attn_res_query_lr_scale` 0.3 / 0.03, default 0.1)
- 4 heads with a learnable **temperature** per gate and head, init 1. It is redundant with the query's norm, so it only changes the optimization dynamics.
- 4 heads with **per-head RMSNorm** for the key norm, instead of one RMS over all 512 channels

`d768-fixqk` isolates learnable qk_mult at d768: the same recipe with qk_mult fixed at 2.5.
