comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batches 190–201: candidate 12 (ragged a2a + 6 MLA heads), ragged and AttnRes speed probes, hyperball decay, and a raised final LR with an EMA sweep** (d512, cw-rno2a; [`0919fe4809`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0919fe4809) ragged port, [`1c43611fc7`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/1c43611fc7) `mla_num_heads`, [`89416d68b9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/89416d68b9) current)

FP8 is dropped (batch 189 stopped).

**Candidate 12** = candidate 11 + ragged all-to-all with the #9708 port (`ragp105`: one-shot transport, single process, capacity 1.05, drop renorm off) + `mla_num_heads=6` on the two MLA layers. Config: `base13`.

| run | seed 0 | seed 1 | mean | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pooled wave, candidate 11 (`ctrl`) | 2.9644 | 2.9667 | 2.9656 | 178.1 |
| ragged, before the port (`rag105`, batch 188) | 2.9633 | — | — | 193.6 |
| **ragged with the port (`ragp105`)** | 2.9610 | 2.9645 | 2.9628 | 182.7 |
| ragged + 6 MLA heads, equal steps (`mla6`) | 2.9538 | 2.9578 | 2.9558 | 190.6 |
| ragged + 6 MLA heads, 2705 steps (`mla6-ft`, equal time to `ragp105`) | 2.9619 | 2.9636 | 2.9628 | 190.3 |
| value-embed gate × learned scalar (`velam`, `value_embeds=gated_lambda`) | 2.9603 | 2.9656 | 2.9630 | 185.4 |

- **The #9708 port takes about 11 ms off ragged's step** (193.6 → 182.7 ms). Against pooled wave, ragged gains 0.003 per step and costs 2.6% step time.
- **6 MLA heads:** −0.0070 at equal steps on both seeds, for +4.2% step time; exactly break-even at equal time to `ragp105`. Kept for the smaller KV cache relative to the head count.
- **`gated_lambda` is neutral** (+0.0002).
- **Candidate 12 at fixed time** (candidate 11's budget, 2526 steps = 2698 × 177.9 / 190 ms): **2.9714 / 2.9750**, exactly candidate 11's 2.9715 / 2.9750. Ragged + 6 heads are a wash at fixed time; the gain is per step only. Candidate 11's numbers were measured on cw-us-east-02a, these on cw-rno2a.

**Ragged speed probes** (candidate 12, 400 steps, median step ms)

| probe | step ms |
|---|---|
| base (`one_shot`, 2 expert chunks, overlap limit 1) | 189.1 |
| collective overlap limit 4 (on `ragp105`) | 184.1 vs 184.9 |
| `device` transport | 200.7 |
| NCCL transport, multi-process | hung while compiling, 3 attempts |
| 1 expert chunk (`moe_ragged_chunks`) | 194.6 |
| 4 expert chunks | 190.8 |

- **Profile (`lc1-prof-ragp105` vs `lc1-prof-c11`):** ragged's step isn't heavier on the GPU (194 vs 195 ms of kernels per profiled step), and inside a step it waits less on the all-to-all (8 vs 15 ms).
  - The extra time is at the step boundary. Ragged needs one process driving all 8 GPUs, which doubles host dispatch (75 vs 38 ms per step).
  - The pad fusions I suspected aren't ragged's; they come from the AttnRes backward.
- **None of the cheap ragged settings help.** Two chunks stays.
- **AttnRes backward pads:** each gate read of a block's precomputed `[G, B, S]` logits, and of its softmax weights, became a pad back to full size in the backward, 290 of them in the HLO.
  - Per-row splits with a one-stack backward are bitwise identical in loss and gradients.
  - Neither step changes speed: 189.4 ms after each, against 189.1 ms. These small kernels are hidden behind other work, so AttnRes is closed as a speed lever. The changes stay, since they're exact.

**Hyperball decay per matrix** ([Hyperball Decay Atlas](https://claude.ai/artifact/74PcjNW2PaNkYV5btbq3Ug); `lc1-b191-hb2`, 2.9631; `--opt-set log_hyperball_decay=true`). The re-projection acts as a per-matrix weight decay, `1 − |W|/|W+u| ≈ lr·cos(W,u) + lr²/2`.
- **Typical matrices:** 0.06–0.10%/step mid-run with cos ≈ 0.07–0.10. Over 90% of the decay comes from updates leaning outward; the orthogonal part contributes almost none.
- **KDA `w_beta`:** decays 2–3× more than any other matrix, with 4× the rescale and swings inward.
- **AdamH lm head:** the largest spikes (p99 1.27%/step, cos up to 0.66).
- **Layer-5 MLA:** `w_o` spikes too, and `w_uv` takes inward steps.
- **Gated-norm matrices:** the highest sustained decay after `w_beta`, rising with depth.

**Batch 199: final LR 0.1 + EMA sweep** (candidate 12, 2817 steps, seed 0; each run also scores the raw final weights and a 50/50 EMA/final blend)

| run | min LR ratio | EMA β / last N | EMA | raw final | 50/50 blend |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ctrl` | 0.05 | 0.995 / 1000 | 2.9535 | 2.9569 | **2.9514** |
| `f10` | 0.1 | 0.995 / 1000 | 2.9543 | 2.9694 | 2.9542 |
| `f10-b99` | 0.1 | 0.99 / 1000 | 2.9561 | 2.9677 | 2.9570 |
| `f10-b998` | 0.1 | 0.998 / 1000 | 2.9584 | 2.9703 | **2.9512** |
| `f10-w500` | 0.1 | 0.995 / 500 | 2.9572 | 2.9720 | 2.9570 |
| `f10-w1500` | 0.1 | 0.995 / 1500 | 2.9556 | 2.9703 | 2.9554 |
| `f10-b998w1500` | 0.1 | 0.998 / 1500 | 2.9605 | 2.9709 | 2.9524 |

- **The 0.1 floor doesn't pay.** Its raw final weights are +0.0125 worse. The best EMA setting on it (β 0.998, 50/50 blend, 2.9512) only ties the 0.05 floor's blend (2.9514).
- **The 50/50 blend helps at the current floor:** −0.0021 against the pure EMA we report now (2.9514 vs 2.9535), on the same trained weights. It needs a second seed before adopting `--ema-blend 0.5` as the reported model.

**Batch 201: `w_beta` sweep** (candidate 12, 2817 steps, seed 0; hyperball logging on every run). Knobs from [`c2317eab2c`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2317eab2c): `init_std_mult_beta`, `kda_beta_scale`, `kda_beta_group`.

| run | Paloma | Δ vs `ctrl` | `w_beta` L0 cos, steps 5–100 / median | L0 decay median |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ctrl` (init ×2, MuonH 2× LR) | 2.9539 | — | 0.25 / 0.084 | 0.15% |
| init ×1 | 2.9529 | −0.0010 | 0.33 / 0.040 | 0.07% |
| init ×4 | 2.9551 | +0.0012 | 0.18 / 0.147 | 0.27% |
| init ×8 | 2.9571 | +0.0032 | 0.19 / 0.190 | 0.36% |
| LR mult 1 | 2.9547 | +0.0008 | — | — |
| LR mult 4 | 2.9534 | −0.0005 | 0.40 / 0.202 | 0.76% |
| learned per-head beta scale | 2.9543 | +0.0004 | 0.25 / 0.164 | 0.29% |
| AdamH | 2.9574 | +0.0035 | 0.02 / −0.020 | ~0 |
| Adam (norm free) | 2.9560 | +0.0021 | — | — |

- **Everything is within noise (0.0056),** but init shows a monotonic trend: ×1 −0.0010, ×2 0, ×4 +0.0012, ×8 +0.0032. `w_beta` doesn't want a bigger sphere.
- **The outward lean is Muon's, not the loss's.**
  - Given a free per-head scale on the logits, the model shrinks it to about 0.8× (median 0.81, 0.90 at the end), while MuonH keeps pushing `w_beta` outward (cos 0.16).
  - Under AdamH the cos is ≈ 0 and the decay vanishes.
  - So the large decay comes from the orthogonalized update of a 512×4 matrix leaning along W, and the projection simply cancels it. It isn't fighting a model that wants larger beta logits.
- **Plain Adam lets the norm drift 4×** (1.98 → 7.85), with no gain.
- Nothing to adopt. If anything, init ×1 is worth a second seed.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batches 203 (GDLA) and df1: differential attention, take two** (candidate 12 = `base14`, d512, 2817 equal steps, seed 0; [`b31b63ac62`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/b31b63ac62) GDLA, [`d304c417c7`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/d304c417c7) mean noise; branch `ladderclimb_v1_diffattn`)

**Summary so far: candidate 13 proposal.** Candidate 12 + KDA state reshaped to 4 heads × (64 key × 256 value), with the faster state-pass tiling:

`--model-set kda_key_dim=64 --model-set kda_value_dim=256 --model-set kda_state_block_v=64` ([`acec39b84f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/acec39b84f), branch `ladderclimb_v1_diffattn`)

**df21: fixed-time confirmation** (cw-us-east-02a; with `block_v=64` the reshaped model runs at candidate 12's speed, so equal steps is equal time)

| run | steps | seed 0 | seed 1 | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| candidate 12 (`block_v` 64) | 2817 | 2.9532 (2.9543 in df1) | 2.9584 (df4) | 191.3 |
| **4 × (64 × 256)** | 2817 | **2.9482** | **2.9489** | 191.0–191.7 |
| 8 × (64 × 128), fixed time | 2754 | 2.9485 | 2.9512 | 194.4 |

- **4 × (64 × 256): −0.0056 / −0.0095 at fixed time (mean ≈ −0.0075),** with no step-time cost.
  - Earlier two-seed equal-step runs gave −0.0067.
  - d768 gave −0.0064 at equal steps (6929 steps).
  - The state size per head is unchanged: 64 × 256 = 16,384 entries, the same as 128 × 128.
  - The q/k (and erase) projections halve, while v/o and the per-channel output and write gates double. Net, about +0.65M parameters per KDA layer at d512.
- **8 × (64 × 128) at fixed time: −0.0062,** a little behind and +2% step time.
- **16 × (64 × 64)** has the largest per-step gain (−0.0146) but needs a prep kernel that packs several small heads per program (+8.6% step today). That's the next kernel project if you want it.

---

**More, narrower KDA heads; d768; a free KDA kernel speedup** ([`acec39b84f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/acec39b84f))

**Head layout at the same total KDA state** (d512, 2817 equal steps; controls 2.9543 / 2.9584)

| KDA heads × (key × value) | seed 0 | seed 1 | mean Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 × (64 × 256) | 2.9500 | 2.9493 | −0.0067 |
| 8 × (64 × 128) | 2.9439 | 2.9485 | −0.0102 |
| 8 × (64 × 128), chunk 64 | 2.9453 | 2.9476 | −0.0099 |
| 16 × (64 × 64) | 2.9397 | — | **−0.0146** |
| 4 × (64 × 256) + MLA and KDA content gates | 2.9460 | 2.9476 | −0.0096 |

- **At the same total state, more independent narrow states keep helping:** 4 → 8 → 16 heads gives −0.007 → −0.010 → −0.015 per step.
- **The KDA content gate isn't additive** on top of 64 × 256 + the MLA gate.

**d768** (6929 steps, cw-rno2a, MLA heads left at the d768 default in both arms): 4 × (64 × 256) gives **2.7143 vs 2.7207 (−0.0064)**. That's the same per-step gain as at d512 (−0.0067); step time +1.9% before the kernel change below.

**Why many small heads were slow, and the fix.**
- The KDA state pass runs one sequential program per (sequence × head, `d_v` slab), and the slab was fixed at 32.
- With more heads, there are more of these latency-bound programs, each doing less work per step.
- **`kda_state_block_v=64`** (new `state_block_v` argument of `kda_fused`) halves the program count. It's exact, since it only changes the tiling; the kernel tests pass at 32 vs 64 for both state-grad paths.
- Per-layer KDA forward+backward on one H100 (prep + state pass):

| layout | `block_v` 32 | `block_v` 64 |
|---|---|---|
| 4 × 128 × 128 (candidate 12) | 2.21 + 2.14 | 2.21 + 2.07 |
| 4 × 64 × 256 | 1.82 + 2.92 | 1.82 + 2.28 |
| 8 × 64 × 128 | 2.32 + 3.11 | 2.32 + 2.42 |
| 16 × 64 × 64 | 4.08 + 3.21 | 4.08 + 2.53 |

- Full-step timing probes (400 steps, same cluster and session):

| config | step ms |
|---|---|
| candidate 12, `block_v` 32 | 190.9 |
| candidate 12, `block_v` 64 | 190.7 |
| 4 × (64 × 256), `block_v` 64 | **190.1 (no cost)** |
| 8 × (64 × 128), `block_v` 64 | 195.2 (+2.3%) |
| 16 × (64 × 64), `block_v` 64 | 207.4 (+8.6%) |

- **The 4 × (64 × 256) shape is now free.** Its −0.0067 per-step gain should hold at fixed time. Two seeds at 2817 steps with `block_v=64` and a same-run control are running to confirm.
  - 8 heads is now about −0.006 at fixed time and is running at its fixed-time step count (2755).
  - 16 heads is still held back by the intra-chunk prep kernels (4.1 vs 2.2 ms), whose per-program work shrinks with the head width. Packing several heads per prep program is the next kernel lever, worth up to about −0.015 per step if it reached 4-head speed.

---

**df14–df17 results** (cw-us-east-02a; controls 2.9543 / 2.9584 at 2817 steps, about 190 ms)

| run | change | steps | seed 0 | seed 1 | mean Δ | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hgate` | MLA H-gate, rank 32 | 2817 | 2.9511 | 2.9563 | −0.0027 | 191.5 |
| `kdahg` | the same content gate on the KDA output gate ([`393d68cfa8`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/393d68cfa8)) | 2817 | 2.9515 | 2.9551 | −0.0031 | 192.2 |
| `kv-hg` | KDA 64 × 256 + MLA H-gate | 2817 | 2.9466 | 2.9480 | −0.0090 | 195.9 |
| `h8` | **8 KDA heads × (64 × 128)** | 2817 | **2.9439** | **2.9485** | **−0.0102** | 198.0 |
| `h8-ft` | the same at fixed time | 2704 | 2.9527 | 2.9540 | −0.0030 | 198.8 |
| `kv-ft` | 4 KDA heads × (64 × 256) at fixed time | 2766 | 2.9519 | 2.9532 | −0.0038 | 194.4 |

- **Content-conditioned output gates replicate in both mixers.**
  - The gate logits gain a rank-32 term read from what the head retrieved: −0.0027 on MLA and −0.0031 on KDA, both seeds negative.
  - Each costs about 1% step time, so each nets about −0.001 at fixed time.
- **8 KDA heads × (64 × 128) is the best per-step result:** −0.0102 on two seeds.
  - It has the same total state and the same q/k and v/o widths as 4 × (64 × 256). The extra gain comes from more independent states, each with its own β and decays.
  - Its kernel cost (+4.4%) leaves it tied with 4 × (64 × 256) at fixed time (−0.0030 vs −0.0038). If the 8-head kernel ran at the 4-head cost, it would be the better shape.
- **Running:**
  - All three stacked (64 × 256 + MLA and KDA content gates), two seeds.
  - 16 KDA heads × (64 × 64).
  - The d768 pair for 64 × 256.

---

**Why 32 × 512 is slow, and HyGA gates** (cw-us-east-02a)

KDA fused forward+backward on one H100, at the per-GPU d512 shape (B = 16, S = 4096, 4 heads; erase gate, Pallas state grads):

| state | chunk 32 | chunk 16 |
|---|---|---|
| 128 × 128 (candidate 12) | 4.5 ms | — |
| 64 × 256 | 4.7 ms | 5.5 ms |
| 32 × 256 | 6.0 ms | — |
| 64 × 512 | 12.1 ms | 9.5 ms |
| 32 × 512 | 31.9 ms | 7.8 ms |

- **The forward is fine at every shape:** 2.2 ms at 32 × 512 vs 1.6 ms at 64 × 256.
- **The backward degrades** as values widen past 256 (about 2.6×) and as keys narrow to 32 (about 1.3×), and the two compound.
  - The prep backward holds whole `C × d_v` fp32 value tiles per chunk, which very likely spills at `d_v` = 512.
  - Chunk 16 halves those tiles and recovers most of the loss.
- **Even so, 32 × 512 costs about +3 ms per KDA layer over 64 × 256** (+8% step), which outweighs its extra −0.004 per step at fixed time.
  - A fully tuned kernel would at best tie 64 × 256 at fixed time, so I'm not spending kernel work on it.
  - **64 × 256 at chunk 32 is the shape to keep.**

**HyGA gates on MLA** ([arXiv 2608.11805](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11805), [`2629cbe0d4`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/2629cbe0d4); seed 0, control 2.9543)

| run | gate | Paloma | Δ | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `df12-hgate` | H-gate: `SiLU(H_i W_d) W_u` (rank 32) added to the output gate's logits, read from the head's own attention output | 2.9511 | −0.0032 | 191.8 |
| `df12-cgate` | C-gate: per-head `2σ((H W_c)_i)` from all heads' outputs | 2.9540 | −0.0003 | 192.5 |
| `df12-hyga` | both | 2.9534 | −0.0009 | 191.6 |

- Our existing output gates read `x`. HyGA's **H-gate reads the attention output itself** (what the head retrieved), which no earlier gate variant did.
- −0.0032 is within one-seed noise. Seed 1 is running, along with the stack on `k64v256` (two seeds).
- **Also running:** 8 KDA heads × (64 × 128). It has the same total state and the same q/k and v/o widths as 4 × (64 × 256), so it separates head count from per-head value width. The d768 pair (candidate 12 vs `k64v256`, 6929 steps) is on cw-rno2a.

---

**df9 / df10 results: the KDA state shape** (cw-us-east-02a; controls 2.9543 / 2.9584 at 2817 steps, about 190 ms)

| run | state (key × value) | steps | seed 0 | seed 1 | mean Δ | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k64v256`, equal steps | 64 × 256 | 2817 | 2.9500 | 2.9493 | −0.0067 | 193.3 |
| **`k64v256`, fixed time** | 64 × 256 | 2766 | **2.9519** | **2.9532** | **−0.0038** | 194.4 |
| `k32v512`, equal steps | 32 × 512 | 2817 | 2.9446 | 2.9467 | **−0.0107** | 270 (+42%) |
| `k128v256` (2× state, diagnostic) | 128 × 256 | 2817 | 2.9473 | — | −0.0070 | 206.4 (+8.7%) |

- **`k64v256` wins at fixed time on both seeds: −0.0024 / −0.0052.**
  - It changes only the KDA layers' key/value widths (`--model-set kda_key_dim=64 --model-set kda_value_dim=256`).
  - The state size is unchanged. The q/k projections halve and the v/o projections double.
- **Value width is what pays.** Narrowing the keys further to widen the values (32 × 512) gains −0.0107 per step, on both seeds. Doubling the state at 256-wide values (`k128v256`) gains less than 32 × 512 does at the original state size.
- **32 × 512 is held back only by speed.** The fused KDA kernels run +42% slower at that shape. A kernel microbenchmark across shapes is running to find which pass is slow; if it's a tiling problem, 32 × 512 could be worth about −0.008 at fixed time.

**Kalman write strength: parked.**
- Every attempt hit a NaN loss between steps 4 and 31, on both seeds and with either optimizer for the projection.
- A debug run shows why: at step 10 the gradient norm of KDA layer 2's `kalman_b` was **5e18**, with every other gradient below 0.4. Its square overflows fp32 in the global-norm clip, and the loss turns NaN a few steps later.
- The scan itself is not the source. On CPU at 4096 tokens its forward and gradients are finite and O(1) for decays 0.5–0.999 and extreme `ω`/`r`.
- So the blow-up arrives through the kernel's `β` cotangent, on tokens where the Kalman β departs from the sigmoid's narrow range. Finding them needs kernel-level instrumentation; I'm not chasing that further now.

---

**df6–df8 results** (cw-us-east-02a, 2817 steps; controls 2.9543 (seed 0) / 2.9584 (seed 1), about 190 ms)

| run | change | seed 0 | seed 1 | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `df6-fts` | per-token logit temperature `2σ(ĥ·w)` on the lm_head input | 2.9554 (+0.0011) | 2.9577 (−0.0007) | 192.5 |
| `k64v256` (df5 / df7) | KDA state 64 × 256, 4 heads | **2.9500 (−0.0043)** | **2.9493 (−0.0091)** | 193.3 (+1.7%) |
| `df7-k32v512` | KDA state 32 × 512 | 2.9446 (−0.0097) | — | 268.7 (+41%) |
| `df8-h2k128v256` | 2 KDA heads × (128 × 256), same total state | 2.9640 (+0.0097) | — | 187.7 |
| `df8-h2k64v512` | 2 KDA heads × (64 × 512), half the state | 2.9593 (+0.0050) | — | 194.3 |

- **KDA keys 64 × values 256 replicates: −0.0067 mean over two seeds at equal steps.** At +1.7% step time that nets about −0.004 at fixed time.
  - **Wider still (32 × 512) keeps gaining** (−0.0097), but the KDA kernels run far slower at `d_k` = 32. A kernel tile tuned for 32-wide keys might recover this.
  - **The heads matter too:** 2 wider heads at the same total state lose (+0.010 / +0.005).
  - The best shape so far is 4 heads, each with a narrow key address and a wide value.
- **The per-token output temperature is neutral** (mean +0.0002), as the removed final GatedNorm was in batch 10. Closed.
- **df9 (running):**
  - `k64v256` at fixed time: 2766 steps = 2817 × 189.8 / 193.3, two seeds.
  - `k128v256`: values 256 with keys left at 128. This doubles the state; it's a diagnostic of state size vs value width, not a candidate.
  - **Kalman write strength** (`kda_kalman_beta`, [arXiv 2609.07816](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07816), [`9ac96e5826`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/9ac96e5826)), two seeds.
    - Each KDA head tracks a scalar memory uncertainty, `b̂ₜ = aₜ bₜ₋₁ + ωₜ` with `bₜ = rₜ b̂ₜ / (rₜ + b̂ₜ)`, and writes with `βₜ = b̂ₜ / (rₜ + b̂ₜ)` in place of `σ(x W_β)`.
    - So a head writes hard while its memory is uncertain and softly once it has absorbed evidence.
    - `ω` and `r` are per-token softplus projections. The recursion is a Möbius map, run as one associative scan of 2 × 2 matrices before the KDA kernel.

---

**df5 results: KDA state shape at fixed size** (cw-us-east-02a, 2817 steps; controls `df1-ctrl` 2.9543 (seed 0, 189.8 ms) and `df4-ctrl-s1` 2.9584 (seed 1, 190.4 ms))

| run | per-head state (key × value) | Paloma | Δ vs seed 0 | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k64v256` | 64 × 256 | **2.9500** | **−0.0043** | 193.1 (+1.7%) |
| `k256v64` | 256 × 64 | 2.9645 | +0.0102 | 227.9 (+20%) |

- **Wider values with narrower keys help, and the reverse hurts.**
  - This matches batch 203's MLA finding, where loss tracked value capacity.
  - The KDA state reads back 256-wide values per head from 64-dim key addresses, with the state size unchanged.
- **Cost:** the v/o projections double (n·256 wide) while q/k halve, so +1.7% step time. That nets about −0.0014 at fixed time, inside noise for one seed.
- **Running (df7):**
  - `k64v256` seed 1.
  - `k32v512`: the same state with even wider values.
  - `k96v192`: a milder reshape (state +12%).

---

**df2 / df3 results** (cw-rno2a, 2817 steps, seed 0; control `df2-ctrl` 2.9542 at 189.7 ms)

| run | change | Paloma | Δ | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `df2-g12n6l01` | GDLA 6 × (1 + 1), λ starts at 0.1 | 2.9543 | +0.0001 | 207.1 |
| `df2-g9n3l01` | GDLA 3 × (2 + 1), λ starts at 0.1 | 2.9539 | −0.0003 | 199.1 |
| `df2-g8n2l01` | GDLA 2 × (3 + 1), λ starts at 0.1 | 2.9603 | +0.0061 | 194.9 |
| `df3-h12x64` | MLA 12 heads × 64 | 2.9557 | +0.0015 | 302.1 |
| `df3-h12x64q` | 12 × 64, `qk_mult` × √2 | 2.9547 | +0.0005 | 302.8 |
| `df3-h8x96` | 8 × 96 | 2.9540 | −0.0002 | 257.6 |

- **The low λ start removes batch 203's small penalty** (`g9n3`: +0.0019 → −0.0003), but there's still no gain. With 2 value heads (`g8n2`) it still loses.
- **Differential attention is closed on this model.** Every variant lands between neutral and worse:
  - Motif's GDLA inside the head budget, plus three larger head counts.
  - DIFF-style pairs.
  - A free mean-value noise map.
  - Two λ starts.
- **Likely reason:** the MLA layers already have the tools DIFF supplies.
  - The ×2-sigmoid output gate can switch a head's read off per token, which is the gated-attention fix for attention sinks.
  - XSA removes the self-value component, and q/k norms with a learned temperature keep maps sharp.
  - λ always collapses early, i.e. at first the model pushes the subtraction out of the way.
- **More, narrower heads at equal FLOPs don't help at equal steps either,** and FA4 runs 64- and 96-dim heads far slower here (+59% / +36% step).
  - So the 4 → 6 head gain was capacity, not head count.
  - Closed.

---

**Follow-ups running** (d512, 2817 equal steps, seed 0)

- **df2 (rno2a, own control `df2-ctrl`): GDLA with λ starting at 0.1** (`mla_diff_lambda_init=0.1`, a learned per-head bias) on `g12n6`, `g9n3` and `g8n2`. λ dropped from 0.5 to about 0.1 early in every batch 203 and df1 run.
- **df3 (rno2a): more, narrower MLA heads at equal attention FLOPs** (`mla_head_dim`, [`911452ce68`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/911452ce68)).
  - *Source:* batch 203 shows the global layers' loss tracking their number of value heads, and 4 → 6 heads gave −0.007 (batch 192).
  - The arms trade head width for head count at the same q/k/v/o parameters and attention FLOPs:
    - `h12x64`: 12 × 64 instead of 6 × 128.
    - `h12x64q`: the same with `qk_mult` × √2. Halving the head dim shrinks the normalized q·k/√d logits by √2.
    - `h8x96`: 8 × 96.
  - The KV latent stays at 512.
- **df5 (cw-us-east-02a; controls `df1-ctrl` and `df4-ctrl-s1`): the KDA state's shape at fixed size** (`kda_key_dim` / `kda_value_dim`, [`9abaa83612`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/9abaa83612)).
  - Each KDA head's 128 × 128 delta-rule state is reshaped to 64 × 256 (wider values, as Gated DeltaNet's `expand_v`) or 256 × 64 (wider keys).
  - State size per head is unchanged. The q/k vs v/o projections trade width.

---

**Batch df1 results** (cw-us-east-02a, 2817 steps, seed 0; control `df1-ctrl` 2.9543 at 189.8 ms)

| run | noise map | Paloma | Δ | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mu` | uniform prefix mean | 2.9554 | +0.0011 | 194.3 |
| `md16` | decayed mean, half-life 16 at init | 2.9565 | +0.0022 | 195.3 |
| `md64` | half-life 64 | 2.9564 | +0.0021 | 194.7 |
| `md256` | half-life 256 | 2.9554 | +0.0011 | 195.0 |

- **No gain anywhere, and the scan costs about 2.5% of step time.**
- **λ follows the GDLA pattern:** it drops from 0.5 to 0.03–0.16 in the first fifth of training, then settles at about 0.21 (layer 3) and 0.15 (layer 5).
- **The learned decays split by head:**
  - Some heads go to a half-life of about 2.5 tokens, i.e. subtracting the last couple of values.
  - Others go to thousands of tokens, i.e. the uniform mean.
  - The model uses a small common-mode subtraction, but it buys no loss.
- **Closed.** The λ-init question is tested on GDLA in df2.

---

**Batch 203 results** (Paloma macro loss, 2817 steps, seed 0, cw-rno2a. Candidate 12 controls on rno2a: 2.9529 (`b201-binit1`) / 2.9539 (`b202-ctrl`), mean 2.9534, about 194 ms per step with hyperball logging on.)

| run | signal + noise heads | value heads | Paloma | Δ vs 2.9534 | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `g6n1eg` | 5 + 1 | 1 | 2.9697 | **+0.0163** | 190.6 |
| `g6n2eg` | 2 × (2 + 1) | 2 | 2.9625 | +0.0091 | 189.1 |
| `g8n2eg` | 2 × (3 + 1) | 2 | 2.9577 | +0.0043 | 196.9 |
| `g8n2` (per-head gate) | 2 × (3 + 1) | 2 | 2.9590 | +0.0056 | 193.0 |
| `g9n3eg` | 3 × (2 + 1) | 3 | 2.9553 | +0.0019 | 199.3 |
| `g12n6eg` | 6 × (1 + 1) | 6 | 2.9527 | −0.0007 | 207.1 (+7%) |
| `eg` (elementwise gate, no differential) | 6 | 6 | 2.9545 | +0.0011 | 192.0 |

**Reading.**
- **The loss tracks the number of value heads, not the subtraction.** 1 value head: +0.016. 2: +0.004 to +0.009. 3: +0.002. 6: 0.
  - Inside the head budget, GDLA costs the global layers their value capacity. That costs far more than the noise cancellation returns.
  - With values intact (`g12n6eg`, DIFF-style pairs), the subtraction is neutral (−0.0007) and the extra heads cost +7% step time.
- **The elementwise output gate alone is neutral** (+0.0011), as in batch 163.
- **What λ learned** (mean over tokens and heads, at 0 / 20 / 40 / 60 / 80 / 100% of training):

  | run | layer 3 | layer 5 |
  |---|---|---|
  | `g12n6eg` | 0.50 → 0.09 → 0.35 → 0.40 → 0.44 → 0.45 | 0.50 → 0.12 → 0.12 → 0.17 → 0.21 → 0.24 |
  | `g9n3eg` | 0.50 → 0.15 → 0.28 → 0.33 → 0.37 → 0.39 | 0.50 → 0.12 → 0.14 → 0.17 → 0.21 → 0.25 |
  | `g6n1eg` | 0.50 → 0.22 → 0.31 → 0.37 → 0.40 → 0.41 | 0.50 → 0.26 → 0.19 → 0.21 → 0.25 → 0.28 |

  - The noise read is as large as the signal read: RMS ratio 0.93 at layer 3 and 1.00 at layer 5 in `g12n6eg`.
  - So the model does use the subtraction late in training. But it first throws λ down from 0.5 to about 0.1: the start is too strong.
- **Next (df2):** a learned λ bias starting at 0.1 (`mla_diff_lambda_init=0.1`) on `g12n6`, `g9n3` and `g8n2`, against a fresh control.
- To pay at fixed time, `g12n6` needs about −0.012 at equal steps (+7% step time).

---


Note: another agent is also running a batch 203 (`badam*`). My differential-attention batches from here on use the `lc1-df<N>-` prefix.

**Why the batch 163 version lost.**
- Batch 163 got −0.003 / −0.004 at equal steps but cost +6.6% step time.
- It added its noise maps on top of the signal heads, as a second full attention call.
- It also tiled each shared noise map out to all `g` heads of its group, so each map was computed `g` times.
- Motif 3's GDLA ([arXiv 2608.09119](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09119)) does neither:
  - The noise heads come out of the head budget: 80 query heads = 64 signal + 16 noise.
  - Each group's signal and noise heads share one KV head, and only the query differs.
  - Its attention kernel therefore runs no extra heads.

**Batch 203: GDLA inside the head budget** (`mla_gdla_noise_heads=m`, MLA layers 3 and 5)
- The `N` query heads form `m` groups of `g` signal heads plus 1 noise head, and run in one kernel call.
- Each group shares one value head, so `w_uv` and the value embeds have `m` heads. Keys stay per head, since MLA up-projections are cheap.
- The output is `D = H_signal − λ·H_noise(group)`, with `λ = sigmoid(x W_λ)` per signal head and token (zero-init, so 0.5).
- Only the signal heads reach `w_o`.

| run | heads (signal + noise) | value heads | output gate | attention cost vs candidate 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `g6n2eg` | 6 = 2 × (2 + 1) | 2 | elementwise (Motif) | same |
| `g6n1eg` | 6 = 5 + 1 | 1 | elementwise | same |
| `g8n2eg` | 8 = 2 × (3 + 1) | 2 | elementwise | +2 heads |
| `g9n3eg` | 9 = 3 × (2 + 1) | 3 | elementwise | +3 heads |
| `g12n6eg` | 12 = 6 × (1 + 1), i.e. DIFF pairs | 6 (no value loss) | elementwise | ×2 |
| `g8n2` | 8 = 2 × (3 + 1) | 2 | per head (ours) | +2 heads |
| `eg` | 6, no differential | 6 | elementwise | control for the gate |

The `g6` arms test whether the noise subtraction is worth giving up signal heads and value heads at no extra cost. `g12n6eg` tests whether it helps when nothing else is taken away.

**Batch df1: differential attention with a free noise map** (original idea; on cw-us-east-02a with its own control)
- *Source:* DIFF's noise map is meant to cancel common-mode attention, the broad mass a softmax spreads over irrelevant context. The cheapest estimate of that common mode is a fixed average of the values, so no second softmax map is needed.
- *Mechanism:* `D = softmax(qkᵀ)v − λ·mean_{j≤t}(v_j)` per head, within documents, with the same token-dependent sigmoid `λ`. Cost is one segment-reset scan, with no extra kernel call.
- *Variants:*
  - `uniform`: the plain prefix mean.
  - `decay`: an exponentially decayed mean with a learned per-head decay, half-life 16 / 64 / 256 at init. This makes the noise map a local/recent baseline.
- *Logged:* `knob_mean_noise_lambda_mean` and the learned half-lives per layer.

| run | noise map |
|---|---|
| `df1-ctrl` | none (cw-us-east-02a control) |
| `df1-mu` | uniform prefix mean |
| `df1-md16` / `md64` / `md256` | decayed mean, initial half-life 16 / 64 / 256 |

Results will be edited in here.

comments.body:
🤖 **Batches 202–205: hyperball step size, `w_beta` on Adam, Adam warmup, cheap MTP** (d512, 2817 equal steps, seed 0, cw-rno2a; [`587e7e2cbe`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/587e7e2cbe), [`1df62e45f0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/1df62e45f0), [`ac5560b321`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ac5560b321), [`d642ff8db7`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/d642ff8db7))

**Base changes**
- **`w_beta` init back to ×1** (`init_std_mult_beta=1`): batch 201 gave −0.0010 (noise), and ×1 is simpler. `w_g` stays at ×2. → `base14`.
- **`w_beta` on plain Adam at 1× the Adam LR** (`kda_beta_group=adam`): 2.9540, against base14's 2.9529 / 2.9539. → **`base15`** (control `lc1-b205-ctrl`: 2.9521).
  - Adam LR sweep on `w_beta`: 0.1× 2.9538, 0.3× 2.9538, 1× 2.9540, 3× 2.9526. It doesn't care about its LR.

**Batch 202/204: hyperball with fixed norms but free step size** (`muonh_step`; base14 + hyperball logging, control 2.9539)

| mode | run | Paloma | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| spectral, Muon's own step size (`lr·α·√max(1, fan_out/fan_in)·d`) | α 0.25 / 0.5 / 1 | 2.9705 / 2.9684 / 3.0080 | +0.017 / +0.015 / +0.054 |
| grad, step ∝ smoothed gradient norm over its early mean | reference over the first 100 / 500 steps | 2.9913 / 2.9607 | +0.037 / +0.0068 |

- **Spectral:** at α 0.5 the relative step per matrix is `w_q` 1.0×, `w_o` 0.85×, `w_g` 0.51× (its ×2 init) and routed experts 1.8×.
- **Grad:** expert gradients grow over training while attention gradients shrink. The step multiplier ends at 2.3× for routed `w_up` and 0.4× for `w_q` and `w_o`.
  - The first grad version keyed on the momentum norm, which drops 10–70× at the Bi-Maxwell rail switch around step 1000, so that version (+0.12) was a bug.
- **MuonH's equal relative step for every matrix beats both alternatives.** Closed.

**Batch 203: longer Adam warmup with a higher Adam peak** (base14; today's Adam warmup is 1% = 28 steps at peak 0.00495, which averages 2.9534)

| Adam warmup | peak ×1 | ×1.5 | ×2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.5% | 2.9568 | 2.9527 | 2.9569 |
| 10% | 2.9586 | 2.9575 | 2.9613 |

A longer warmup hurts at the same peak, and a higher peak only wins back what it costs. Nothing to adopt.

**Batch 205: cheap MTP** (`future_aux`; base15, control 2.9521 at 190.9 ms)

| head | weight | Paloma | Δ | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16k-bucket hash of t+2 | 0.05 | 2.9557 | +0.0036 | 205.9 |
| hash of the (t+1, t+2) bigram | 0.05 | 2.9595 | +0.0074 | 204.6 |
| hash of the (t+1…t+3) trigram | 0.05 | 2.9561 | +0.0040 | 203.2 |
| t+2 hash through a 128-wide bottleneck | 0.05 | 2.9539 | +0.0018 | 198.0 |
| cosine regression on the mean embedding of t+2, t+3 | 0.05 | 2.9532 | +0.0011 | 190.2 |
| bigram hash, decaying to 0 at mid-run | 0.1 | 2.9546 | +0.0025 | 203.7 |
| bigram hash, decaying to 0 at the end | 0.05 | 2.9528 | +0.0007 | 203.6 |

- **Every future-prediction objective costs main-loss quality at d512, at 1× tokens.** The more of the future it targets, the more it costs. Decaying the weight to 0 gets back to neutral, but it doesn't turn positive.
- **The 16k-bucket hash heads aren't cheap:** +7% step time from the fused CE and AdamH on a 512×16k head. The embedding regression is free.
- **This matches both full-MTP attempts (batches 18, 163).** At this scale and token count, MTP takes capacity rather than adding signal. Closed at d512. It would only be worth retrying where the model has spare capacity: at larger rungs, or in the overtrained regime.

issues.body:
The weekly fork-migration system from #8048 is in place: a refresh-fork skill and
per-fork descriptors (#8068, #8117), a weekly ferry coordinator (#8245) with Loom
federation (#8284), and automated re-pinning for the vLLM GPU wheel (#8292). The TPU
vLLM stack refreshed to tpu-inference v0.26.0 (#8207) on top of the externalized
stack (#8063), and the GPU wheel now discovers its `_C` extension by shape across the
CUDA 13 / stable-ABI boundary (#8250). This issue tracks the work that remains after
that rollout, and is the canonical fork-migration tracker going forward. It supersedes
#8048 and folds in the refresh trackers #8298, #7097, #7143, and #6480.

1. Promote the Harbor one-time catch-up. marin-community/harbor#73 re-ports the fork
   overlay onto current upstream and folds the standalone `harbor-config` package into
   `harbor.models`. It is mergeable with `marin-precommit`, `marin-style-sync`, and
   `tests` green. Two steps need an admin/reviewer: drop the retired `harbor-config`
   context from the fork `main` branch protection (it no longer reports, so it blocks
   the merge), then review and merge, and promote the caught-up tree to protected
   `main`. Done when fork `main` carries the caught-up overlay and its protection no
   longer requires `harbor-config`.

2. Bump the Marin Harbor pin. After harbor#73 lands, re-pin `config/external/harbor`
   to the landed `main` SHA, migrate the `harbor_config.*` imports in
   `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py` to `harbor.models.*`, and
   keep the migration.toml [harbor] nuances. The aime-smoke e2e already passed
   end-to-end against the catch-up branch on qwen3-0.6b. Closes out the blocker path
   #8298.

3. Migrate MarinSkyRL as a managed Harbor consumer (#7920). The SkyRL fork depends on
   `harbor[analysis,datasets,daytona]` floating on `main` plus the standalone
   `harbor-config` wheel, so the harbor.models fold in harbor#73 breaks any SkyRL
   relock. Pin harbor to an explicit immutable ref, migrate off `harbor-config` to
   `harbor.models`, and give SkyRL a Marin-style update-external plus one terminal-bench
   e2e. Cadence stays decoupled and coordinated on breaking changes rather than weekly
   lockstep. Tracked under #7920.

4. Make the ferry's evalchemy leg observable. The weekly run produced no PR and filed
   no blocker for evalchemy. Confirm whether that is a legitimate no-op (the fork
   already matches upstream `main`) or a silent failure, and have the leg emit an
   explicit no-op summary either way.

5. Publish prebuilt TPU vLLM fork wheels (#7143). Cold TPU jobs still source-build the
   `vllm` and `tpu-inference` forks; a Marin-controlled index would let serve, eval,
   and RL install a pinned wheel. Standalone spec in #7143.

6. Resolve the Marin-owned pin audit (#6480). Decide whether Levanter can move to a
   Transformers 5 range and drop the tpu-inference Gemma4 guard, and keep the
   JAX/libtpu/torch/torchvision alignment documented against the fork stack. The
   descriptor records these as nuances; the decision is open. Spec in #6480.

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
A TaskCompendium grade cannot say that the task itself is broken, and it drops the evidence the verifier produced. `verifyit` returns a `Reward` with `status` (`scored`, `invalid_task`, `infra_error`) and a JSON `detail` object. `taskcompendium.grading.grade_answer` keeps only `Reward.reward`. A task whose own grading contract is inconsistent (a reference that fails its own verifier, a malformed rubric, a missing private file) is therefore reported as `infra_error` or as an exception. Callers treat both as transient and retry. A partial-credit grade also loses its per-criterion results, so a caller cannot check which criteria passed.

Today, on `origin/main`:

- `lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/grading.py`: `Outcome` is `graded | extraction_error | infra_error`. `GradeResult` is `status, reward, error`. `grade_answer` returns `GradeResult(Outcome.GRADED, grade_text_candidate(verifier, candidate).reward)`, so `Reward.status` and `Reward.detail` are discarded.
- `lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/harbor/adapter.py`: `SemanticVerifier._write_result` writes only `status`, `reward`, and `error` to `taskcompendium-result.json`.
- `lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/grade.py` already has the target contract: `Status.INVALID_TASK`, `Reward.detail`, and `write_reward`, which writes `verdict.json` as `{"reward", "status", "detail"}` and omits `reward.json` for unscored verdicts.

At the head of #9623 (schema `0.22`), `GradeResult` gains `passed`, `diagnostics`, `failure`, `score_min`, `score_max`, and `rewards` (numeric components). `Outcome` gains `unavailable` and `skipped`, but still has no invalid-task value. `grade_answer` is unchanged. A `ShellVerifierSpec` that runs `verifyit` inside the grading machine has no reward source that reads `verdict.json`: an `invalid_task` verdict writes no `reward.json`, so `rolloutengine.grading._file_grade` reports `infra_error` with `failure=missing_reward`. The gap is open on main and at the PR head.

Proposed:

- Add `Outcome.INVALID_TASK = "invalid_task"`, with `reward=None`. Callers must not retry it.
- Map `verifyit.grade.Status` to `Outcome` in `grade_answer` (`scored` to `graded`, `invalid_task` to `invalid_task`, `infra_error` to `infra_error`) and copy `Reward.detail` into `GradeResult.diagnostics`. Catch `verifyit.grade.InvalidTask` raised by `candidate_spec` and return `Outcome.INVALID_TASK`.
- Add a reward source to `taskcompendium.environment` for verifiers that write verifyit's verdict file:

  ```python
  class VerdictReward(BaseModel):
      """A verifyit verdict.json: status, reward in [0, 1], and JSON detail."""
      kind: Literal["verdict"] = "verdict"
      path: str  # absolute, for example /logs/verifier/verdict.json
  ```

  `ShellVerifierSpec.reward` accepts it beside `StdoutReward`, `FileReward`, and `ExitCodeReward`. The grader maps `status` as above and stores `detail` in `diagnostics`.
- Write `diagnostics` to `taskcompendium-result.json` in the Harbor adapter so a Harbor trial and a direct grade produce the same record.

Usage: a task ships a private `grade.py` that calls verifyit and writes `verdict.json` with `write_reward`. Its `ShellVerifierSpec` sets `reward=VerdictReward(path="/logs/verifier/verdict.json")`. A caller filters `grade.status == Outcome.INVALID_TASK` into task repair, retries only `infra_error`, and checks partial credit with `grade.diagnostics["criteria"]`.

Evidence:

- In the last production run of a task-generation pipeline (construct-003), 126 of 150 failed judge calibration reports had no misgraded case, only ungraded ones. Task defects and infrastructure failures were counted together.
- Fixed partial-credit controls assert per-criterion results, for example "C1 to C6 pass and C7 fails". With only a scalar reward, these controls cannot be checked. Assertion format: `experiments/post_training/capability_env_gen/docs/partial_controls.md` on branch `mark/autoenv`.
- `experiments/post_training/capability_env_gen/docs/task_contract.md` on branch `mark/autoenv` (outcome table with four statuses).

Not in scope for TaskCompendium: reading the verdict file at grading time is implemented in `lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py` (#9623), next to `_file_grade`. The detail schema for each verifier mode belongs to verifyit.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`grade_answer()` discards `verifyit.Reward.status` and `.detail`; `resolve_verifier()` converts `InvalidTask` to `ValueError`, which the Harbor adapter records as `infra_error`. On #9623, `_file_grade()` requires `reward.json`, while `verifyit.write_reward()` omits it for `invalid_task` and `infra_error`, so a shell verifier reports a missing reward. PR #9608 also rewrites pure grading and removes the Harbor adapter; #9623 adds the shell path, and both touch this contract.

**Relevant code**
- [TaskCompendium grading](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/rollout-engine/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/grading.py) — pure verdict fields discarded.
- [verifyit verdict writer](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/grade.py) — unscored verdict omits `reward.json`.
- [rolloutengine shell grading](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/rollout-engine/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py) — missing reward becomes infrastructure failure.
- [Harbor result writer](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/rollout-engine/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/harbor/adapter.py) — diagnostics omitted.
- [#9608 grading contract](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9608) — competing pure-grading change.

# Proposed Fix

1. Reconcile #9608 and #9623 before changing the shared grading files. Keep `validate_verifier()` fail-fast, but make `grade_answer()` return `Outcome.INVALID_TASK` with `reward=None` for malformed private verifier contracts.
2. Map all three `verifyit.Reward.status` values for text and action candidates, copy `Reward.detail` into `GradeResult.diagnostics`, and preserve the existing extraction/submission-failure distinction.
3. Add `VerdictReward(path)` to `ShellVerifierSpec`. Clear stale verdicts, validate `verdict.json` after the shell command, map its status and detail into `GradeResult`, preserve execution diagnostics, and classify missing or malformed verdicts as infrastructure errors.
4. Write `diagnostics` to `taskcompendium-result.json` if the Harbor adapter remains after #9608. Add regression tests for partial-credit criterion detail, invalid private specs, all three shell verdict statuses, missing/malformed verdicts, and Harbor serialization.

These overlapping open PRs preclude a parallel implementation PR; land the change on their reconciled base.

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
With the `json` submission convention, GLM-5.3 answered a number task correctly in 3 of 3 trials, and all 3 were recorded as `extraction_error`. Each reply was

````
```json
{"answer": 42}
```
````

`extract_answer` calls `json.loads` on the whole message, so the Markdown fence fails parsing (`Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`). Without the fence the reply would still fail, because the convention requires `answer` to be a string and the model sent the integer `42`. On the same task and endpoint, the `plain` and `answer_call` conventions graded 3 of 3 at reward 1.0. As written, the JSON convention measures whether the model avoids a code fence, and training on it would teach fence avoidance.

Today: `lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/submission.py` on `origin/main`. `extract_answer` requires `json.loads(response.content)` to be an object whose `answer` is a nonempty string. `submission_instruction` says `Give your answer as a JSON object with an "answer" field.` and does not mention fences or the string type. The head of #9623 moves request building into `submission_request` but leaves `extract_answer` unchanged, and `rolloutengine` grades answer tasks through the same `grade_answer`, so the gap is open on main and at the PR head.

Proposed: pick one.

- (a) Before parsing, strip one fenced code block that encloses the whole reply. `verifyit.modes.extract.unwrap_fence` already does this. For `answer_type=number`, accept a finite JSON number and convert it to its string form. Any other non-string `answer` stays an `extraction_error`.
- (b) Keep extraction strict and state the contract in the instruction: `Reply with only a JSON object, without a code fence. "answer" must be a string.`

Option (a) changes what counts as a valid submission. Option (b) only changes the instruction text.

Usage: no caller change. Lowering and rollouts that select `SubmissionConvention(id="json", answer_format=AnswerFormat.JSON)` grade the fenced reply above as a number answer of `42` under (a), or receive the explicit instruction under (b).

Reproduce: lower a `numeric` task (expected `42`) under `SubmissionConvention(id="json", answer_format=AnswerFormat.JSON)` and run `taskcompendium.harbor.runner.run_trial` against GLM-5.3.

Evidence: two runs on 2026-10-05 (GLM-5.3, interactive tier), 9 Harbor trials each. plain: 3/3 graded 1.0 (reply `42`). json: 0/3 (`extraction_error`, every reply the fenced object above). answer_call: 3/3 graded 1.0 (`submit_answer` with `{"answer": "42"}`). A direct call with the identical JSON-convention request returned the same fenced reply with `finish_reason: "stop"` and 53 completion tokens (41 reasoning), so the reply was complete.

Not in scope for TaskCompendium: answer normalization after extraction (numeric tolerance, boxed answers) stays in verifyit.

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
`verifyit.candidate` grades an already extracted answer for only four modes: `exact`, `numeric`, `mcq`, and `predicted_action`. The other answer-file modes (`math`, `ifeval`, `json-schema`, `xml-elements`, `csv-columns`, `reasoning-gym`) can be graded only through `grade(spec, tests_dir, workspace)`, which reads the answer from a file in a workspace and resolves spec paths against a tests directory on disk. A caller that holds the candidate as text and keeps private verifier files in memory, such as a chat rollout with no machine, cannot use these modes.

Today, on `origin/main`:

- `lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/candidate.py`: `supports_candidate_mode` returns true for the four modes above. `candidate_spec` and `grade_text_candidate` dispatch only `ExactSpec | NumericSpec | McqSpec`.
- Direct graders already exist for some of the other modes: `grade_math.grade_math_candidate(spec, candidate)`, `grade_ifeval.grade_ifeval_candidate(spec, candidate)`, `grade_json_schema.grade_json_schema_candidate(schema, instance)`, and `grade_reasoning_gym.grade_reasoning_gym_candidate(spec, entry, candidate, params=...)`. `grade_xml` and `grade_csv` have only file-based `grade`.
- `JsonSchemaSpec.schema`, `ReasoningGymSpec.entry`, and `ReasoningGymSpec.params` are paths relative to the directory that holds `verifier.toml`.
- TaskCompendium stores a verifyit mode name and its parameters in `VerifierSpec(kind, parameters_json)`. It calls `candidate_spec(kind, parameters)` and `grade_text_candidate` (`lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/grading.py`), so it gains each mode added here without schema changes.

Proposed:

- Add `grade_xml_candidate(spec: XmlElementsSpec, candidate: str) -> Reward` and `grade_csv_candidate(spec: CsvColumnsSpec, candidate: str) -> Reward`, factored out of the file-based graders.
- Extend `candidate.py` to the six modes above. Path-valued fields resolve against caller-supplied file contents instead of a directory:

  ```python
  def candidate_spec(mode: str, parameters: dict[str, Any], *, files: Mapping[str, bytes] = {}) -> CandidateSpec: ...
  def grade_text_candidate(spec: TextSpec, candidate: str, *, files: Mapping[str, bytes] = {}) -> Reward: ...
  ```

  `files` maps the spec-relative path (for example `schema.json` or `entry.json`) to its bytes. A path missing from `files` raises `InvalidTask`.
- Keep `empty_output` behavior identical to the file-based graders.

Usage:

```python
spec = candidate_spec("json-schema", {"schema": "schema.json"}, files={"schema.json": schema_bytes})
reward = grade_text_candidate(spec, extracted_answer, files={"schema.json": schema_bytes})
```

TaskCompendium would pass its private verifier files as `files`.

Evidence: tasks in the construct-003 production run used `math`, `json-schema`, `xml-elements`, `csv-columns`, `ifeval`, and an instruction-constraint check for short structured answers (`experiments/post_training/capability_env_gen/docs/task_contract.md`, "Verification contract", on branch `mark/autoenv`). On `origin/main`, these tasks can be graded only by a shell verifier in a separate machine that runs the `verifyit` CLI.

Not in scope for verifyit: how an answer is extracted from a conversation (TaskCompendium submission conventions), and where private files are stored (TaskCompendium `TaskSpec`).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

`candidate_spec()` rejects the six answer modes in this issue, and `grade_text_candidate()` dispatches only exact, MCQ, and numeric specs. The file graders already implement these contracts, but JSON Schema and Reasoning Gym read private paths from disk, while XML and CSV keep their parsing inside `grade()`. TaskCompendium's `grade_answer()` has no way to pass verifier file bytes. PR #9608 also edits `candidate.py` and TaskCompendium grading, so implementation should be based on its final shape if it lands first.

**Relevant code**

- [`candidate.py#L18-L57`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/candidate.py#L18-L57) — supported modes and dispatch.
- [`grade_json_schema.py#L51-L125`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_json_schema.py#L51-L125) — file loading and schema validation.
- [`grade_reasoning_gym.py#L28-L119`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_reasoning_gym.py#L28-L119) — entry/params loading and scoring.
- [`grading.py#L45-L96`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/grading.py#L45-L96) — TaskCompendium call chain.
- [`models.py#L247-L260`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/models.py#L247-L260) — private verifier resources.

# Design

Extend `CandidateSpec` and `TextSpec` with `MathSpec`, `IfevalSpec`, `JsonSchemaSpec`, `XmlElementsSpec`, `CsvColumnsSpec`, and `ReasoningGymSpec`. Keep `candidate_spec(mode, parameters, *, files: Mapping[str, bytes] = EMPTY_FILES)` and `grade_text_candidate(spec, candidate, *, files: Mapping[str, bytes] = EMPTY_FILES)` free of filesystem access; `EMPTY_FILES` is an immutable empty mapping. Look up each path by its exact spec-relative key and decode its bytes as UTF-8. Missing files, undecodable bytes, or malformed private data raise `InvalidTask`; malformed candidate text returns a scored zero with the mode's existing detail. Validate private data before checking `empty_output`, so a broken task never becomes a valid zero because the answer is blank.

Factor JSON Schema and Reasoning Gym decoding/validation into functions shared by the file and byte paths. Reuse `grade_math_candidate()` and `grade_ifeval_candidate()`; add `grade_xml_candidate()` and `grade_csv_candidate()` by moving their current parsing and scoring out of `grade()`. Dispatch optional Schema and Reasoning Gym dependencies only when those modes are used. Apply the existing fence handling for JSON, XML, and CSV; `math` receives the already extracted answer. Keep `empty_output="zero"` and `"grade"` behavior aligned with the file graders.

Land the VerifyIt API first. After #9608 settles, pass decoded `TaskSpec.resources.verifier` files through TaskCompendium's verifier resolution and grading path in a follow-up PR, including validation. Submission extraction and private-file storage formats stay outside this issue.

## Costs and risks

The file and byte paths can drift if they parse or validate private data separately. Reasoning Gym's scorer may execute candidate expressions, so callers still need the isolation required by its direct API. The integration touches TaskCompendium while #9608 is open.

## Testing

Add focused candidate tests for one passing and one failing answer per new mode, plus missing/malformed private files, both empty-output policies, and Schema JSON/YAML/TOML parsing. Compare direct and file grades for the same XML, CSV, Schema, and Reasoning Gym fixtures, including `Reward.status` and `detail`. Add a TaskCompendium test that grades from verifier resources without creating a workspace, then run the package test suites and the required lint entry point.

## Open question

Do any intended verifier inputs live in `TaskSpec.resources.all`, or should grading use only `resources.verifier`? The proposed integration uses only `resources.verifier` to keep shared worker resources out of the private grading contract.

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
`aggregate_rewards` combines component grades with `ALL`, `MEAN`, `MAX`, `MIN`, or `PRODUCT`, and every component has equal weight. A rubric often needs three kinds of components: gates that must pass or the reward is 0, weighted criteria, and weighted penalties. `MEAN` lets a failed gate reduce the reward without zeroing it. `ALL` drops partial credit. A caller that needs gates and weights must write its own aggregation and repeat the status rules that `aggregate_rewards` already enforces.

Today, on `origin/main`, in `lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/grade.py`:

- `aggregate_rewards(verdicts, *, expected_total, policy, round_digits=None) -> Reward`. A missing component earns 0. Any `infra_error` or `invalid_task` component discards all credit, and `infra_error` takes precedence. Detail holds `passed`, `total`, and `missing`.
- `aggregate_first_fit` handles one-to-one assignment.
- No weights, gates, or penalties exist. The `judge` mode has `constraints` (IFEval checks that must pass before the model is called), which is a gate only for IFEval checks.

Proposed:

```python
class ComponentRole(StrEnum):
    GATE = "gate"          # must score 1.0, otherwise the total is 0
    CRITERION = "criterion"
    PENALTY = "penalty"    # subtracts weight * reward

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Component:
    name: str
    role: ComponentRole
    weight: float = 1.0    # finite and positive; ignored for gates

def aggregate_weighted(
    components: Sequence[Component], verdicts: Mapping[str, Reward], *, round_digits: int | None = None
) -> Reward: ...
```

- Status rules match `aggregate_rewards`: `infra_error` first, then `invalid_task`, then a missing component counted as 0.
- If any gate scores below 1.0, the result is `scored(0.0, failed_gates=[...])`, and components after that gate do not need to be graded.
- Otherwise the reward is `max(0, sum(weight * reward for criteria) - sum(weight * reward for penalties)) / sum(criterion weights)`, clamped to [0, 1].
- `detail` holds each component's reward, `failed_gates`, `positive_sum`, `penalty_sum`, and `denominator`.
- Invalid weights, duplicate names, or no criteria return `invalid_task`.
- A helper `gates_passed(components, verdicts) -> bool` lets a caller skip judge calls after a failed gate.

Usage: a task's private grading script runs its own deterministic checks, each returning a `Reward`. If `gates_passed` is true, it calls `grade_checklist_criteria` from the companion judge issue, aggregates everything with `aggregate_weighted`, and writes the result with `write_reward`.

Evidence:

- `experiments/post_training/capability_env_gen/capability_pipeline/composite_policy.py` on branch `mark/autoenv`: a 552-line aggregation contract with gates, weighted criteria, penalties, critical criteria, and caps, written outside verifyit because `aggregate_rewards` has no weights.
- In the construct-003 production run, about 129 items were lost to disagreement between the admission check and that combined gate (run audit; not in the repository).

Not in scope for verifyit: the checks a task runs and its weights (the task's own scripts), and conditional caps tied to a specific check, which a task script can apply before aggregation. A TOML `mode = "composite"` that nests child specs can follow if callers need it from the CLI.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

`aggregate_rewards` validates component verdicts and gives `infra_error` precedence over `invalid_task`, but its positional input and fixed policies cannot express named gates, criterion weights, or penalties. The `mark/autoenv` composite policy implements those rules outside verifyit, including an early machine-gate exit before judge work. [#9761](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9761) will supply per-criterion judge verdicts; [#9608](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9608) edits `grade.py` for a separate grading change, so implementation should recheck the file before editing.

**Relevant code**
- [`grade.py#L78-L147`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/grade.py#L78-L147) — verdict validation and status precedence
- [`test_grade.py#L102-L205`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/verifyit/tests/test_grade.py#L102-L205) — aggregation regression coverage
- [`composite_policy.py#L428-L533`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/af0ca2285e99dbcef75599e01bf7be7fd1607450/experiments/post_training/capability_env_gen/capability_pipeline/composite_policy.py#L428-L533) — existing gates, weights, penalties
- [`README.md#L56-L65`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/verifyit/README.md#L56-L65) — public reward contract

# Weighted and gated aggregation

Add `ComponentRole`, frozen `Component`, `aggregate_weighted`, and `gates_passed` to `verifyit.grade`. This is a public grading contract: callers can mix deterministic checks with the per-criterion judge results from #9761 without copying verifyit's verdict validation.

## Design

1. Validate the declaration before using verdicts: nonempty unique names, known roles, finite positive weights (including ignored gate weights), at least one criterion, and the existing `round_digits` range. Reject undeclared verdict names. Invalid declarations return `invalid_task`.
2. Validate every supplied verdict through the existing reward validator before applying gates. Return the first `infra_error` in declaration order if any exists; otherwise return the first `invalid_task`. Include the component name and cause in the returned detail. This keeps a failed gate from masking a supplied infrastructure failure.
3. Treat a missing declared verdict as score zero. Missing criteria remain in the denominator; missing penalties subtract zero; missing gates fail. If any gate is below 1, return `scored(0)` with all failed gate names. Otherwise compute the specified weighted criterion sum minus weighted penalty sum, divide by total criterion weight, clamp to `[0, 1]`, and apply optional rounding after clamping. Reject nonfinite aggregate arithmetic as `invalid_task`.
4. Record each declared component's score, missing names, failed gates, positive sum, penalty sum, and denominator in JSON-safe detail. `gates_passed` returns true only when every gate has a present, valid, fully scored verdict; it is a judge-call guard, and callers still pass all available verdicts to `aggregate_weighted` for the final status.

The task script owns its checks, weights, and conditional caps. No TOML mode or judge changes are part of this issue.

## Testing

Write failing behavioral tests in `lib/verifyit/tests/test_grade.py` before implementation: mixed weights and penalties; failed and missing gates; missing criteria in the denominator; error precedence even with a failed gate; invalid names, roles, weights, and nonfinite totals; rounding and persisted `write_reward` status. Run the verifyit package tests and the repository pre-commit entry point. Update the verifyit README with the public contract.

## Open question

Should an undeclared verdict name return `invalid_task`, as proposed, or be ignored? Rejecting it would catch a misspelled component name before a rubric silently changes score.

issues.title: [verifyit] Add weighted and gated reward aggregation

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
The `judge` checklist rubric returns one fraction for all criteria. A caller cannot combine the judged criteria with other checks under different weights, and cannot reduce judge noise by asking more than once. A rubric that mixes deterministic checks with model-judged criteria has to rebuild the checklist prompt and parser outside verifyit to get these.

Today, on `origin/main`, in `lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py`:

- `_judge_checklist` asks one yes/no question per criterion and returns `scored(passed / len(results), criteria=[{"criterion", "passed", "reasoning"}, ...])`. All criteria have equal weight.
- Each criterion is judged once at `temperature=0.0`. `JudgeSpec` has no sample count or resolution rule.
- `grade_judge_candidate(spec, candidate, *, connection, runtime, context, gate_candidate)` is the public entry point for callers that already hold the candidate text.

Proposed:

- Add a public function that returns one `Reward` per criterion, in `spec.criteria` order, so a caller can pass them to an aggregation function:

  ```python
  def grade_checklist_criteria(
      spec: JudgeSpec, candidate: str, *, connection: JudgeConnection | None = None,
      runtime: JudgeRuntimeSource | None = JudgeRuntimeSource.ENVIRONMENT, context: str = "",
  ) -> tuple[Reward, ...]: ...
  ```

  `_judge_checklist` becomes the mean over this tuple, so current behavior does not change.
- Add repeated judgments to `JudgeSpec`:
  - `samples: int = 1`
  - `sample_resolution: str = "majority"`, with `"two_then_third"` as the other value: two judgments, and a third only when the first two disagree.

  Each criterion's `detail` keeps every sample verdict and the call count.
- An unresolved criterion (for example, a sample that ends in an infrastructure error) makes the whole grade unscored.

Usage: a task's private grading script calls `grade_checklist_criteria`, weights the criteria together with its own machine checks, and combines them with the weighted aggregation proposed in the companion issue.

Evidence:

- `experiments/post_training/capability_env_gen/capability_pipeline/composite_policy.py` and `docs/judge.md` on branch `mark/autoenv`. That pipeline implemented weighted judge criteria, critical criteria, and `two_then_third` consensus outside its judge client, because the client returned only a scalar.
- In the construct-003 production run, about 129 items were lost to disagreement between the admission check and the combined machine-plus-judge gate (run audit; not in the repository).

Not in scope for verifyit: which criteria a task has and their wording (the task), and ordinal rubric anchors, which a task can encode as binary threshold criteria.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

The checklist path filters blank criteria, asks once per remaining criterion, and returns only their mean; direct callers cannot weight the individual verdicts. `_ask` can make a second provider call to repair malformed output, so sample counts and provider call counts need separate definitions. No open PR found for #9761 or `grade_checklist_criteria`; [#9762](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9762) is the separate aggregation change.

**Relevant code**
- [`grade_judge.py#L139-L174`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L139-L174) — validation and blank-criterion filtering.
- [`grade_judge.py#L184-L236`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L184-L236) — direct candidate gates and dispatch.
- [`grade_judge.py#L466-L499`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L466-L499) — checklist grading and retry path.
- [`spec.py#L261-L295`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/spec.py#L261-L295) — serialized judge contract.
- [`grade.py#L356-L365`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7190b39f183ed938b9e9d2711eb96468b94b3a84/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/grade.py#L356-L365) — provider failures become unscored CLI verdicts.

# Proposed Fix

This changes a public API and a serialized grading contract, so the implementation should land as a focused verifyit PR with these steps:

1. Add `grade_checklist_criteria(spec, candidate, *, connection=None, runtime=JudgeRuntimeSource.ENVIRONMENT, context="") -> tuple[Reward, ...]`. Validate the checklist rubric and return exactly one reward per criterion in input order. Reject blank criteria during validation; silently dropping them would make tuple positions ambiguous. Apply the same empty-output policy, constraints, context limit, and endpoint selection as `grade_judge_candidate`; a blank candidate or failed constraint yields an ordered tuple of zero rewards without provider calls.
2. Add `samples=1` and a two-value `SampleResolution` enum to `JudgeSpec`, serialized as `majority` or `two_then_third`. For `majority`, require a positive odd sample count and judge every sample. For `two_then_third`, require `samples=3`: judge twice, then call a third time only on disagreement. Reject nondefault sampling on reference and labels rubrics rather than ignoring it.
3. Keep `_ask`'s malformed-reply retry separate from sampling. Record every resolved sample's verdict and reasoning in each criterion reward, plus the number of actual provider calls, including retries. If any call or sample cannot resolve, raise as the direct candidate API currently does; the file/CLI path then returns `infra_error` for the whole grade, with no partial credit.
4. Make the scalar checklist grade the mean of the criterion rewards, retaining its `passed`, `total`, and ordered `criteria` detail fields for existing callers. Document the new API and sampling fields in `lib/verifyit/README.md`.
5. Add fake-provider regression tests before implementation for order and scalar parity at defaults, 3-vote majority, both 2-call and 3-call `two_then_third` paths, retry-inclusive call counts, invalid specs before any provider call, and an error after an earlier positive sample yielding no scored CLI reward. Run the verifyit tests and repository lint/review gates before opening the PR.

The `samples=3` requirement for `two_then_third` makes `samples` the maximum number of judgments and avoids silently overriding the configured count. Weighted composition remains in #9762.

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
The rollout engine can grade a task only at the end of a model rollout. A task author cannot check a task's verifier against a known final state before training on it: for example, that a reference solution scores 1, that a plausible wrong solution scores 0, or that a partly correct solution earns the expected partial credit. Shell-graded tasks need these checks most, because their verifier reads the final machine state, and the only way to produce that state today is to run a model.

Today, at the head of #9623 (`lib/rolloutengine`, not on `origin/main`):

- `ShellboxRolloutEngine.run(task)` creates the machine, runs the model loop, and then grades through the private `rolloutengine.grading._grade_rollout(task, convention, messages, machine, factories)`.
- `_grade_rollout` already handles each verifier kind: pure answer verifiers through `taskcompendium.grading.grade_answer`, `ShellVerifierSpec` in the task machine or in a separate grading machine with `collect` and `artifacts`, and `skipped`.
- `_validate_task` rejects any nonempty `TaskSpec.resources` group, including `oracle`. Schema `0.22` therefore has no executable path for oracle material.
- The machine lifecycle (`machines._task_machine`, file installation, setup, healthcheck) is private.

Proposed: a public entry point that builds the task machine, applies a supplied final state, and runs the task's verifier with the same code path as a rollout:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SuppliedState:
    messages: tuple[dict[str, Any], ...]          # final conversation; the last item is the assistant submission
    files: tuple[EnvironmentFile, ...] = ()       # installed after environment setup, before grading
    commands: tuple[EnvironmentCommand, ...] = () # run after files, for state that is not a file

async def grade_state(self, task: TaskSpec, state: SuppliedState) -> GradeResult: ...
```

on `ShellboxRolloutEngine`, so it uses the engine's machine factories and convention. For a staged task, it grades only the first stage, or accepts one `SuppliedState` per stage. Machines are closed on every exit path, as in `run`.

Usage: before admitting a task, the author grades a reference solution and labeled wrong solutions, then compares each `GradeResult` with its label:

```python
grade = await engine.grade_state(task, SuppliedState(messages=final_messages, files=reference_files))
assert grade.status == Outcome.GRADED and grade.reward == 1.0
```

Evidence:

- `experiments/post_training/capability_env_gen/capability_pipeline/synthesis.py` (`_validate_controls`, which accepts `workspace` candidates) and `docs/partial_controls.md` on branch `mark/autoenv`. That pipeline graded authored workspaces through the same verifier as trials, using its own sandbox wrapper.
- 15 of the 16 tasks accepted in the construct-003 production run used a verifier that ran in a container. Each needed a reference-solution check before acceptance.

Not in scope for rolloutengine: which reference and wrong solutions a task has, and how their labels are checked (the task author's pipeline). The `GradeResult` fields used for partial-credit labels are covered by the TaskCompendium issue on verifier status and detail.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

At the head of [#9623](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9623), `run()` creates a task machine and reaches grading only after model turns; callers cannot submit a known transcript and workspace directly. The existing machine lifecycle and `_grade_rollout` already cover pure, skipped, and shell verifiers, including artifact transfer to a separate grading machine. `TaskSpec.resources.oracle` is rejected with every other resource group, so a supplied state must remain an explicit caller input until that resource contract is designed.

**Relevant code**
- [`engine.py#L71-L97`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7eb1dff26f70df3422c7f2ca0ffc9b6f59240b96/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/engine.py#L71-L97) — machine and session lifecycle
- [`task_session.py#L94-L117`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7eb1dff26f70df3422c7f2ca0ffc9b6f59240b96/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/task_session.py#L94-L117) — stage preparation
- [`grading.py#L38-L88`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7eb1dff26f70df3422c7f2ca0ffc9b6f59240b96/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py#L38-L88) — validation and verifier dispatch
- [`machines.py#L27-L56`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7eb1dff26f70df3422c7f2ca0ffc9b6f59240b96/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/machines.py#L27-L56) — file installation and commands
- [`models.py#L359-L439`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7eb1dff26f70df3422c7f2ca0ffc9b6f59240b96/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/models.py#L359-L439) — staged task contract

# Proposed design: grade a supplied state

## Goal

Task authors should be able to grade reference and negative-control states through the same verifier used by a rollout, without issuing a model request. Implement this on top of #9623 after its task-session contract stabilizes. No open PR currently targets #9763; [#9757](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9757) owns richer verifier status and detail.

## Public contract

Add `SuppliedState` to `rolloutengine.contracts` and `ShellboxRolloutEngine.grade_state(task, state) -> GradeResult`:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SuppliedState:
    messages: tuple[dict[str, Any], ...]
    files: tuple[EnvironmentFile, ...] = ()
    commands: tuple[EnvironmentCommand, ...] = ()

async def grade_state(self, task: TaskSpec, state: SuppliedState) -> GradeResult: ...
```

`messages` is the exact verifier-visible transcript. The method does not prepend the messages returned by `prepare()`; callers include task context and a final assistant submission when the verifier needs them. A shell verifier may grade only filesystem state with an empty transcript; pure-answer grading requires a nonempty transcript. Files use absolute machine paths and are installed after environment and stage setup, so they may intentionally replace earlier files. Commands run afterward in tuple order. The method never calls `self.model` and returns no token or rollout record.

## Execution

1. Validate the task with the rollout validator. Reject interaction sessions: their custom `TaskSession` may grade application-specific state, and this API only specifies Shellbox state. Reject files or commands for a null environment and an empty transcript for a pure-answer verifier before creating a machine. Leave assistant-message extraction to the existing grader.
2. Put the attempt timeout inside an `AsyncExitStack`, as `run()` does, so cleanup is outside the deadline. Enter `_task_machine`, construct the default `_ShellboxTaskSession`, and call `prepare()` so capability checks and stage setup match `run()`. Install supplied files with `_install_files`, run commands with `_run_setup_commands`, then call `session.grade(state.messages)`. This reaches `_grade_rollout` and its separate grading machine where configured.
3. Close the session before the machine and finish machine cleanup on success, command failure, grading failure, timeout, and cancellation. A supplied command with a nonzero exit raises `RuntimeError`; command or attempt timeout raises `TimeoutError`. Unexpected machine, preparation, and grading exceptions propagate after cleanup. Return the existing `GradeResult` for graded, skipped, extraction-error, and verifier-reported infrastructure outcomes; do not manufacture a `RolloutInterrupted` without rollout data.

For a staged task, build the same first-stage phase as `_run_stages`: replace the parent verifier with `task.stages[0].verifier`, clear `stages`, and apply that stage's context, timeout, and user overrides. Pass the stage to `_ShellboxTaskSession` so its files, setup, and healthcheck run. Return only that stage's `GradeResult`, not an aggregate task grade. A later API can accept one state per stage and reuse the existing stage reduction rules; treating one supplied state as a whole staged task would mislabel partial calibration.

The caller supplies oracle files explicitly in `SuppliedState`. Keep `run()`'s rejection of `TaskSpec.resources.oracle` and the other resource groups: loading them into the worker machine would require a separate visibility and schema decision. Author pipelines own reference/wrong-state labels and compare them against the returned grade; this API does not store or interpret those labels.

## Validation

Write ShellSim behavior tests before implementation. Compare direct grading with `run()` for equivalent pure-answer and shell states, including a wrong answer; verify setup → supplied files → commands → verifier ordering, `collect` plus artifacts in a separate grader, and zero model calls. Test first-stage-only behavior, invalid null-machine input, nonzero supplied commands, and machine closure after success, failure, timeout, and cancellation. Update `lib/rolloutengine/README.md` and `docs/references/task-rollouts.md` with the contract and a reference-solution example; run the package's default tests and repository pre-commit gates before a stacked PR.

## Costs and open question

The API adds a second task execution path, so reuse `_task_machine`, `_ShellboxTaskSession.prepare`, and `_grade_rollout` rather than copying their behavior. The existing engine constructor still requires a model callable and rollout limits even though this method never uses them; keeping one engine preserves its machine factories and submission convention. A dedicated model-free grader would be reasonable if calibration becomes a primary caller. Should later-stage calibration be required in the first PR? The proposed first-stage contract keeps `grade_state(task, state)` unambiguous; a per-stage sequence would also need to define partial and failed-stage aggregation, which is under discussion on #9623.

`taskcompendium.verifier_registry.resolve_verifier` calls `verifyit.candidate_spec(mode, parameters)` without the `files` mapping added by #9759. After #9759 lands, `verifyit.supports_candidate_mode` returns true for `json-schema`, `xml-elements`, `csv-columns`, `ifeval`, `math`, and `reasoning-gym`. The `json-schema` schema and `reasoning-gym` params come from private files, so `candidate_spec` raises `ValueError("verifier file not supplied")` instead of grading them. `supports_verifier` and `compatible_lowerings` then raise for those `VerifierSpec` values instead of returning false and skipping the task.

Pass the task's verifier-role resources to `candidate_spec` as `files`, keyed by the path named in the spec. The source is `TaskSpec.resources.verifier` on `main`, or `ShellVerifierSpec.files` or the equivalent private files at the head of #9623. Until that wiring exists, gate `json-schema` and `reasoning-gym` in `supports_verifier` so they return false instead of raising.

With the plain dependency and no verifyit extras, importing those modes raises `ImportError` for `jsonschema` or `reasoning_gym`. Declare the extras TaskCompendium relies on or report the mode as unsupported.

TaskCompendium's tests on the #9759 branch pass (119 and 128 passed) because no existing test exercises these modes. The candidate graders themselves (#9759) and the task-specific files shipped with a generated task are outside TaskCompendium's scope.

# Research

On current `main`, VerifyIt supports only four candidate modes; #9759 would make the missing-file failure reachable. `compatible_lowerings()` calls `supports_verifier()` → `validate_verifier()` → `resolve_verifier()` → `candidate_spec()` without the task's verifier files, so a path-based mode would raise while selecting tasks. PRs #9608, #9623, and #9642 change this grading path, and #9759 has no implementation PR yet.

**Relevant code**

- [`candidate.py#L18-L47`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/36c462ae5cfb98f05dc8163e14a761879791f2de/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/candidate.py#L18-L47) — current candidate API and mode gate.
