spillover_issues.author: Helw150
spillover_issues.body:
🤖 Picks up part of **item 4 (structured generation)** of #7090.

## Proposal

Add the **conversion subset of StructEval** as tasks in lm-eval-harness, so structured-generation compliance can run alongside our other harness evals.

- Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/TIGER-Lab/StructEval (single parquet, 2,035 rows)
- Paper: [StructEval: Benchmarking LLMs' Capabilities to Generate Structural Outputs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20139) (TIGER-Lab)
- Project page: https://tiger-ai-lab.github.io/StructEval/

## Scope: the non-renderable conversion tasks

StructEval has two halves. The renderable half (HTML/React/Vue/SVG/Mermaid/TikZ…) is scored by rendering + VQA, which doesn't fit lm-eval-harness. The **conversion half between data formats is mechanically scorable** and maps cleanly onto the harness:

| Task family | Tasks |
|---|---|
| CSV → JSON / XML / YAML | 150 |
| JSON → CSV / XML / YAML | 150 |
| XML → CSV / JSON / YAML | 150 |
| YAML → CSV / JSON / XML | 150 |
| TOML → JSON / YAML | 100 |

700 examples total (50 per direction), filtered from the parquet by `task_name` (e.g. `"CSV to JSON"`). Each row carries `query` (the full prompt including the source document), `feature_requirements`, and `raw_output_metric` (keyword list for scoring).

## Implementation sketch

1. One lm-eval-harness task group (e.g. `structeval_conversion`) with a sub-task per conversion direction, all reading `TIGER-Lab/StructEval` with a `task_name` filter.
2. Metrics, two layers:
   - **Syntactic validity**: extract the output block and parse it with the target format's parser (`json.loads`, `yaml.safe_load`, `csv.reader`, `xml.etree`, `tomllib`) → binary parse-success.
   - **Content fidelity**: StructEval's own `raw_output_metric` keyword match; optionally stricter round-trip equality (parse source and output to Python objects and compare) for the directions where that's well-defined.
3. Generation config: greedy, stop on closing code fence; prompts are already self-contained in `query`.

## Notes / open questions

- StructEval prompts are instruction-shaped ("Please output JSON: …"), so this slots in as a chat/instruct eval; a base-model variant would need light prompt surgery (few-shot completion form).
- This covers the *format compliance* part of item 4. The "**large amounts** of compliant data" axis (does compliance survive 500-row CSVs, deeply nested JSON?) is not in StructEval and is left for a separate, fully programmatic eval (generate N ground-truth records → render in format X → score by parser round-trip, sweeping N). XLSX likewise isn't covered here.
- Upstreaming: worth checking whether EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness would take this as a PR; otherwise it can live in our task fork.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 Scoping this as an analysis (new eval + task-registration plumbing, not a self-contained bug fix), so no PR yet — a design decision is needed first.

# Research

The proposal's "one lm-eval-harness task group with a sub-task per direction" assumes we can drop task YAMLs into a local task dir. **We can't, as-is.** Marin doesn't vendor lm-eval — it's a pip pin on the stanford-crfm fork ([`pyproject.toml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/pyproject.toml) `lm-eval[math,api,ifeval] @ d5e3391`). Tasks are selected by name via `EvalTaskConfig`, converted to Levanter's `TaskConfig`, then materialized by lm-eval's `TaskManager`.

The blocker for StructEval specifically: its scoring (extract fenced block → parse with target parser `json/yaml/csv/xml/tomllib` → keyword match on `raw_output_metric`) is **custom Python**. In lm-eval that means a `process_results`/filter `!function` reference, which must be importable and the task must be discoverable. Two ways to make a task discoverable — register it in the fork, or point `TaskManager` at a local dir via `include_path` — and **neither is wired up**:

**Relevant code**
- [`eval_harness.py#L1136`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval_harness.py#L1136) — `TaskManager()` built with **no `include_path`**; no local task dir is ever loaded
- [`eval_harness.py#L1004-L1058`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval_harness.py#L1004) — `TaskConfig` inline fields: `dataset_path`, `output_type`, `metric_list`… but `metric_list` only takes registered metrics or `!function` refs, not inline Python
- [`evaluation_config.py#L15-L27`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evaluation_config.py#L15) — `EvalTaskConfig(name, num_fewshot, task_alias, task_kwargs)`, the marin-facing surface
- [`task_configs.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/task_configs.py) — where task-set tuples live once a task is registerable
- [`levanter_lm_eval_evaluator.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evaluators/levanter_lm_eval_evaluator.py) — `EvalTaskConfig` → `TaskConfig` conversion

Data side of the proposal checks out: `TIGER-Lab/StructEval` is one parquet, and the 700 conversion rows are filterable by `task_name` (e.g. `"CSV to JSON"`) with `query`/`feature_requirements`/`raw_output_metric` columns. TIGER-Lab datasets are already used elsewhere (`experiments/datasets/eval.py`), no StructEval refs yet.

# Proposed approach (needs a human decision)

The eval itself is small; the **task-registration mechanism** is the real choice. Options:

1. **Local task dir + `include_path` (recommended).** Add StructEval task YAMLs and a `structeval_score.py` (the parser/keyword scorer) under a marin-owned tasks dir, and thread an `include_path` through `LmEvalHarnessConfig` → `TaskManager(include_path=...)`. Self-contained, no fork churn, reusable for future custom tasks. Cost: new plumbing in `eval_harness.py` (~a dozen lines) + the scorer + task YAMLs (one per direction, or one templated group).
2. **Upstream to the stanford-crfm fork.** Land the tasks in the fork, bump the pin, then just add `EvalTaskConfig("structeval_...")` in `task_configs.py`. No marin plumbing, but cross-repo PR + pin bump, and the scorer lives outside marin.
3. **Fully-inline via `task_kwargs`/`metric_list`.** Only works if scoring reduces to registered metrics — it doesn't (custom parse+keyword), so this is out unless we accept a much weaker exact-match metric.

Recommendation: **option 1**. It unblocks StructEval and every future custom-scored eval, and keeps the scorer in-repo and tested.

Open questions for the maintainer before implementation:
- **Metric strictness**: parse-success (binary) + `raw_output_metric` keyword match, or also the stricter round-trip object-equality mentioned in the issue? Round-trip is only well-defined for some directions.
- **Chat vs base**: proposal notes prompts are instruct-shaped; run instruct-only first (`apply_chat_template=True`), defer the base-model prompt surgery?
- **Fork appetite**: is bumping the stanford-crfm fork pin on the table, or do we keep custom tasks marin-local (favoring option 1)?

Happy to implement option 1 once the metric definition and the local-tasks-dir approach are confirmed.

spillover_issues.author: timodonnell
spillover_issues.body:
On marin GPU training (`--extra gpu`, CoreWeave H100 `cw-rno2a`), levanter dense-LM attention runs **non-fused**, leaving significant throughput on the table at long sequence lengths.

## Root cause — a backend/dependency mismatch
- levanter's default GPU attention backend is `AttentionBackend.NVTE` (Transformer Engine), but the `gpu` extra ships **`flash-attn-4[cu13]`**, not `transformer_engine`. So NVTE hits `transformer_engine is not installed … Falling back to the reference implementation` (`levanter/layers/attention.py`) — a non-fused O(seq²) kernel that also OOMs at seq 8192.
- `AttentionBackend.JAX_FLASH` avoids the OOM but is an XLA-fusion blocked-flash (memory-safe, not a fused CUDA kernel).
- The **`flash-attn-4`** that the `gpu` extra installs has **no levanter backend wired to it** (enum: `{DEFAULT, NVTE, SPLASH, JAX_FLASH, VANILLA}`; `attention.py` never imports `flash_attn`). So the fused library marin ships is dead weight for dense-LM training.

## Evidence (from MarinFold exp108 — 3B Qwen3, seq 8192, 8×H100)
- The TE-not-installed fallback warning on the default backend.
- A perfetto trace of a real run (`jax_flash`): attention appears only as XLA `gemm_fusion_dot` + `exp`/`reduce` softmax fusions — no fused/flash/pallas/TE kernel. ~25% of GPU compute time is reduce/softmax, ~45% is non-GEMM.
- OOM (`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, 64 GiB score matrix) with the reference path at batch 128 × seq 8192.

## Ask
Provide a working fused-attention path for levanter **dense-LM** GPU training. Two options:
1. **Wire a levanter attention backend to the `flash-attn-4` marin already ships** (preferred — it's installed, avoids adding a heavy dep), or
2. Add `transformer_engine` to the `gpu` extra so the existing NVTE default works.

## Impact
Any levanter dense-LM GPU run on marin. Concretely, MarinFold's first GPU sweep is training with non-fused attention: Open-Athena/MarinFold#108.

comments.author: timodonnell
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

Confirmed: `default_attention_type()` returns NVTE on GPU, but the gpu extra ships `flash-attn-4` + `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` and not `transformer_engine`, so the default warns and drops to the unfused path. Levanter already has a differentiable FA4/CuTe JAX binding in grug (custom-VJP backward, bf16/fp16 causal self-attention, GQA, packed segment ids via per-token lower bounds, sliding window, SM80/90/100/120) with fwd+grad parity tests against reference — it just isn't reachable from `dot_product_attention`.

**Relevant code**
- [`attention.py#L82-L89`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/layers/attention.py#L82-L89) - GPU default = NVTE
- [`attention.py#L415-L506`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/layers/attention.py#L415-L506) - `_try_te_attention` fallback contract (warn → None → blocked JAX flash)
- [`_fa4_cute_backend.py#L652-L750`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute_backend.py#L652-L750) - differentiable FA4 kernel boundary (`jax.custom_vjp`)
- [`_fa4_cute.py#L149-L170`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute.py#L149-L170) - causal/packed/sliding-window → `lower_bounds`/`valid` lowering
- [`lib/levanter/pyproject.toml#L90`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/pyproject.toml#L90) - gpu extra already ships flash-attn-4 + cutlass-dsl

# Proposed Fix

Option 1 (wire the shipped flash-attn-4), all in `levanter/layers/attention.py`:

- Add `AttentionBackend.FA4 = "fa4"`. `default_attention_type()` returns FA4 on GPU when `flash_attn` + `cutlass` are importable, else NVTE (TE installs keep today's behavior).
- Add `_try_fa4_attention(...)` mirroring `_try_te_attention`: bin NamedArray axes to BSHD with the existing `_bin_and_group_axes_by_function`, lower the layers `AttentionMask` (`is_causal` + `segment_ids` + `sliding_window`) to FA4 `lower_bounds`/`valid` via the existing grug helpers, and `shard_map` `fa4_cute_attention_forward(..., sm_scale=scaling_factor)` with haliax physical pspecs (splash-style; batch/head sharding OK, sequence must be unsharded).
- Unsupported configs (dropout>0, bias, `logits_soft_cap`, `attn_sink`, `causal_offset`, explicit/non-causal mask, cross-attention, non-bf16/fp16, unsupported arch) warn once and return None → existing memory-safe blocked JAX flash; explicit `attn_backend: fa4` raises instead.
- No dependency changes; grug FA4 entry points get public exports (hoisting to `levanter/kernels/` can follow separately).

Rejected: `transformer_engine` in the gpu extra (heavy, tightly version-coupled to jax/CUDA; nothing tracks jax 0.10 reliably); `jax.nn.dot_product_attention(implementation="cudnn")` (no packed segment_ids, and packing is the common dense-LM path); the FA4 THD variant (head_dim-128-only, rejects MHA, sliding window unimplemented on SM90).

Tests: CPU — mask→lower-bounds lowering + fallback/forced-raise dispatch; GPU-gated — fwd+grad parity of `dot_product_attention(attn_backend=fa4)` vs reference across MHA/GQA/packing/sliding-window (mirroring `tests/grug/test_fa4_cute_attention.py`). Validation: dense-LM step at seq 8192 on H100 with no fallback warning and the fused kernel visible in the trace.

Note: I did not use `levanter_flash_patch.zip` from the earlier comment — an opaque patch archive from an unaffiliated account shouldn't be applied; maintainers may want to hide that comment.

comments.author: timodonnell
comments.body: 🤖 Fix up at #7015: adds `AttentionBackend.FA4` wired to the grug FA4/CuTe segmented kernels and makes it the GPU default when the `gpu` extra's `flash-attn-4`/`nvidia-cutlass-dsl` are importable (NVTE otherwise). Validated on a cw-rno2a H100 pod: fwd+grad parity vs reference across MHA/GQA/packed-segments/sliding-window at 7e-2 tolerance, and 3.4× faster than the `jax_flash` fallback on this issue's shape (seq 8192, GQA 32/8, head_dim 128, bf16: 11.3 ms vs 38.9 ms fwd+bwd per iteration, single GPU).

spillover_issues.author: Helw150
spillover_issues.body:
🤖 _Reworked by an agent (William's session). Original title/scope: "Test Qwen 2.5 Base on David's PPL sets, Correlate with Coder Models SWE-Bench Perf." — generalized below; the coder/SWE-bench instance is retained as a planned extension._

## Hypothesis

A base model's **perplexity (bits-per-byte) on a target skill's reasoning traces** predicts how good that model becomes **after post-training** on that skill — before running any post-training. If true, base-model PPL on the right distribution is a cheap screen for "will this base respond to RL/SFT on skill X."

This is the mechanistic version of the SimpleRL-Zoo finding ("Qwen bases respond to zero-RL, Llama/Mistral don't"): the base that already compresses the reasoning-trace distribution best is the one post-training can most easily amplify.

## What we ran this session (math / SimpleRL-Zoo instance)

- **Eval set:** new `math_reasoning` PPL bundle — `nvidia/OpenMathReasoning` `cot` + `tir` splits (verified long CoT math traces), target-only BPB, 256 docs/split, 4096 ctx. Built in David's perplexity-gap format.
- **Models:** the 10 SimpleRL-Zoo base models (Qwen2.5 0.5B–32B, Qwen2.5-Math-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, DeepSeek-Math-7B, Mistral-7B-v0.1, Mistral-Small-24B).
- **Where:** scored in-process via Levanter on a v5p-8 dev TPU.
- **Correlated against:** the published SimpleRL-Zoo post-training accuracy table (avg over GSM8K / MATH500 / Minerva / Olympiad / AIME24 / AMC23).

### Result (n=10)

![Base-model PPL vs post-SimpleRL accuracy (n=10, r=-0.89)](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Helw150/fca0e45e3fa10b7d0c0a8ecb4c79fbfa/raw/simplerl_corr.png)

_Interactive version (Plotly scatter with cot/tir + base/post toggles and a 7–8B-cohort filter) lives in `experiments/score_simplerl_math_reasoning_ppl.py`'s companion viewer (`simplerl_viewer/index.html`, served locally during the session)._

| Predictor | → post-SimpleRL Avg |
|---|---|
| base **cot** BPB | Pearson r = **−0.89**, Spearman ρ = −0.87 |
| base **tir** BPB | Pearson r = **−0.92**, Spearman ρ = −0.87 |
| within 7–8B cohort (cot) | Pearson r = **−0.97** |

Lower base BPB on the reasoning traces ⇒ higher post-RL math accuracy. Holds across n=7→10 as points landed; strongest within a fixed size band (removes the size confound).

| Model | base cot BPB | base Avg | +SimpleRL Avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-32B | 0.402 | 45.9 | 61.9 |
| Qwen2.5-14B | 0.418 | 43.2 | 56.8 |
| Mistral-Small-24B | 0.430 | 27.6 | 49.6 |
| Qwen2.5-7B | 0.440 | 40.3 | 55.2 |
| Qwen2.5-Math-7B | 0.443 | 37.2 | 59.5 |
| DeepSeek-Math-7B | 0.494 | 11.3 | 29.2 |
| Llama-3.1-8B | 0.495 | 10.6 | 22.0 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | 0.504 | 18.5 | 36.1 |
| Mistral-7B-v0.1 | 0.523 | 5.3 | 18.6 |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | 0.587 | 12.1 | 20.9 |

## Artifacts produced

- `experiments/evals/math_reasoning_ppl.py` — `math_reasoning` validation sets (OpenMathReasoning cot/tir), registered as a bundle in `experiments/evals/perplexity_gap_registry.py`.
- `experiments/exp_simplerl_base_math_reasoning_ppl.py` — executor experiment scoring the 10 base models on the bundle (one Iris TPU job per model).
- `experiments/score_simplerl_math_reasoning_ppl.py` — lightweight dev-TPU scorer (one model per subprocess, clears HF cache between models to fit disk).
- **Levanter fix:** `lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/mistral.py` — `MistralConfig` now honors an explicit `head_dim` (read it in `from_hf_config`, use it in `HeadSize` and `attention_config`). Required to load Mistral-Small-24B (head_dim=128 ≠ hidden/heads); backward-compatible no-op when `head_dim` is None. `LlamaConfig.from_hf_config` has the same gap — worth a follow-up.
- `scripts/iris/dev_tpu.py` — added `--priority` flag to `allocate`.

## Caveats

- Predicts **level** (base and post-RL accuracy), not the **gain** (delta is noisy w.r.t. BPB).
- Across all sizes the −0.89 is partly the size confound (bigger ⇒ lower BPB everywhere); the within-cohort −0.97 is the cleaner cross-architecture signal.
- n is small.
- base-BPB → base-accuracy is near-tautological; the non-obvious result is base-BPB → **post-RL** accuracy.

## Next steps

1. **More David PPL sets** — run the same 10 base models on additional bundles and compare per-bundle correlation:
   - *signal:* `synthetic_reasoning` (StepMath + algorithmic; needs a 3-line bundle wrapper), `code_interpretation`, `ppl_circuit_coverage_v2`.
   - *control:* `base_raw` (Paloma + uncheatable) — generic-text BPB should predict math-RL outcome **weakly**; that's what shows the predictor is reasoning-distribution-specific, not generic LM quality.
2. **Post-trained BPB** — score the 10 `hkust-nlp/*-SimpleRL-Zoo` checkpoints on the same traces to correlate base-BPB ↔ post-BPB directly (not just vs published accuracy).
3. **Original coder/SWE-bench instance** — score Qwen2.5(-Coder) bases' PPL on code-reasoning/SWE traces and correlate with Coder-model SWE-bench performance, mirroring the math result.
4. Commit/PR the artifacts above; consider upstreaming the Levanter `head_dim` fix.

comments.author: Helw150
comments.body:
🤖 Session summary — extended the base-PPL → post-RL study to a full exploitation/exploration decomposition and a semantic-branching metric. All numbers below are the 10 SimpleRL-Zoo base models, scored on a v5p-8 via Levanter, targets = the published SimpleRL-Zoo accuracy table.

## 1. Exploitation — correct-solution NLL (BPB)
Base BPB on the verified OpenMathReasoning `cot`/`tir` traces *is* the correct-solution NLL. It predicts post-RL math accuracy:
- `cot` → post-RL Avg: **r = −0.89**; `tir` → **r = −0.92**; within the 7–8B cohort **r = −0.97**.

**Distribution-specificity** (added `synthetic_reasoning` = StepMath + algorithmic/CLRS, 32 slices): real math traces predict post-RL far better than templated synthetic reasoning — `cot` −0.89 vs `synth` −0.68…−0.72 (StepMath best, CLRS worst). The predictor is specific to the *target* distribution, not "reasoning-shaped" text.

**PPL vs the pre-RL metric**: base PPL beats pre-RL accuracy at predicting post-RL **exactly where the benchmark saturates/floors** — GSM8K (|r| 0.98 vs 0.74), Minerva (0.92 vs 0.85), AIME24 avg@32 (0.84 vs 0.79). On clean mid-difficulty metrics (MATH500/Olympiad/AMC) the pre-RL number wins.

## 2. Exploration — does adding a policy-spread term help?
Computed per-target-token, same forward pass: token entropy `H`, `p_top`/`branch_mass`, renormalized-tail entropy, and an **embedding effective-rank** (participation ratio of the policy-weighted top-k *output-embedding* cloud — "semantic branching", which ignores syntactic synonyms that token entropy over-counts).

- **Token entropy is ~redundant with BPB** (collinearity +0.93). A confident model is peaked on the correct token *and* peaked overall.
- **Embedding effective-rank is less redundant** (collinearity +0.78) and adds real signal: the joint model `post_+RL ~ BPB + emb_rank` gives **R² = 0.931 (adj 0.91)** vs BPB-only 0.797 (adj 0.77). `emb_rank` β = −67, **t = −3.68, p = 0.008**; model F(2,7) = 47, p = 0.0001. **LOO-CV RMSE drops 10.6 → 6.7** acc-pts (out-of-sample improvement → not just overfitting an extra knob).
- Sign is **negative**: at matched BPB, *more* semantic branching → *worse* post-RL. So even the cleaner "semantic" metric leans toward decisiveness/clarity, not "exploration helps."

## 3. The deflating caveat — it predicts capability *level*, not RL-friendliness
RL adds a near-constant **+15.8 ± 4.1** pts to everyone, so **base and post-RL accuracy are 0.97 correlated**. Consequences:
- Predicting base vs +RL is the same problem (joint R² 0.923 vs 0.931) — the base/+RL toggle is cosmetic.
- Predicting the **RL gain** (post − base) **fails: R² = 0.33**, and `emb_rank` *hurts* adj-R² there.

So this work shows base PPL (+ semantic effective-rank) forecast **math-capability level**, which RL preserves — **not** *which weak base benefits most from RL*. The gain stays largely unexplained.

## Honest limitations
n = 10, and the models aren't independent (≈3 families × a size ladder, with a strong scale confound), so OLS p-values are optimistic — treat as suggestive, not established. Metrics are teacher-forced on *correct* traces at T=1 (a proxy for free-sampling exploration); the real exploration signal is sequence-level / correct-vs-incorrect separation. Target is the published post-RL **Avg**, not measured pass@K. `emb_rank` used k=16 / output embeddings.

## Artifacts (branch, uncommitted)
- `experiments/evals/math_reasoning_ppl.py` + `synthetic_reasoning` bundle in `perplexity_gap_registry.py`
- `experiments/exp_simplerl_base_math_reasoning_ppl.py` (executor) and `experiments/score_simplerl_math_reasoning_ppl.py` (lightweight dev-TPU scorer, `--metric nll|entropy`)
- Levanter `compute_target_entropy` (entropy, p_top, tail, **emb_eff_rank**) in `lib/levanter/.../main/perplexity_gap.py`; plus a `MistralConfig` `head_dim` fix (needed to load Mistral-Small-24B)
- `scripts/iris/dev_tpu.py` `--priority` flag
- Interactive monitor (lenses × per-benchmark/base/+RL/gain targets, pre-RL-vs-PPL scoreboard, sigmoid + joint BPB+emb_rank fit with floored predictions, live R²/adj-R²/LOO).

## Suggested next steps
1. Validate against **measured pass@K**, not the published Avg.
2. More base models / independent families to break the size confound (cluster- or family-held-out fits).
3. Sequence-level exploration (distinct-answer diversity, or silhouette clarity on a static AIME rollout set) to actually target the *gain*.

<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment proposes scientific and technical reasoning PPL coverage under #5819 using train/dev or generated non-benchmark data, while keeping exact HLE, GPQA Diamond, CritPt, SciCode, and similar held-out items out of regular tracking. The research pass found the PPL gap framework already exists, so the open work is dataset selection and bundle wiring rather than new evaluation infrastructure. The recommended `science_train_core` bundle would reference MCQA work from #5828, add license-cleared biomedical train/dev slices, generated science QA/cloze from source documents, scientific notebook continuation, numeric/unit and equation-notation probes, and existing formal-methods coverage from #5060. Implementation is waiting on maintainer decisions about license posture, bundle split/rollup conventions, and whether formula continuation belongs here or under surface-form probes.

### Helpful links
- Parent: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5819
- Formal methods coverage: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5060
- Research and proposed approach: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5829#issuecomment-4483266920
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Part of #5819. Add scientific and technical reasoning coverage using non-benchmark validation data and train/dev canaries only. Do not use exact HLE, GPQA Diamond, CritPt, SciCode, or similar held-out benchmark items in core PPL tracking.

AI2 ARC is useful but mostly grade-school science MCQA. It should be part of MCQA/science canary coverage, not the whole scientific reasoning surrogate.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Build science/technical slices that move before e19/e20 flops and cover more active reasoning than raw arXiv/PubMed text alone. Candidate sources: ARC train/dev, SciQ/QASC train/dev, MedQA/MedMCQA/PubMedQA train/dev if license-compatible, arXiv/S2ORC/PubMed-derived generated QA, scientific Python notebooks, formal-methods snippets, unit conversion/numeric science templates, and technical equation/notation continuation.

Raw PPL over science prose is useful but too passive; include supervised target-only short-answer, MCQA, notation, and code/analysis continuation variants where feasible.

### Links

* Parent: #5819
* Formal methods coverage: #5060

## Results

Open. Decide which train/dev datasets belong in MCQA vs science, and which generated source-document tasks should become regular tracking slices.

# Research

This is a scope/design decision issue under epic #5005 / parent #5819, sibling to #5828 (MCQA train/dev) and #5618 (surface-form probes). The ask is to land a `science_train_core` PPL bundle of non-benchmark validation slices for scientific/technical reasoning that moves before e19/e20 flops, without polluting tracking with HLE/GPQA-Diamond/CritPt/SciCode exact items. ARC is explicitly downgraded to MCQA/science canary, not the whole surrogate.

The PPL gap framework is already in place; this is dataset selection + bundle wiring, not new infra.

**Relevant code**
- [`perplexity_gap_registry.py#L72-L110`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/perplexity_gap_registry.py#L72-L110) — bundle pattern (`base_raw`, `multilingual_raw`, `runnable_long_tail`, `bio_chem`); add `science_train_core` here.
- [`formal_methods_ppl.py#L94-L181`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/formal_methods_ppl.py#L94-L181) — template for non-HF archive sources with `IngestionPolicy`, `usage_policy=EVAL_ONLY`, contamination-risk notes.
- [`perplexity_gap.py#L113-L138`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/perplexity_gap.py#L113-L138) — `supervised_text_dataset(..., input_key, target_key)` is the right hook for target-only MCQA/short-answer variants.
- [`exp1600_uncheatable_evals.py#L44-L57`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/exp1600_uncheatable_evals.py#L44-L57) — `arxiv_physics` / `arxiv_computer_science` are already wired as raw PPL; do not duplicate, extend the science taxonomy.
- [`bio_chem_notation.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/bio_chem_notation.py) — sibling notation bundle; same shape applies to science notation slices.

# Proposed Approach (for human review, not a PR yet)

Multi-module dataset onboarding (≫100 LOC across `experiments/evals/`, `marin.datakit`, HF uploads). Out of scope for the small-fix path. Proposing the slice list and integration points; needs maintainer sign-off before implementation.

Recommended initial `science_train_core` bundle (all train/dev or non-benchmark):

1. MCQA delegated to #5828 — `science_train_core` references but does not duplicate ARC/SciQ/QASC/OpenBookQA train/dev rendered via `supervised_text_dataset` (target=answer letter and answer text variants).
2. Biomedical MCQA train/dev under license check: MedMCQA train, MedQA-USMLE train, PubMedQA `pqa_artificial` (synthetic, not the labeled test split). Skip if license-blocked.
3. Generated science short-answer / cloze: derive from S2ORC and PubMed Central OA abstracts (HF: `allenai/peS2o` or `pubmed`); template `input`=context+question, `target`=numeric or short span. Build under `experiments/science_generated_qa.py`, scored via `supervised_text_dataset`.
4. Scientific Python notebook continuation: filtered nbformat cells from `bigcode/the-stack-v2` Jupyter slice (analysis/exec blocks only); raw PPL via `raw_text_dataset`.
5. Numeric/unit-conversion + equation-notation continuation: templated synthetic family (SI units, dimensional analysis, LaTeX equation completion). Author a small generator in `experiments/evals/science_notation_probes.py`, publish HF dataset, then wire like #5618.
6. Formal-methods coverage already lands via #5060 (`formal_methods/smt_lib`, `tptp`, `coqgym`, `dimacs_cnf`); reference, don't duplicate.

Integration: add `science_train_core_bundle()` to [`perplexity_gap_registry.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/perplexity_gap_registry.py) and register it in `registered_perplexity_gap_bundles()`. Each new HF dataset must pin a revision and set `usage_policy=EVAL_ONLY` with contamination-risk notes per `formal_methods_ppl.py` precedent. Run a pilot gap report against Marin-8B / Llama-3.1-8B / Qwen3-8B and link findings into #5005, per #5060 definition-of-done.

Open questions for maintainers before implementation:

- License posture on MedQA-USMLE and MedMCQA — include or defer to a separate license-cleared issue?
- Single bundle or split bio vs general-science to avoid one family masking the other (per #5060 reporting rule)?
- Per-subject rollup convention: align with #5828's choice so MCQA/science share aggregation code.
- LaTeX-formula continuation here, or as a synthetic surface-form probe under #5618?

Holding off on a branch until the slice list and license posture are confirmed.

spillover_issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment covers professional-document PPL slices under #5819 as a GDPval-like surrogate without using GDPval-AA tasks or reference answers. The research pass found that existing Marin PPL slice registries can support the work and that Common Pile mirrors already cover several candidate families, including caselaw, regulations, government publications, patents, and PubMed. The recommended initial cut is legal cases, regulations/policy, patents, medical/clinical text, and financial filings, with net-new ingestion mainly for SEC EDGAR and DailyMed/FDA labels. The issue is currently a design handoff: implementation should wait for maintainer decisions on source families, license posture, held-out strategy, and whether to share scaffolding with sibling #5819 issues.

### Helpful links
- Parent: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5819
- Research and proposed approach: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5827#issuecomment-4483266974
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Part of #5819. Add professional-document competence validation coverage as a GDPval-like distributional surrogate, without using GDPval-AA tasks or reference answers.

Current structured/table coverage helps, but we need more workplace/legal/financial/medical document surfaces: disclosures, contracts, filings, policy text, memos, and tabular report sections.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Add non-benchmark PPL or target-only slices from public professional documents that move before e19/e20 flops. Candidate sources: SEC EDGAR filings (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, exhibits, financial tables), contracts from Pile of Law / public SEC exhibits, CourtListener or other public legal corpora, patents, FDA labels / DailyMed, clinical guidelines, PubMed Central medical review text, earnings-call transcripts, government audit reports, and procurement documents.

Some slices should be raw document text; others can be supervised transformations such as section heading -> section text, table context -> row/cell text, clause context -> next clause, or report prompt -> structured summary. Avoid using benchmark QA/tasks derived from these corpora as core tracking.

### Links

* Parent: #5819

## Results

Open. Pick 3-5 high-value source families and define stable heldout extraction with metadata.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Actionability check — scoped as design/research, not a bug fix; PR is inappropriate at this stage
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (open PRs/issues against #5819 cluster)
- [x] Research existing PPL slice infrastructure and overlap with Common Pile

# Research

Marin already has a slice-registry pattern (`LongTailPplSlice` → `RawTextEvaluationDataset`) and three reference implementations (long-tail families, runnable HF slices, structured-text manifests). Common Pile mirrors already cover ~half of the candidate source families in this issue (caselaw, regulations, USGPO, USPTO patents, PubMed, UK Hansard), so most of this work is registry wiring + held-out split definition, not new bulk downloads. Net-new ingestion is required only for SEC EDGAR, FDA DailyMed/labels, and earnings-call transcripts.

**Relevant code**
- [\`experiments/evals/long_tail_ppl.py#L29-L86\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/long_tail_ppl.py#L29-L86) — \`LongTailPplFamily\` + \`LongTailPplSlice\` registry pattern to copy
- [\`experiments/evals/long_tail_ppl_runnable.py#L21-L98\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/long_tail_ppl_runnable.py#L21-L98) — runnable HF-backed slices (\`RunnableLongTailPplSlice\`)
- [\`experiments/structured_evals.py#L74-L236\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/structured_evals.py#L74-L236) — \`IngestionSourceManifest\` + \`_eval_only_policy\` for eval-only contamination guard
- [\`experiments/common_pile/tokenize_common_pile.py\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/common_pile/tokenize_common_pile.py) — existing mirrors: \`caselaw_access_project_filtered\`, \`regulations_filtered\`, \`usgpo_filtered\`, \`uspto_filtered\`, \`pubmed_filtered\`, \`uk_hansard_filtered\`
- [\`experiments/paloma.py#L83-L89\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/paloma.py#L83-L89) — \`raw_text_dataset\` wiring for perplexity-gap reports

Sibling issues under #5819 (#5823–#5829) all need the same scaffolding; #5827 should not invent a parallel one.

# Proposed Approach

Five source families, each backed by an existing mirror where possible, ranked by cost-to-stand-up:

1. **legal_cases** — Common Pile \`caselaw_access_project_filtered\` (already mirrored). Held-out: hash-based 1% slice keyed by case ID with metadata \`{court, year, jurisdiction}\`. Eval-only flag to prevent recirculation into training mixes.
2. **regulations_policy** — Common Pile \`regulations_filtered\` + \`usgpo_filtered\`. Held-out: 1% by document ID with metadata \`{agency, doc_type, year}\`.
3. **patents** — Common Pile \`uspto_filtered\`. Held-out: pinned date window (e.g. last quarter of latest release) with metadata \`{ipc_class, grant_year}\`; date-based held-out is more robust to leakage than random.
4. **medical_clinical** — Common Pile \`pubmed_filtered\` for review text; net-new \`raw/dailymed\` ingestion (FDA SPL XML or HF mirror) for drug labels. Held-out: 1% by PMC/SPL ID with metadata \`{section_type, year}\`.
5. **financial_filings** — Net-new \`raw/sec_edgar\` ingestion. Recommend the \`eloukas/edgar-corpus\` HF mirror (10-K/Q sections, parquet, dated) over scraping EDGAR directly to avoid open-internet cost. Held-out: pinned filing window with metadata \`{form_type, section_id, cik, fy}\`.

Out of initial scope: contracts (license-mixed), CourtListener (overlaps caselaw), earnings-call transcripts (no clean public source), procurement (small per-source corpora). These can be follow-ups once the registry exists.

Scaffolding to add (estimated ~300-500 LOC across files):
- \`experiments/evals/professional_document_ppl.py\` — \`ProfessionalDocumentFamily\` StrEnum + \`ProfessionalDocumentSlice\` dataclass mirroring \`LongTailPplSlice\`. Each slice declares \`heldout_split_strategy\` (id_hash, date_window, ipc_class) and metadata fields.
- Two new \`marin.datakit.download\` modules: \`sec_edgar.py\` (\`eloukas/edgar-corpus\`) and \`dailymed.py\` (FDA SPL or HF mirror). Both follow the \`download_hf_step\` pattern used by structured-text.
- A staging transform per family that emits \`staged.jsonl.gz\` with a \`metadata\` field carrying the held-out keys. Reuse \`stage_table_record_source\` where shape fits; otherwise a thin \`stage_professional_document_source\`.
- Wire \`professional_document_raw_validation_sets()\` analog to \`structured_evals_raw_validation_sets()\` so the perplexity-gap pipeline picks them up automatically.
- Tag every slice with \`epic:5819\`, \`issue:5827\`, \`family:<name>\` to track movement against early flops vs. e19/e20.

Questions for a maintainer before implementation:
1. Is the 5-family cut above correct, or do you want to swap (e.g. drop financial_filings if EDGAR download is a non-starter, swap in earnings calls)?
2. License-policy preference for net-new sources: eval-only (like structured-text) or open for mixing into midtraining? This sets the \`UsagePolicy\` and contamination caveats.
3. Held-out strategy: date-window vs. id-hash — preference for one across all families to keep dashboards comparable?
4. Should this share a registry with the other #5819 children (#5823–#5829), or stay independent? A shared \`experiments/evals/aa_surrogate_ppl/\` package would reduce duplication across siblings.

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment tracks instruction-following and formatting PPL coverage under #5819 without using IFBench/IFEval prompts as regular tracking data. The research pass found that Marin already has the needed scoring and bundle infrastructure, including supervised target-only loss, and the main missing piece is a generated registry of constraint-family slices. The current recommendation is a deterministic, in-repo template-generated bundle covering JSON emission, tabular output, exact-count bullets, constrained rewrites, field preservation, negative constraints, sort/filter tasks, and refusal formats. Implementation is waiting on maintainer choices about source strategy, family list, default bundle registration, and target size.

### Helpful links
- Parent: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5819
- Research and proposed approach: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5824#issuecomment-4483266849
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Part of #5819. Add instruction-following and formatting validation coverage without using exact IFBench prompts or other held-out benchmark items.

Current format probes cover delimiter/numeric/structured surfaces, but the core suite needs natural-language instructions with constraints: rewrite, count, filter, sort, transform, emit JSON/table, follow style constraints, preserve fields, and obey negative constraints.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Create generated or mined train/validation slices by constraint family, scored with supervised target-only loss where possible. The eval should move smoothly before e19/e20 flops and catch regressions in instruction adherence and output formatting without requiring full judge-based generation.

Potential slices: prompt -> JSON object, prompt -> TSV/CSV row, prompt -> bullet list with exact count, prompt -> transformed string/table, prompt -> constrained rewrite, and prompt -> refusal/abstain format where appropriate.

### Links

* Parent: #5819
* Chat/agent PPL context: #4963

## Results

Open. Pick constraint families, generation templates, and a small regular tracking subset.

comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Actionability check — design-shaped experiment, not a bug fix; open Results, no DoD. Open PR is wrong response.
- [x] Duplicate preflight (no open PR; siblings #5819, #4963)
- [x] Research existing instruction-following PPL surface
- [x] Post research + proposed approach for human review
- [ ] Await human design call before any implementation

# Research

The repo already has the bundle/scoring scaffolding (`PerplexityGapBundle`, `model_perplexity_scores`, `RawTextEvaluationDataset`, `supervised_text_dataset` with `input_key`/`target_key` for target-only loss). What's missing is a registry of generated, constraint-family slices that exercise instruction adherence without touching IFBench/IFEval prompts. The only instruction-following raw asset today is `wis-k/instruction-following-eval` — that is the held-out IFEval set we must not use as regular PPL tracking data per #5819's no-benchmark-maxxing rule.

**Relevant code**
- [`perplexity_gap_registry.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/perplexity_gap_registry.py) — bundle/model registry pattern to extend
- [`gh_archive_structured_output.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/gh_archive_structured_output.py) — closest precedent (structured-output slices wired as raw validation sets)
- [`long_tail_ppl_runnable.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/long_tail_ppl_runnable.py) — HF-backed slice pattern, no bulk mirror
- [`perplexity_gap.py#L113-L138`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/perplexity_gap.py#L113-L138) — \`supervised_text_dataset\` already supports target-only loss via input/target keys
- [`eval_datasets.py#L533-L545`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/eval_datasets.py#L533-L545) — existing IFEval download (must remain held-out, not PPL-tracked)

# Proposed Approach (for human sign-off)

Build \`experiments/evals/instruction_format_ppl.py\` modeled after \`gh_archive_structured_output.py\`/\`long_tail_ppl_runnable.py\`. Surface a \`instruction_format_bundle()\` consumable by \`registered_perplexity_gap_bundles()\`. Slices use \`supervised_text_dataset(input_key=\"prompt\", target_key=\"completion\")\` so loss is on the formatted target only, exactly matching the issue's \"supervised target-only loss where possible\" ask.

Constraint families (StrEnum, mirrors \`LongTailPplFamily\`):
1. \`json_emit\` — prompt → JSON object obeying a schema
2. \`tabular_emit\` — prompt → TSV/CSV row(s) with required columns/types
3. \`bullet_count\` — prompt → bullet list with exact-N items
4. \`constrained_rewrite\` — rewrite preserving content under style/length constraints
5. \`field_preservation\` — transform while keeping named fields verbatim
6. \`negative_constraint\` — \"do not include X / avoid Y\" satisfied in target
7. \`sort_filter\` — sort/filter a provided list by stated rule
8. \`refusal_format\` — produce a refusal in a constrained shape

Source strategy — pick one, not all (this is the decision the issue defers):

Option A (preferred, cheapest, fully non-benchmark): **template-generated**. Each family ships a small deterministic generator (~200-500 prompts) producing (prompt, target) pairs from typed templates. Lives entirely in-repo, no HF mirror, no IFBench overlap risk, seed-pinned. Cost: ~1 day of template authoring per family.

Option B: **mined from existing SFT mixes** already in the tree (e.g., Tulu personas-instruction-following from `exp1880_sft_baseline.py#L64`) filtered by constraint-family classifier. Lower authoring cost but introduces a classifier dependency and contamination questions.

Option C: hybrid — Option A for the 8 families above as a non-overlapping regular tracking set, plus an opt-in diagnostic-only Option B bundle.

Recommend **Option A** as the regular tracking bundle (matches #5819's \"non-benchmark surrogate, regular tracking\" framing) and defer Option B to a follow-up. Initial regular subset: ≤50 (prompt, target) pairs × 8 families = ≤400 items, well under the 256-doc default cap per slice. Wire into `registered_perplexity_gap_bundles()` so the existing 8B/32B vs Llama/Qwen pair sweep picks it up automatically.

Open questions for the issue author before implementation:
1. Confirm Option A (template-generated) over B/C.
2. Confirm the 8 families above — drop/add any?
3. Should this go into the default \`registered_perplexity_gap_bundles()\` (auto-runs against all registered models) or stay opt-in like \`gh_archive_structured_output\` until the slices stabilize?
4. Target size — is ≤50/family adequate, or do you want 200+/family for stable diffs?

Will implement once 1-4 are resolved.

spillover_issues.body:
The AdamH copies used by current and historical Grug divide by `norm(new_p)` without a floor. A zero-norm matrix produces a NaN update even at learning rate zero. This poisoned a 67B SFT checkpoint on its first warmup update; the next forward pass reported NaN loss.

Reproduce:
1. Create a zero `2 x 2` parameter and an all-ones gradient.
2. Build `experiments.grug.moe.adamh.scale_by_adamh(learning_rate=0.0)` and apply one update.
3. Observe that every returned update is NaN. The vendored `experiments.june_tpu_67b_a2b.moe.adamh` copy behaves identically, including for stacked matrices.

Expected: zero-norm parameters remain finite under AdamH, including during a zero-learning-rate warmup step.

comments.author: mridulagarwal03
comments.body: 🤖 https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9806 floors the updated matrix norm in `scale_by_adamh` at 1e-10 for the Grug MoE and hero FSDP copies. A zero matrix no longer produces a NaN update on a zero learning-rate or zero-gradient step.
